title: Sr. Project Manager - Gas Power Generation
description:
A DAY IN THE LIFE

Blattner is seeking a Sr.Project Manager to join our growing Gas Power Generation team. This person provides senior leadership and manages the operational and financial aspects of complex, multi-disciplinary programs and projects, including portfolio-level coordination. They serve as a primary liaison with client stakeholders across projects; navigate early project development (NOI to warranty), contract negotiations, engineering early work, sequencing, and supply chain strategies. They enforce Standard Work Instructions and Quality Programs, drive process utilization, safety, and risk management, and ensure the company’s values are upheld.

STEP INTO THE ROLE

Portfolio, Program & Project Leadership

  • Leads portfolio- and program-level planning and serves as sponsor to multiple Project Manager teams, ensuring strategic alignment across projects.
  • Manages projects from NOI through Warranty and sponsors Project Manager teams as needed.
  • Successfully manages multiple complex projects while mentoring and overseeing other Project Managers.

Stakeholder, Client & Communication Management

  • Develops stakeholder engagement strategies and builds strong relationships across projects and programs.
  • Serves as the primary liaison with client teams/leadership, ensuring portfolio-level alignment and strategic decision-making across projects.
  • Independently negotiates complex contracts and exhibits and provides guidance to Project Managers on contract strategy and resolution of high-risk negotiation points.
  • Understands the company mission and supports future opportunities through client relationships.

Requirements, Planning & Scheduling

  • Oversees identification, analysis, documentation, and lifecycle management of requirements across multiple projects, ensuring final deliverables meet strategic and technical expectations.
  • Develops complex, long-term, cross-team schedules; reviews schedules created by Project Managers.

Risk, Quality & Change Control

  • Sets program- and portfolio-level risk strategies, manages escalated risks, and establishes recovery plans across multiple projects.
  • Leads formal review and change-control processes to assess progress and approve adjustments.
  • Leads assurance reviews and third-party audits; supports PMs in resolving issues.
  • Champions best practices, process utilization, quality, safety, and risk management across the organization.

Financial Management

  • Oversees negotiation, prioritization, and deployment of budgets across programs and projects; directs resource allocation decisions and provides financial oversight to Project Manager teams.
  • Oversees project and program budgets, including change management processes.
  • Manages and trains others on monthly financial forecasting and time-phasing.
  • Reviews and validates financial performance across projects, providing guidance to Project Managers and ensuring portfolio-level billing and change controls are accurate.

People Leadership, Coaching & Talent Development

  • Sets direction for large or multiple teams; communicates vision, builds capability, and provides training, coaching, and mentoring.
  • Onboards and trains PM1s in tools, processes, workflows, and financial forecasting.
  • Contributes to management of PM1s, including performance reviews, development coaching, and structured growth plans.
  • Provides 1:1 coaching and fosters a high-performance culture.

Innovation & Continuous Improvement

  • Drives innovation and contributes to internal initiatives, committees, and cross-functional improvements.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED

  • Bachelor’s degree in construction or engineering; or equivalent combinations of technical training and/or related experience.
  • 7 or more years of total project/construction experience; 5 or more years leadership experience; preferred renewable construction experience.
  • Exceptional leadership and communication (oral, presentation, written).
  • Deep knowledge of cost accounting, construction regulations, and risk management.
  • Advanced planning and conceptual skills; able to develop portfolio-level sequencing and schedules.
  • Knowledge of salary structures, market pricing, compensation modeling, and pay practices.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office products.
  • Ability to prioritize, operate independently, and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential information.

  • 401(k) with company match

location: Spring, Texas, United States of America
description:
OEM Systems Software Engineer IThis role has been designed as 'Hybrid' with a requirement that you will work on average 2 days per week from an HPE office.

Who We Are:

Hewlett Packard Enterprise is the global edge-to-cloud company advancing the way people live and work. We help companies connect, protect, analyze, and act on their data and applications wherever they live, from edge to cloud, so they can turn insights into outcomes at the speed required to thrive in today’s complex world. Our culture thrives on finding new and better ways to accelerate what’s next. We know varied backgrounds are valued and succeed here. We have the flexibility to manage our work and personal needs. We make bold moves, together, and are a force for good. If you are looking to stretch and grow your career our culture will embrace you. Open up opportunities with HPE.

Job Description:

OEM Systems Software Engineer I is a strategic position bridging customers and the HPE engineering team. You will work with OEM and Service Provider (SP) customers to help them implement their solutions on the HPE ProLiant platform. The role is also responsible for providing strategic design advice for future HPE ProLiant products based on their customer-facing experience. You will work with internal teams as well as external partners and vendors to achieve the organization's business goals. We are looking for an energetic, goal-oriented, and strategic problem solver to join our team.
Responsibilities
  • Work with OEM and SP customers to resolve issues on HPE ProLiant platforms.
  • Improve HPE ProLiant software deliverables such as SPP (Service Pack for ProLiant), iLOrest, and COM.
  • Identify and debug software bugs and report findings to the Development team.
  • Develop test plans, test cases, test scenarios, traceability matrices, and test reports.
  • Attend automation core team meetings to analyze and design the automation framework.
  • Test future-generation (Beta) ProLiant Servers.
  • Conduct feasibility studies and requirements analysis for new feature implementation; raise requests with the product management team for implementation in future ProLiant generations.
  • Implement test processes for HPE DX servers in collaboration with Nutanix and external partners.
  • Collaborate with internal and external development teams to design and implement customer-requested features and resolve issues.
  • Work with external NIC and RAID controller vendors to resolve issues.
  • Perform OS updates for Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL) and SUSE Linux Enterprise in UEFI and Secure Boot modes to verify OS compatibility on HPE ProLiant Servers.
  • Own Quick Setup, test execution, and reporting of test results.
Education and Experience Required
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Electronics, Information Systems, or a related field.
  • Typically, 2-4 years of experience.
Knowledge and Skills
  • Experience working with industry-standard servers; well-versed in server architecture and design for Intel and AMD platforms.
  • Knowledge of NICs, NVIDIA GPUs, SSDs, HDDs, and RAID controllers.
  • Systems programming knowledge, including x64 architecture, storage, and networking.
  • Python scripting knowledge for writing test cases.
  • Linux experience, including RHEL, SUSE, and Ubuntu.
  • Working knowledge of XML and JSON.
  • REST API implementation expertise to communicate with iLO (BMC).
  • Knowledge of UEFI BIOS and Ethernet networking.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to clearly communicate design proposals and negotiate options with customers.
  • Knowledge of software systems testing methodology, including execution of test plans, debugging, and testing of scripts and tools.

Facilities 30 Second Cut

Under general direction of the Maintenance Lead, this position is responsible for a variety of exciting work which involves maintaining and repairing infrastructure of the Hiland Mountain Correctional Center. These include but are not limited to; perimeter security systems, Closed Circuit Television (CCTV) camera systems, cable television systems, electronic doors and locks, fire protection systems, telephone and telephone voice mail systems, Intercom systems, Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems, and computer networking wiring systems.


Our Missions, Values, and Culture:

The institution includes 11 buildings, containing approximately 120,000 square feet of space, sitting on approximately 62.7 acres of land adjacent to Eagle River, Alaska. title: Director, AI-Ready Digital Engagement Innovation
description:
Job Description

The Director, AI-Ready Digital Engagement Innovation leads AI Discoverability by establishing a future-forward vision for how all US Market Human Health branded content is structured, governed, and activated. This role ensures company assets are optimized not only for human engagement on brand properties, but for seamless discovery, interpretation, and citation by external AI-driven search engines, large language models (LLMs), and emerging conversational interfaces.

This leader continuously monitors shifts in external discovery behavior (from traditional SEO to AEO, GEO, and LLMO) and translates emerging technology trends into actionable content architecture, metadata standards, and pilot roadmaps. By setting the strategic rules for information architecture and machine readability, this role ensures our branded content remains trusted, authoritative, and prominently surfaced across the rapidly evolving AI ecosystem.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

AI Search and Discoverability: Define and champion the future-state discoverability vision across all US Market digital touchpoints. Lead the strategic transition from traditional destination-based search engine optimization (SEO) to AI-mediated discovery models, including Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and Large Language Model Optimization (LLMO).

Content Architecture, Taxonomy, and Metadata Standards: Establish enterprise-wide standards for information architecture, semantic metadata, taxonomy, and structured content design. Ensure branded & unbranded assets, indications, and scientific value propositions are structured to support both intuitive human navigation and accurate machine interpretation by third-party AI platforms.

Trend Intelligence and Innovation Roadmap: Continuously monitor, evaluate, and operationalize external signals across generative AI, conversational search, digital health platforms, and intelligent agents. Prioritize, design, and guide rapid innovation pilots and proof-of-concept initiatives to keep the digital footprint ahead of technological disruption. Create and maintain roadmap for the US Market liaising with stakeholders in DHH.

Governance of Machine-Readable Assets: Define structural governance frameworks that safeguard brand integrity, regulatory compliance, and factual accuracy in AI-mediated environments. Ensure automated systems and generative search engines surface authorized, compliant, and up-to-date branded messaging.

Performance Measurement and Ecosystem Health: Establish and own next-generation performance metrics focused on AI presence. Define and track key indicators such as LLM citation frequency, answer engine visibility share, schema adoption rates, and overall content discoverability across third-party AI ecosystems.

Strategic Operational Partnership: Collaborate closely with the Director of Digital Engagement Operations to translate high-level content architecture and AI discoverability standards into daily operational workflows, enabling seamless adoption across all commercial business units.

POINTS OF COLLABORATION

  • Executive Director, Customer Engagement Orchestration: Strategic alignment on innovation roadmap, technology priorities, and investment.

  • Director, Digital Engagement Operations: Operational handoff of standards, taxonomies, and guidelines for business unit execution.

  • Digital Human Health (DHH): Technical collaboration on search technology, enterprise data integration, and discoverability tracking.

  • Brand Marketing and Commercial Operations: Alignment on brand-specific messaging priorities and commercial goals.

  • Media Strategy: Coordination between owned-content discoverability and paid/earned media campaigns.

  • Legal, Regulatory, and Compliance: Establishing guardrails for brand safety, accuracy, and compliance within AI environments.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE

  • Education: Advanced degree in marketing/business analytics, digital media and analytics, or related field strongly preferred.

  • Professional Experience: Minimum of 10+ years of progressive experience in digital strategy, search strategy (SEO/AEO), content strategy, or digital capability innovation.

  • AI Search Expertise: Proven understanding of AI-driven search paradigms, including Answer Engine Optimization (AEO), Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), and LLM citation mechanics.

  • Content Strategy Skills: Demonstrated experience establishing information architecture, taxonomy structures, and metadata frameworks across complex digital ecosystems.

  • Strategic Vision: Demonstrated track record of converting emerging digital trends into actionable strategic roadmaps and successful pilot programs.

  • Regulated Environment: Experience operating within highly regulated industries (e.g., pharmaceuticals, healthcare, or financial services) is strongly preferred.

  • Influential Leadership: Exceptional communication and matrix leadership skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional technical, creative, and commercial partners. Strong executive presence and ability to interact with leaders of all levels of the enterprise.

Required Skills:

Accountability, Accountability, Adaptability, Brand Positioning, Content Analysis, Content Delivery, Content Development, Content Marketing, Content Strategy, Content Writing, Creativity, Digital Consumer Engagement, Digital Marketing, Digital Strategy, Digital Transformation, Engagement Strategies, Executive Presence, Information Architectures, Market Access, Marketing Automation, Marketing Budget Management, Market Research, Messaging Strategies, Omnichannel Marketing, People Leadership {+ 9 more}

title: Uniform Attendant
location: FL - Orlando - Universal Stella Nova Resort
description:
At Loews Hotels at Universal Orlando, our team members get to make a difference and have fun every day. Our world-class team brings to life the incredible, award-winning hotels located at Universal Orlando Resort.


Named one of Central Florida’s Top Workplaces and one of America’s Best-in-State Employers by Forbes, we are committed to our “power of we” culture.


Are you looking for a place where you can bring your authentic self to work every day and be able to connect, engage and delight?


  • We offer excellent benefits and perks including one free meal per shift and free theme park access.
  • We have a dynamic culture that makes every day interesting, challenging, fulfilling and fun.
  • We embrace diversity at our core and offer the opportunity for all team members to reach their potential.
  • We invest in training and development opportunities for all team members.
  • We promote social responsibility by being a good neighbor in the community.
  • We care for you, just as we care for others.

Who We Are: Founded in 1960, Loews Hotels & Co operates iconic hotels and resorts across the U.S. Together, our diverse and welcoming teams craft exceptional experiences in iconic destinations.


Growth and belonging start here; you’ll be valued for who you are and the goals you have. Whether your next career chapter involves making memories for guests or supporting our properties in our Corporate Office, every role—from Guest Services to Finance, Culinary to IT—offers opportunities to grow and make a meaningful impact.


Creating a Team Member experience where you belong no matter what race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status that makes you, you is a daily focus for us.


About Universal Stella Nova Resort

Join the team and step into another galaxy, where you’ll help guests land in a universe of thrills and adventure.


What We’re Looking For:
A reliable, detail-oriented Uniform Attendant who ensures every team member looks polished and professional. You’ll manage the end-to-end uniform lifecycle—from issuing, labeling, and tracking to receiving, laundering coordination, light repairs, and returns—so our operations teams can focus on delivering exceptional guest experiences. In this role, you’ll work closely with Housekeeping/Laundry, HR, and department leaders to maintain inventory accuracy, support onboarding, and uphold cleanliness and presentation standards for all uniforms.

Who You Are:

  • Quality Focused: You care about appearance, cleanliness, and consistent presentation.

  • Focused Organized and Systematic: You keep inventories accurate and processes on track.

  • Service Minded: You’re approachable and helpful when team members need assistance.

  • Dependable Teammate: You communicate clearly and follow through on commitments.

  • Veterans and military spouses are encouraged to apply.

What You’ll Do:

  • Issue, receive, and track team member uniforms using established logs or systems; ensure proper labeling, sizing, and assignment by department and role.

  • Inspect incoming/outgoing uniforms for cleanliness, damage, and wear; route items for laundering, pressing, spot treatment, or light repairs as appropriate.

  • Perform basic mending (buttons, hems, minor seams) and coordinate with Laundry or outside vendors for more extensive alterations/repairs.

  • Maintain organized stockrooms/lockers; conduct regular inventory counts and reconcile variances; support month end reporting as needed.

  • Prepare uniform kits for new hires; collect, document, and process returns for separations and role changes.

  • Monitor par levels; place or assist with orders for replacements, specialty items, name tags, and accessories in alignment with brand standards.

  • Ensure compliance with cleanliness, safety, and PPE protocols within the uniform room and laundry support areas.

  • Provide friendly, efficient service to team members for exchanges, sizing, and special requests; escalate guest facing uniform issues to leadership when necessary.

  • Coordinate with HR and department managers to align on policy updates, grooming standards, and uniform program changes.

  • Keep accurate records (issuance, repairs, losses, charges) and protect confidentiality of team member information.

Other Responsibilities:

  • Regularly lift up to 45 pounds, reach, bend, crouch, kneel, push, pull, and walk.

  • Maintain regular and reliable attendance in alignment with company standards and operational needs.

  • Embrace flexibility by performing other duties as assigned to support team and organizational goals.

Your Qualifications Include:

  • Previous experience in hospitality or relevant industry preferred.

  • Basic computer skills required.

  • Familiarity with Microsoft Suite and InvoTech preferred.

  • Must complete OSHA-mandated safety training within the first 30 days of employment.

  • Position requires the ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and written, with team members, leaders, and guests.

  • Position requires flexibility to work a varied schedule, including days, nights, weekends, and holidays, as scheduled.

  • Position requires the ability to lift, push, and pull 50+ pounds repetitively throughout shift.

title: Transportation Coordinator
description:
SUMMARY
The Managed Transportation Coordinator is responsible for executing and monitoring daily shipments to ensure accuracy, efficiency, and complete end-to-end visibility. This role supports customers, carriers, warehouses, and internal teams through proactive communication, issue resolution, and maintaining high-quality data within the Transportation Management System (TMS).

Monday to Friday 9:30am-6:00pm
RESPONSIBILITIES
Shipment Execution & Tracking

Execute and monitor daily shipments, including tendering, dispatching, tracking, and updating statuses in the TMS.
Track and trace shipments to ensure on-time pickup and delivery; identify delays or service risks.
Confirm appointments and coordinate dock requirements and order readiness with warehouses.
Validate shipment details and process documentation (BOLs, packing lists, customs documents, PODs).

Customer & Carrier Communication

Provide customers with accurate ETAs, delay notifications, and recovery updates.
Communicate with carriers via phone, email, and portals to obtain timely shipment information.
Partner with warehouse operations and customer service to prioritize and coordinate shipments, including special handling or time-sensitive moves.

Data Integrity, Billing & Reporting

Maintain accurate TMS data including reference numbers, weights, dimensions, accessorials, and shipment notes.
Prepare exception logs, recovery summaries, KPI metrics, and other required reports.
Support billing audits to ensure invoicing accuracy and adherence to SLAs.

Issue Resolution & Continuous Improvement

Resolve shipment issues quickly and escalate recurring concerns to the MT Representative/Manager.
Recommend mode changes or alternative solutions when shipments are at risk.
Identify opportunities for process improvements and cost-saving initiatives.

EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE

2–3 years of experience in transportation or warehouse operations.
College diploma or degree in Business, Logistics, or related field (asset).
Experience with TMS platforms; WMS experience an asset.
Experience supporting e-commerce or B2C, B2B, Final Mile transportation environments is beneficial.

SKILLS

Strong organizational skills and attention to detail with high data accuracy.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to prioritize, multitask, and make sound decisions in a fast-paced environment.
Analytical problem-solving mindset with the ability to react quickly to service issues.
Customer-first mentality and ability to maintain composure under pressure.
Commitment to continuous learning and improvement.
Collaborative, team-oriented approach.

title: Physical Security Planner
description:
Physical Security Planner

The Opportunity:
As a Physical Security Planner on the DPRI team, you are on the front lines of safeguarding the nation’s most critical overseas military infrastructure investments. This is a unique opportunity to apply your expertise in force protection and electronic security systems to large-scale, international construction projects that are shaping the future of U.S. strategic posture. You will serve as a key security advisor, ensuring that multi-million-dollar facilities are resilient, secure, and compliant from concept to completion. Your work will directly contribute to the operational integrity of strategic initiatives, protect warfighting assets, and provide you with a critical role in a dynamic, mission-focused environment.

Join us. The world can't wait.


You Have:

  • 5+ years of experience in physical security, antiterrorism, force protection, or electronic security system (ESS) project management for military or government facilities

  • Experience preparing detailed implementation plans, including cost and resource estimates, for large-scale security infrastructure projects

  • Experience with the planning and integration of electronic security systems, including CCTV, automated access control, and intrusion detection systems (IDS)

  • Experience performing structured risk analyses for construction or renovation projects to ensure security requirements are properly incorporated into facility designs

  • Ability to conduct on-site surveys and technical inspections to validate facility designs and construction efforts against security program requirements

description:

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman Aeronautics Systems has an opening for to join our team of qualified, diverse individuals. This position will be located partially on site at one of the following Aeronautics Systems sites: Palmdale CA, El Segundo CA, Clearfield UT, or Melbourne, FL.

In this role, you will be a part of the Facilities Strategic Planning & Integration team whose charter is to maximize operational excellence and efficiency of the distributed Facilities organization through centralized, strategic homeroom support of systems, tools, processes, portfolio planning, and coordination of Sector/Corporate initiatives impacting the broader NGAS Facilities organization.

A core focus of this position is driving system and process adoption by developing robust training programs, leading stakeholder change management initiatives, and managing process reviews and User Acceptance Testing (UAT) to ensure smooth transitions during process and tool rollouts.

This Principal Facilities Process Engineer Level 3 or Senior Principal Facilities Process Engineer Level 4 will be responsible for standardizing, maintaining, and improving facilities processes, tools, and training across multiple AS locations. This role manages core facilities process documentation, supports and optimizes facilities software tools, and leads training and integration efforts to ensure consistent, efficient operations nationwide. The position partners closely with site facilities teams, functions (e.g. ESHM, security, operations, IT), and business stakeholders to drive operational excellence and a consistent employee experience.

Duties & Responsibilities:

  • Review and optimize standardized facilities processes and procedures for multiple sites.
  • Coordinate periodic reviews and updates to documentation to align with changing requirements and business needs.
  • Monitor key metrics and feedback from sites to identify gaps & opportunities.
  • Lead structured Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigations into critical facility system failures to isolate technical or process flaws.
  • Prioritize needs for improvement based on calculated business value.
  • Collaborate with key resources and stakeholders on solution development.
  • Coordinate requirements gathering, configuration changes, testing, and rollout of tool enhancements and new features.
  • Design and execute structured change management plans to transition diverse stakeholder groups (from executive leadership to frontline technicians) through software updates and process modifications.
  • Implement corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) discovered during RCAs, adjusting operational workflows or system integrations to prevent repeat failures.
  • Author clear, accessible training documentation, standard operating procedures (SOPs), quick-reference guides, and video tutorials tailored to different user roles and technical skill levels.
  • Design and deliver training for facilities staff and stakeholders on processes, tools, and best practices. Support change management for process and tool changes, including communication plans and adoption tracking.
  • Develop and maintain user guides, quick-reference material, and standard configurations to support consistent tool usage.
  • Act as a primary contact for user questions, support, and feedback related to facilities processes and tools.
  • Work with site leaders to understand local requirements and align them with standard practices.
  • Develop and standardize workflows for long-range facility planning, space utilization, and asset lifecycle management.

This requisition may be filled as either a Principal Facilities Process Engineer Level 3 or a Senior Principal Facilities Process Engineer Level 4.

Basic Qualifications for a Level 3 Facilities Process Engineer:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Facilities Management, Architecture or Construction Management, Operations Research, Engineering, (Industrial, Systems, Mechanical), Computer Science, Management Information Systems (MIS), or a relevant technical field with 5 Years of relevant experience; OR a Master's Degree in the stated fields with 3 years of relevant experience; OR a PhD in the stated fields with 1 year of relevant experience.
  • Strong organizational skills in managing time, projects, and resources.
  • Strong skills in process mapping, workflow design, and requirements gathering.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities across geographically dispersed locations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office/365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project, Teams, SharePoint or equivalent collaboration platforms).
  • Ability to work in cross functional teams and interact with both managers and customers.
  • Ability to organize stakeholders while providing project visibility and closure plans.

Basic Qualifications for a Level 4 Facilities Process Engineer:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Facilities Management, Architecture or Construction Management, Operations Research, Engineering, (Industrial, Systems, Mechanical), Computer Science, Management Information Systems (MIS), or a relevant technical field with 8 Years of relevant experience; OR a Master's Degree in the stated fields with 6 years of relevant experience; OR a PhD in the stated fields with 4 year of relevant experience.
  • Strong organizational skills in managing time, projects, and resources.
  • Strong skills in process mapping, workflow design, and requirements gathering.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities across geographically dispersed locations.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office/365 (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project, Teams, SharePoint or equivalent collaboration platforms).
  • Ability to work in cross functional teams and interact with both managers and customers.
  • Ability to organize stakeholders while providing project visibility and closure plans.


Preferred Qualifications:

  • Self-starter with the ability to work with minimal supervision, ability to multitask and exercise good judgment, with good follow-up skills
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills; comfortable training various audiences.
  • Experience managing/supporting enterprise-level facilities systems integration, technical plant engineering, or operational process design.
  • Proficiency with CMMS (e.g., Maximo, Corrigo), Project Management Systems (e.g., Procore), IWMS/CAFM space planning and/or CAD tools (e.g., Archibus, AutoCAD, REVIT, BIM), and/or business intelligence platforms (e.g., Power BI, Tableau).
  • Background or knowledge on how to lead cross-functional teams to perform root cause analysis on critical facility infrastructure failures.
  • Ability to analyze facility performance data to generate actionable insights and cost-saving initiatives.
  • Exceptional instructional capability, strong public speaking skills, empathy for users navigating technical changes, and a rigorous approach to software quality assurance testing.
  • Experience with facility design and drafting, including space layouts and utilization plans
  • Experience with design and construction of classified facilities
  • Experience working within an ITAR-regulated environment, defense manufacturing plant, or aerospace facility.
  • Certified Lean Six Sigma Green or Black Belt.
  • Familiarity with data integrations, APIs, SQL, or dashboarding tools (e.g., Power BI, Tableau) used to visualize CMMS performance.
  • Experience working in a large, complex, or highly regulated organization.
  • Aerospace and/or Defense Industry Experience
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government Secret Security Clearance.

We offer flexible work arrangements, phenomenal learning opportunities, exposure to a wide variety of projects and customers, and a very friendly inclusive environment! We are looking for self-motivated, proactive, and goal-oriented people to help us grow our services and become even better at what we do.

At Northrop Grumman, we are on the cutting edge of innovation-- building the next generation of sophisticated aircraft to protect our country. • Lead the design, implementation, testing, enhancement, integration, and ongoing support of technology-enabled tax reporting and compliance solutions.
• Establish governance standards for tax systems, data, calculations, workflows, access, change management, documentation, and user support.
• Evaluate and deploy reporting, analytics, workflow automation, and generative AI solutions with appropriate controls and review.
INCOME TAX REPORTING PROCESS SUPPORT
• Serve as a hands-on technology and process leader for the systems, workflows, calculation models, data validation, reconciliations, controls, and reporting outputs that support the quarterly and annual global income tax provision process under ASC 740, in partnership with the tax reporting function.
• Partner with Tax leadership and Corporate Accounting to support the underlying systems, data, controls, workflows, and calculation processes used in current and deferred tax calculations, effective tax rate analyses, tax reserves, valuation allowances, uncertain tax positions, and provision-to-return activities, while tax accounting judgments and conclusions remain with the tax reporting function.
• Support the systems, data, documentation, and reporting processes used by the tax reporting function in preparing income tax disclosures included in Forms 10-Q and 10-K and coordinating responses to external auditor requests.
• Support forecasting processes for income tax expense, effective tax rate, and cash taxes through scalable models, standardized data, and reporting tools, in coordination with Tax leadership and Finance.
• Translate significant tax accounting positions and judgments determined by Tax leadership into sustainable system, data, workflow, control, and reporting solutions.
COMPLIANCE, CO-SOURCING AND TAX MODELS
• Partner with domestic and international tax teams and external providers to improve the systems, data, calculations, and workflows supporting income tax compliance.
• Lead co-sourcing initiatives with tax providers to evaluate process ownership, knowledge transfer, automation, strategic insourcing, and sustainable delivery models.
• Support the design, governance, and continuous improvement of complex domestic and international tax calculation models and technology-enabled reporting and compliance processes.
• Review provider work product from a process, data, system, and control perspective and coordinate resolution of identified issues.
• Establish and maintain processes to help ensure return-to-provision, provision-to-return, and related data flows are timely, complete, traceable, and appropriately reflected in tax systems and accounts.
PROCESS EXCELLENCE, CONTROLS AND RISK REDUCTION
• Lead initiatives to simplify legacy tax processes, eliminate redundant activities and spreadsheet dependencies, reduce manual intervention and human error, and improve auditability.
• Design standardized, scalable workflows that strengthen data quality, accountability, transparency, and execution across tax reporting and compliance.
• Partner with Internal Audit, Corporate Accounting, and Information Technology to strengthen tax process controls, SOX documentation, system controls, and evidence retention.
• Identify and escalate material process, data, system, control, and execution risks to Tax leadership on a timely basis.
• Develop dashboards and performance metrics to provide visibility into process status, data quality, controls, risks, and improvement opportunities.
LEADERSHIP AND CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COLLABORATION
• Serve as a trusted advisor to Tax leadership on tax technology, data, reporting processes, co-sourcing, controls, and transformation priorities.
• Lead, coach, and develop tax professionals and project resources supporting tax technology, reporting, and compliance initiatives.
• Build strong partnerships with Corporate Accounting, Treasury, FP&A, Legal, Internal Audit, Information Technology, regional tax teams, external auditors, and tax providers.
• Manage external technology and tax providers for assigned initiatives, including scope, deliverables, quality, issue resolution, budget, value, and efficiency.

The accomplished individual will possess...
• Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, Information Systems, or a related field.
• CPA required.
• 10+ years of progressive corporate tax experience, including experience in a Big Four or other major public accounting firm and/or a multinational corporate tax department.
• Strong knowledge of ASC 740, public company tax reporting, and corporate income tax compliance processes.
• Demonstrated experience leading tax technology, data, automation, co-sourcing, or process transformation initiatives.
• Hands-on experience with tax provision and compliance systems, complex calculation models, data validation, and process controls.
• Strong leadership, analytical, project management, technical writing, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
• Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and proficiency with corporate tax provision and compliance software.

An outstanding professional will have...
• Master's degree in Taxation, Accounting, Finance, Information Systems, or a related discipline.
• Experience with OneSource Tax Provision and OneSource Income Tax Compliance.
• Experience with multinational consumer, retail, apparel, luxury goods, or other complex public company operations.
• Experience with tax data governance, ERP and tax-system integrations, reporting analytics, workflow automation, or generative AI tools in a controlled corporate environment.
• Exposure to domestic and international tax calculations, OECD Pillar Two, transactions, and legal entity restructuring.

title: Seasonal Orchard Work - Thinning 2026
description:
Looking for full-time work over your school or university holidays?

We have full-time apple thinning opportunities available across our orchards in Hastings, Napier and Central Hawke’s Bay from November through to December.

This is a great opportunity to earn money over summer, stay active outdoors and gain hands-on experience in New Zealand’s horticulture industry.

What you'll be doing

Apple thinning is an important part of producing our high-quality apples. You will be removing excess apples from trees, helping the remaining apples to grow to the quality standards we’re known for around the world. You'll receive training and support from our experienced orchard teams.

This role involves:

  • Working outdoors in a range of weather conditions
  • Being on your feet for most of the day
  • Repetitive hand and arm movements
  • Carrying and working from ladders
  • Walking across uneven orchard terrain
  • Working as part of a team to meet quality and productivity targets

What you'll bring

  • Availability to work full-time throughout the thinning season (November to December)
  • A good level of physical fitness and the ability to perform repetitive manual work
  • Confidence working outdoors and on ladders
  • Reliable transport to and from work each day
  • A positive attitude, strong work ethic and willingness to learn
  • Reliability and the ability to turn up ready to work each day
  • The ability to work well as part of a team
  • The legal right to work in New Zealand and the ability to pass pre-employment checks

Note: If you have exams, planned leave or other commitments, we encourage you to discuss these with us during the recruitment process.

What we offer

  • Hourly rate of $23.95, with piece rate opportunities available
  • Full-time seasonal work
  • Training and support from experienced orchard teams
  • A great team environment where your contribution is valued
  • The opportunity to stay active and work outdoors
  • Exposure to New Zealand's largest apple growing and export business
  • The chance to earn money and build experience over your summer break

Who we are

At Mr Apple, apples are what we do. As New Zealand’s largest apple grower and exporter, we proudly grow, pack and market premium apples enjoyed around the world.

Our success comes from our people. With more than 2,00 team members from a wide range of background, we’re committed to creating opportunities for people to learn, develop and contribute to something they can be proud of.

Join us this summer and be a part of a team helping deliver the perfect crunch to customers around the world.

title: Processing Operator II
description:
Department: South Plant Plant Processing
Reports To: Processing Supervisor
Hours: 7 PM - 7 AM
Job Summary:

Processing Operator is responsible for operating dryer and mill room to process clay into a finished product, and applying inspection and test methods to determine product conformance.

2026 USA TODAY Top Workplaces
2026 Forbes Most Successful Small-Cap Companies
2025 Large Business of the Year: Awarded by Imagine Thomasville

Essential Functions:

Operates and maintains the milling, screening and drying processes.

Understands internal customer needs and specifications and takes action to meet expectations.

Understands process of feeding clay from the shed to dryer and communicates modifications needed to meet specifications.

Adjusts equipment operating controls to modify product properties in response to specifications, raw material properties, ambient conditions, etc.

Assures standards are being met.

Monitors equipment operation by observation of gauges, test data, or direct observation

Sets up equipment for different product runs.

Troubleshoots problems in the mill and dryer area.

Apply inspection and test methods to determine product conformance.

Collects samples and performs specific analytical test on products and raw materials to measure conformance to specifications.

Understand what the data is saying and takes actions as needed, i.e., communicates with processing, warehouse and packaging teammates to ensure that necessary adjustments are made to keep products conforming to specifications.

Communicates verbally, i.e. answers inquiries and provides information.

Assures all safety rules, regulations and precautions are followed.

Assures areas are clean and free of clutter.

Assists in maintaining equipment in the processing area.

Performs daily routine maintenance of equipment.

Performs basic repairs and works with maintenance personnel to complete other repairs as needed.

Performs safety and mechanic inspections to maintain mill and dryer systems.

Operates front-end loader and bobcat as needed. Training must be documented before operating equipment.

Performs other duties as assigned

Acquire further training and proficiency in other job functions on processing team.

Provide back-up support for other positions on the processing team

Provide back-up support to other departments as needed

Actively seek and identify improvement opportunities to reduce losses, and implement measures, in coordination with the full team to effect those improvements.

Other actions as needed to satisfy company goals, processes, and procedures, and to uphold the values inherent to Oil – Dri.

Experience:

Must meet the assessment requirements for this position

Must possess basic mechanical skills

Must be able to visually monitor electronic equipment, cameras and control panels to be able to interpret the data and take appropriate actions.

Must be able to read and comprehend product specifications.

Must have basic understanding of process controls.

Must understand all safety requirements and other communications.

Must have good verbal communication skills

Must have the ability to use tools

Must be able to enter data into computer databases.

Must be willing to make decisions within the scope of his responsibilities be accountable for those decisions.

Must satisfy the spirit of WE CARE.

Must be able to stand for the duration of the shift

Must be able to lift 50 pounds frequently

Bending, reaching, twisting, stooping, walking, and climbing stairways and ladders frequently

Must be able to climb ladders up to 100 feet

Must be able to communicate clearly by radio, telephone, and in person

Must be able to function in the required role while wearing appropriate PPE including, but not limited to: Safety glasses, hearing protection, hard hat, dust mask, protective coveralls, and other as may be required by a hot/cold, dusty, loud industrial environment.

Must meet all physical requirements of the position. Hire Rate $22.64 + $2.00 shift differential

title: Team Coordinator
description:
Why Join EML?


An Award-Winning Celebratory Culture That Recognises You


EML is known for its strong culture of appreciation, connection and celebration. Our people benefit from a powerful Reward & Recognition program, with more than 30,000 recognition moments shared in a single year, making our people feel valued and supported.


Flexibility That Supports Your Life

After your probation (subject to performance), you have the flexibility to work from home along with the choice between:

  • Monthly rostered days off, or
  • A 9-day fortnight

giving you more control over your time and work life balance.


Grow With a Specialist Organisation


Because personal injury is the only thing we do, EML offers one of the most stable and future‑focused careers in the industry. Our deep expertise, purpose‑driven work and development pathways help you build a long‑term career in a field where your skills will always be in demand. EML’s investment in AI-powered technology is designed to reduce admin, giving you more time to focus on making a real difference in people’s lives.



Make a real difference in people's lives with EML


As part of our diverse team based in Sydney you will help make a positive impact on someone’s life every day. You will feel great satisfaction knowing your talent and hard work has a purpose.

Working in a small but high-performing team, you’ll play an important role supporting senior leadership, their teams and the broader business unit, while helping to create a positive and productive workplace experience. This opportunity has become available due to an internal promotion, reflecting the development and career growth opportunities available at EML.

You'll be the backbone of administrative support across the NI SME&S business operations, ensuring our leaders and teams can operate effectively and efficiently. Providing high quality administrative operational support as well as exceptional customer service for our internal and external stakeholders, you'll manage competing priorities, coordinate key business activities, and help maintain the smooth day to day running of our offices.

This role is ideal for someone who is highly organised, proactive and detail-focused, with a strong ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality outcomes in a fast-paced environment. You’ll bring excellent communication and interpersonal skills, enabling you to build strong working relationships and support stakeholders at all levels, while maintaining a high level of accuracy and discretion across all documentation, reporting and correspondence. You take initiative, are confident navigating competing demands, and are comfortable working both independently and as part of a collaborative team, with advanced capability across the Microsoft Office suite preferred but not essential.

This will be a permanent, full-time position based in our Sydney office, with flexibility to work from home once fully trained.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Provide responsive, professional and customer focused support to senior leaders and stakeholders across the business.
  • Coordinate travel, business purchases, shared inbox enquiries and a range of administrative activities.
  • Support employee engagement initiatives, recognition activities and workplace events that contribute to a positive employee experience.
  • Collaborate with the broader administration team to deliver consistent, high-quality support and identify opportunities for continuous improvement.
  • Build strong stakeholder relationships, manage competing priorities and contribute to the successful delivery of team and business objectives.

What We’re Looking For

  • You bring strong written and verbal communication skills, a customer focused mindset, and a natural ability to build rapport and develop effective relationships with a diverse range of stakeholders.
  • Highly organised and detail-focused, you take pride in producing accurate, high-quality work across documentation, reporting and correspondence, while managing competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
  • Adaptable, resilient and enjoy problem solving, remaining calm and effective when priorities shift or unexpected challenges arise.
  • You take ownership of your work, demonstrate initiative and always looking for ways to improve processes, solve issues and support those around you.
  • Comfortable working both independently and as part of a team, you handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion and professionalism.
  • You have strong technical capability and are confident using Microsoft Office applications and learning new systems and technology (advanced skills preferred but not essential).

Why You’ll Love Being Part of EML


You’ll enjoy a range of benefits designed to support your wellbeing, growth and success:


  • Hybrid work options for better balance.
  • Fitness Passport providing heavily discounted access to your local gyms, pools and fitness facilities.
  • Discounts at 350+ retailers via RewardsHub plus discounts with corporate banking, super and private health insurance partners.
  • Corporate wellbeing program, including gym and health insurance discounts.
  • Comprehensive learning and development tailored to help you grow.
  • More than a traditional Employee Assistance Program, our EAP provides access to professional medical advice and safety features for our employees and their families
  • Company-wide celebration events that keep us connected.
  • Annual incentive scheme + regular salary reviews.

Ready to Make an Impact?


If you're looking for a purposeful, people‑focused career with stability, balance and a culture that celebrates you we would love to hear from you.


Apply now and help people get their lives back.

title: On-Call Digital Project Manager
description:
The Team

You'll work as the primary point of delivery alongside a cross-functional team of engineers, UX designers and researchers, business analysts, product managers, analytics specialists, content strategists, and accessibility experts. We partner closely with state and federal stakeholders to deliver, enhance, and continuously improve public-facing websites and digital services. Working collaboratively, we bring together strategy, design, and delivery to create holistic, user-centered solutions that meet mission needs, comply with accessibility standards, and drive measurable outcomes.

The Work

In this individual contributor role, you will support the planning and execution of work for two cross-functional delivery teams focused on modernizing existing state and federal digital services and websites that support high-impact public programs. You’ll work closely with team members and clients to help prioritize deliverables based on agreed-upon roadmaps, coordinate releases, track dependencies, and ensure work stays aligned to timelines and desired outcomes. You’ll partner with a diverse set of stakeholders and decision makers to maintain clarity, momentum, and transparency throughout delivery.

A key part of the work is strengthening how teams operate: refining intake and prioritization, improving Agile ceremonies and ways of working, clarifying roles and decision paths, and establishing repeatable processes for quality, accessibility, and continuous improvement. If you enjoy complex, mission-driven work where thoughtful collaboration and steady delivery discipline make a visible difference, this is a great opportunity to grow and lead.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Ability to work in a matrixed mode and lead cross disciplinary teams.
  • Actively communicate with clients to understand and define current needs and priorities.
  • Establish and maintain schedules, product roadmaps, and release plans in accordance with customer and stakeholder needs.
  • Manage budgets, prepare cost estimates, and track resources using financial management tools
  • Perform continuous risk assessment and mitigation; work with management to identify and remove resource, feasibility, and technical barriers that can impede development
  • Maintain a positive, results-oriented work environment by building partnerships with internal and external partners
  • Foster a culture of creativity, collaboration, innovation, and excellence in the work environment and continuously elevate the quality and caliber of the organization.
  • Manage projects independently, be self-motivated to identify and manage risks, and committed to achieving project goals and milestones.

*** As an on-call with our team, you might work zero to 30 hours per week, depending on our workload.

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in related field.
  • 5+ years project management experience leading digital development efforts
  • Ability to obtain a Public Trust Clearance.
  • Must be a US Citizen, required by the federal government client.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • PMP certification
  • Understanding of human-centered design principles and integrating design
  • Demonstrated experience with the software development cycle including working with cross disciplinary teams, including UX and engineering
  • Ability to provide technical strategic guidance to the customer and project team.
  • Experience launching digital solutions, including ongoing analysis and continuous product improvements.
  • Experience managing budgets and resource allocation.
  • Working knowledge of the technical software development process, Agile delivery methods including Agile Scrum and/or Kanban
  • Proficiency working with JIRA and Confluence.
  • Team player with excellent problem-solving and consensus-building skills.
  • Experience working with state and Federal government
  • Experience working with Drupal or other open source applications

title: Tank Farm Operator
description:
PURPOSE:
Manage ship-to-shore operations and oil movement activities (Tank Farm) in alignment with Lubricant Quality Standards. Supervise the daily blending of lubricants as scheduled by the Production Planner to ensure seamless operations and high-quality output.

NATURE AND SCOPE:
The Tank Farm Operator reports directly to the Plant Manager and is responsible for overseeing bulk receipt operations via marine vessels, ISO tanks, and tank lorries, ensuring accurate system-related activities and documentation.

This role's key challenge lies in producing on-spec batches without requiring corrections, ensuring precise input, and adherence to quality and safety standards. The operator supervises batch initiation, additive dosages, and compliance with laboratory instructions while documenting and reporting actual inputs and discrepancies.

Additionally, the operator ensures timely and accurate SAP entries for bulk receipts, facilitates lab sample dispatches, and coordinates with filling operations once lab clearance is confirmed.

This is a shift-based role and involves contractor staff management.

PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES:

  1. Tank Operations and Documentation:
    • Supervise weekly tank dipping and sealing/locking of tanks.
    • Record and arrange re-use of part fillers/slops based on laboratory guidance.
    • Document inputs for batches and blends, reporting discrepancies to the lab.
    • Perform accurate and timely system entries for bulk receipts in SAP.
  2. Receipt Operations:
    • Supervise and perform decantation of base oil from tank lorries, ISO tanks, flexibags, and sea vessels.
    • Pre-arrival coordination between terminal and vessels for smooth operations.
    • Conduct hourly comparisons of ship-to-shore figures during receipt operations and verify quality and quantity of shipments.
    • Calculate loss/gain during receipt operations and perform root cause analysis (RCA) for variances.
  3. Ship-to-Shore and Oil Movement Operations:
    • Conduct ship-to-shore operations in compliance with Group policies and best practices.
    • Manage oil movement facilities using manual and automated systems for product transfer, storage, and loading.
    • Handle non-standard discharge operations, including lightering and ship-to-ship transfers, while coordinating with port/jetty authorities.
  4. Blending Operations:
    • Oversee blending processes.
    • Monitor additive dosage and ensure compliance with lab instructions.
    • Facilitate dispatch of blend samples to the laboratory and coordinate production based on lab clearance.
  5. Equipment Maintenance and Coordination:
    • Liaise with the Maintenance team for repairs and upkeep of blending equipment, boiler, compressor, pumps, and related facilities.
    • Liaise with Planning and Maintenance teams to ensure maintenance of bulk storage tanks as per defined schedule.
    • Ensure calibration of all metering equipment in coordination with Maintenance team
    • Maximize availability of ship-to-shore, oil movement, and associated equipment.
  6. Audit and Continuous Improvement:
    • Facilitate internal and external audits, ensuring accurate and complete documentation.
    • Address audit findings and implement corrective actions.
    • Identify and execute process improvement opportunities for efficiency and compliance.
  7. Collaboration and Communication:
    • Engage regularly with vessel surveyors, handlers, and port authorities to ensure smooth discharge operations.
    • Conduct demurrage analysis to improve operational efficiency.
  8. Health, Safety, Security, and Environment (HSSE):
    • Actively promote HSSE culture and mindset and engage in HSSE activities.
    • Conduct regular safety audits, drills, and compliance checks.
  9. Quality and Environmental Management Systems:
    • Implement QMS and EMS practices as per ISO 9001:2015 and ISO 14001:2015 standards.
  10. Additional Responsibilities:
    • Act as SAP Superuser for blending and receipt functions.
    • Ensure the safety of personnel and company assets throughout operations.

Key Competencies:

  • Strong knowledge of ship-to-shore, oil movement operations and HSSE fundamentals.
  • Proficiency in SAP.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to perform root cause analysis.
  • Effective communication and collaboration with internal teams and external stakeholders.
  • Familiarity with quality and environmental management systems (ISO standards).

Education - Engineering (Petroleum/Chemical/Mechanical/Electrical)
Experience – 3 to 6 years
Work schedule - 5 day work week with shift duties and Saturday working based on production demand
Job location – Kemari

Job Description:

Advance how our customers operate while you advance your career. Join GDIT as a Zero Trust ICAM & PKI SME and build an impactful career in enterprise IT, collaborating with people who are driven and resourceful like you.

MEANINGFUL WORK AND PERSONAL IMPACT

As a Zero Trust ICAM & PKI SME, the work you do at GDIT will be impactful to the mission of supporting infrastructure security on the CITS contract for USCENTCOM. You will play a crucial role in leading the engineering, deployment, and operational integration of identity-centric, credentialing, and access control solutions across USCENTCOM’s network enclaves, aligned with DoD Zero Trust principles.

HOW A ZERO TRUST ICAM & PKI SME WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

Your responsibilities span across the three core ICAM pillars:

1. Identity Management (Identity Lifecycle & Directory Services)

  • Design, implement, and maintain enterprise Identity Management solutions, prioritizing DISA’s enterprise solution to ensure seamless integration with Zero Trust architectures.

  • Architect and manage Master User Records (MUR), directory services (e.q., Active Directory), and Automated Account Provisioning (AAP) pipelines.

  • Troubleshoot complex identity synchronization, profile mapping, and lifecycle workflows across heterogeneous enclaves and mission partners.

  • Build, deploy, and maintain identity connectors and integrations with enterprise HR/authoritative data sources and cloud environments.

  • Maintain system documentation, data dictionaries, and SOPs for identity lifecycle management tasks.

2. Credentialing & PKI (Authenticators, Non-Person Entities & Cryptography)

  • Design, engineer, and operate enterprise Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) solutions aligned with DoD/NSS PKI standards, CNSSP-1300, and CJCSM requirements.

  • Configure, harden, and maintain Certification Authorities (CAs), Registration Authorities (RAs), Validation Authorities (OCSP), and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs).

  • Architect and operationalize enterprise Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM) processes, automating certificate issuance, renewal, and revocation across web servers, endpoints, and secure communication channels.

  • Implement Network Device Enrollment and automated Non-Person Entity (NPE) credentialing utilizing protocols such as SCEP, EST, and ACME.

  • Lead PKI-enablement for enterprise applications, network appliances, and workloads to enforce mutual TLS (mTLS) and smart-card/phishing-resistant MFA (CAC/PIV, hardware tokens).

  • Maintain disaster recovery, business continuity, and key recovery/custody plans for cryptographic infrastructure.

3. Access Management & Governance (Authorization, Federation & PAM)

  • Configure, enforce, and optimize fine-grained access control models, including Role-Based (RBAC), Attribute-Based (ABAC), Policy-Based (PBAC), and Identity-Based Access Control (IBAC).

  • Lead the deployment and operational administration of Privileged Access Management (PAM) platforms (e.g., Delinea) to safeguard privileged accounts and enforce just-in-time access.

  • Implement Identity Governance and Administration (IGA) solutions (e.g., SailPoint) for access certifications, segregation of duties (SoD), and role mining.

  • Troubleshoot complex federation and Single Sign-On (SSO) integrations utilizing modern protocols (SAML 2.0, OAuth 2.0, OIDC).

  • Collaborate with multi-disciplinary cybersecurity teams to enforce continuous authentication and dynamic authorization in line with Zero Trust principles.

Cross-Pillar Operations & Compliance

  • Perform regular maintenance, vulnerability scanning, security STIG remediation, and patching across all ICAM and PKI server environments.

  • Ensure strict adherence to DoD ICAM policies, DISA STIGs, FIPS cryptographic benchmarks, and DoD Zero Trust reference architectures.

  • Interface with third-party vendors (e.g., F5, Microsoft, SailPoint, Delinea, Keyfactor, Thales) for tier-3/escalated troubleshooting.

  • Produce management reports, audit metrics, compliance packages, and system administration runbooks.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED

Bring your technology expertise and drive for innovation to GDIT. The Zero Trust ICAM & PKI SME must have:

  • Clearance: Active Secret

  • Citizenship: U.S. Citizenship required

  • Education: Bachelor's Degree in a related discipline (Cybersecurity or Information Assurance concentration preferred) or six (6) years of real-world or military experience in information assurance, network security, or systems administration.

  • Certification: Applicable DoD 8140 / DoD 8570 IAT Level II/III or IAM Level II/III Certification (e.g., Security+ CE, CASP+, CISSP) along with relevant role-based credentials (e.g., CIAM, CIGE, CIMP, Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate, or Okta Certified Professional).

  • Experience: 10+ years of related engineering and operations experience in enterprise IT and cybersecurity.

Technical Competencies by Pillar

1. Identity Management

  • 10+ years of experience in enterprise identity architectures and directory infrastructure (Active Directory, LDAP).

  • Deep understanding of Master User Records (MUR), Identity Governance & Administration (IGA platforms such as SailPoint), and automated provisioning workflows.

  • Familiarity with DISA enterprise identity solutions and federal identity federation models.

2. Credentialing & PKI

  • In-depth expertise in Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) concepts: X.509 certificates, CA trust hierarchies, Certificate Revocation Lists (CRLs), and Online Certificate Status Protocol (OCSP).

  • Hands-on engineering experience administering enterprise CA platforms (e.g., Microsoft AD CS, Keyfactor) and integrating with DoD/Federal PKI (FPKI).

  • Direct experience with Certificate Lifecycle Management (CLM) tools and automated enrollment protocols (SCEP, EST, ACME).

  • Experience with CAC/PIV middleware, hardware tokens, and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs) (e.g., Thales/SafeNet).

3. Access Management & Governance

  • Advanced proficiency in designing and implementing access control models (RBAC, ABAC, PBAC, and IBAC).

  • Hands-on experience configuring and managing Privileged Access Management (PAM) suites (e.g., Delinea).

  • Strong understanding of modern authentication protocols and federation mechanisms (SAML 2.0, OAuth, OpenID Connect, Kerberos, mTLS).

  • Proven experience supporting Zero Trust policy enforcement points (PEP) and policy decision points (PDP).

Desired Skills & Qualifications

  • Microsoft Windows Hybrid Administrator or ITIL 4 Foundation Certification.

  • Operational familiarity with USCENTCOM mission networks, enclaves, and operating environments.

  • Scripting and automation proficiency (PowerShell, Python, or Bash) for automating identity provisioning and certificate management workflows.

  • Experience integrating mTLS and certificate validation within enterprise API gateways, microservices, and reverse proxies.

  • Proven ability to author system architecture documents, CONOPS, disaster recovery runbooks, and engineering implementation guides.

Travel Requirements

title: Sr. Manufacturing Process Flow & Control DFX Engineer
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

Blue Origin's Emerging Systems business unit is building TeraWave, a satellite communications constellation powered by the most advanced optical communications architecture ever attempted: thousands of optically interconnected satellites delivering symmetrical data speeds of up to 6 Tbps anywhere on Earth, providing enterprise and hyperscale customers with resilient, scalable connectivity for critical operations where terrestrial infrastructure cannot reach.

As a Senior Manufacturing Process Flow & Control DFX Engineer, you will own the end-to-end manufacturing process flow and process control design integration for TeraWave production — bridging production line architecture, process control systems, and volume production readiness. As a foundational element of TeraWave operations, hardware must be produced through process flows architected not only for throughput but for manufacturability, testability, reliability, and serviceability at constellation scale. This is a hands-on role for an engineer who has designed, optimized, and scaled complex manufacturing process flows and control systems in fast-moving, high-volume manufacturing environments and wants to apply that experience to hardware operating at orbital scale.

Special Mentions:

  • Relocation assistance is available for qualified candidates.
  • Travel: Up to 50%.

Responsibilities:

Process Flow & Control Design, Integration & Manufacturing

  • Lead manufacturing process flow design for satellite modules and subsystems: production line architecture, workflow sequencing, station design, takt time optimization, and material flow.
  • Own process control development — including statistical process control (SPC), process monitoring, traveler and work instruction systems, MES integration, and data collection workflows — to ensure robust, repeatable production.
  • Manage process documentation, routing definition, capacity planning, vendor and internal coordination, and production line oversight.
  • Drive process validation, control plan development, first-article and production readiness reviews to support production ramp.

Design for Excellence (DFX)

  • Drive Design for Excellence (DFX) principles — DFM, DFT, DFA, DFR, and DFS — across the full manufacturing process flow and control lifecycle to ensure hardware scales from prototype through volume production for TeraWave operations.
  • Design for Manufacturability (DFM): Optimize process sequencing, station layout, and workflow design to maximize yield, throughput, and minimize cost at constellation-scale production volumes.
  • Design for Test (DFT): Architect in-line test and inspection points, data capture, and process monitoring to enable efficient factory acceptance, traceability, and in-field diagnostics.
  • Design for Assembly (DFA): Simplify process steps, minimize handoffs, and optimize station design to reduce cycle time, rework, and error rates across the line.
  • Design for Reliability (DFR): Apply process FMEA, control plans, statistical process control, and reliability prediction to ensure consistent, defect-free production supporting long-duration operation in the orbital environment.
  • Design for Serviceability/Supply Chain (DFS): Coordinate with supply chain and manufacturing partners to align process flows with material availability, standardization, and obsolescence mitigation across the production lifecycle.
  • Partner with manufacturing, quality, and supply chain teams to define acceptance criteria, drive yield and throughput optimization, and support production ramp for sustained TeraWave operations.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field.
  • 10+ years of experience in manufacturing process engineering, process flow design, or production control in a product development and volume production environment.
  • Experience designing and optimizing manufacturing process flows, line balancing, and process control systems for complex hardware.
  • Hands-on experience with statistical process control (SPC), process FMEA, control plans, MES/ERP systems, and production line bring-up.
  • Demonstrated application of DFX principles (DFM/DFT/DFA/DFR) in bringing process flows from design into volume production.
  • Excellent technical documentation and communication skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's degree in Industrial, Manufacturing, or Mechanical Engineering.
  • 15+ years of relevant experience.
  • Lean Six Sigma certification (Green Belt or Black Belt) or equivalent process improvement expertise.
  • Experience with high-mix or high-volume production line design, automation integration, and Industry 4.0 / smart factory concepts.
  • Experience developing process flows for space, aviation, or other high-reliability manufacturing environments.
  • Experience with capacity modeling, simulation, and throughput analysis tools.
  • Background in production hardware including comprehensive DFX practices (DFM/DFT/DFA/DFR), process optimization, supply chain coordination, and yield optimization at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with production ramp and factory scale-up.

Why Blue Origin

At Blue Origin, we are driven by Gradatim Ferociter — "Step by Step, Ferociously." As a Senior Manufacturing Process Flow & Control DFX Engineer, you will design and industrialize the production processes building an orbital constellation at unprecedented scale, alongside world-class engineers solving problems at the intersection of advanced manufacturing, process control, and spaceflight.


Base Pay Range for:

CA applicants is $156,802.00 - $219,522.45

Other site ranges may differ


Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.


Export Control Regulations

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


Background Check

  • Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
  • Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
  • Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
  • Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

  • Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
  • Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)

  • Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.
