2027 Summer Intern, Contracts Administration

At ICF, we work on projects that have an impact on real people. From ensuring families have a house that will survive the next hurricane, to helping curb teen vaping, to keeping our nation safe from cybersecurity threats, and more - ICFers are changemakers who do work with purpose.

We are currently hiring interns to join our Contracts, Procurement and Pricing (CPP) teams (Contracts, Subcontracts, Purchasing, and Compliance). This group is part of the internal support process within ICF, helping the project teams win and manage their projects. We help shape policy and procedures to comply with government, commercial, state, and local practices to ensure we remain compliant with our client guidelines. Some of ICF’s major clients include Federal Highway Administration, Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), Exelon Utilities, LA Metro, Centers for Disease Control (CDC), Army Research Institute and Puerto Rico Dept of Housing.

This is a full-time, 10-week, entry level internship position that begins in June and ends in August 2027. The internship will work a hybrid schedule from our Reston, VA office (2x per week). At this time, we are unable to provide relocation nor housing assistance. Pay is $23 per hour.

As a Contracts Intern, you will provide direct support to the ICF Contract Administration (CA) Team by:

  • Assisting with the review of Non-Disclosure and Teaming Agreements for future business opportunities where ICF will be a subcontractor.

  • Assisting with the management of contract files on the Contracts’ SharePoint site (e.g., naming, reorganizing, uploading documents, identifying documents by type and tagging them).

  • Assisting with contract set-ups in our Contract Management System.

  • Assisting with internal data calls and internal audits.

You will gain valuable experience in the proposal development process from the CA’s point of view to include:

  • Reviewing solicitation terms and conditions (RFPs, etc.)

  • Assisting with the business/price volume response to include: compliance review, writing the price narrative, and completing required forms/certifications.

  • Coordination with the proposal response team, including Pricing, Subcontracts, Proposal Coordinators, et al., including attending formal proposal review meetings.

As a Subcontracts Administration Intern, you will provide direct support to the Subcontracts Administration Team by:

  • Assisting with the drafting of Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), Teaming Agreements, and modifications to existing agreements related to future business opportunities where ICF may engage companies or independent consultants as subcontractors or partners.

  • Supporting vendor setup and maintaining subcontract records in SharePoint to help ensure the accuracy and completeness of subcontract compliance files.

  • Using Microsoft Copilot and other approved productivity tools, as appropriate, to assist with summarizing solicitation or agreement requirements, organizing compliance information, and improving the efficiency and quality of administrative work products, subject to review and approval by the Subcontracts Administration Team.

  • Assisting with the preparation of subcontractor Requests for Proposals (RFPs) and Requests for Quotations (RFQs) for distribution to external vendors, consultants, or teaming partners.

You will gain valuable experience in subcontract management and proposal development from the perspective of Subcontracts Administration, including:

  • Reviewing Requests for Proposals (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), and related solicitation documents to identify subcontract requirements, terms, and conditions.

  • Coordinating with proposal response teams, including Pricing, Contracts, Proposal Coordinators, and other stakeholders, by attending formal proposal and subcontract review meetings.

  • Supporting communications with potential and existing subcontractors regarding documentation, compliance requirements, and related administrative needs.

As a Purchasing Intern, you will provide direct support to the ICF Purchasing Team by:

  • Assisting with the review, drafting, and negotiation of Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs), Master Services Agreements (MSAs), Software as a Service (SaaS) and other software subscription agreements, Statements of Work (SOWs), and Purchase Orders (POs).

You will gain exposure to the sourcing and proposal process from a Buyer’s perspective, including:

  • Preparing and distributing Requests for Proposal (RFPs), Requests for Quotations (RFQs), and Requests for Information (RFIs).

  • Participating in supplier sourcing and competitive evaluation activities.

  • Reviewing supplier proposals for completeness, responsiveness, and compliance with procurement requirements.

  • Supporting supplier negotiations and contract award activities.

  • Assisting with supplier performance and risk assessments.

As a Compliance Intern, you will focus on supporting policy, reporting, and data analysis efforts that support the Contracts, Procurement, and Pricing team as well as other ICF stakeholders. Duties may include:

  • Creating new AI bots and job aids for purchasing system compliance topics and contracts compliance guidance

  • Researching state and local regulations and requirements for comparison with federal law

  • Tracking and updating clause matrices for U.S. Government regulations

  • Assisting in data analysis and reporting for small business utilization, prime contract data, etc.

Individuals with a focus-area preference (Contracts, Subcontracts, Purchasing, and/or Compliance) should note such on their cover letter or resume, otherwise, applicants may be considered for any of the above teams.

This newly created role is ideal for someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment, values accuracy and accountability, and is excited to help support and strengthen compliance processes.

Who We Are

Washington Mills is built on values that matter. Founded more than 150 years ago, we have earned our reputation as one of the world’s most trusted and reliable producers of abrasive, ceramic and refractory grains and powders. Serving thousands of customers and offering the broadest selection of abrasive grain and specialty electro-fused minerals in the market today, we constantly pursue growth in our products, our approach, and our people. Our founding principles of honesty, integrity and reliability still guide our business today, and we are a proud community of hands-on problem solvers, committed to shaping the materials applications of the future. title: Fuel Compliance Technician Helper
description:
It's fun to work in a company where people truly BELIEVE in what they're doing!

We're committed to bringing passion and customer focus to the business.

Position Summary

The Fuel Compliance Technician Helper supports the inspection, maintenance, repair, and regulatory compliance of fuel storage and dispensing systems. This position assists with routine inspections, preventative maintenance, troubleshooting, and repairs to help ensure fuel-system equipment remains safe, operational, and compliant with applicable federal, state, and local regulations.

The ideal candidate is dependable, mechanically inclined, safety-conscious, and detail-oriented, with a willingness to learn fuel-system inspection, maintenance, and compliance practices.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The following duties and responsibilities may be assigned as necessary:

  • Assist with monthly inspections of fuel tanks, dispensers, piping, leak-detection equipment, spill containment systems, and other fuel-system components.
  • Document inspection results, identified deficiencies, corrective actions, and maintenance activities accurately and timely.
  • Assist in maintaining fuel systems in compliance with applicable regulatory, environmental, and company requirements.
  • Assist qualified technicians with troubleshooting, maintenance, repair, and preventative maintenance of fuel-system equipment.
  • Perform basic repairs and component replacements under the direction and supervision of qualified technicians.
  • Identify leaks, damaged components, unsafe conditions, and potential compliance issues and promptly report them to the appropriate supervisor.
  • Maintain accurate and organized inspection, maintenance, and repair records.
  • Assist with testing and verifying the proper operation of fuel-system equipment following repairs or maintenance.
  • Follow all company safety procedures, environmental requirements, and applicable regulatory standards when working with fuel and petroleum products.
  • Maintain tools, equipment, work areas, and inspection supplies in a clean, safe, and serviceable condition.
  • Assist with emergency repairs and corrective actions when fuel-system issues arise.
  • Communicate inspection findings, equipment deficiencies, and repair needs to supervisors and other appropriate personnel.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

  • High school diploma or equivalent preferred.
  • Previous experience with fuel systems, automotive or mechanical equipment, construction, maintenance, or a related field is helpful but not required.
  • Basic mechanical aptitude and troubleshooting skills.
  • Ability to read and follow technical instructions, inspection procedures, and safety requirements.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to accurately document inspection and maintenance activities.
  • Ability to work independently while also taking directions from experienced technicians.
  • Valid driver's license and reliable transportation may be required.
  • Ability to work outdoors and in varied weather conditions.
  • Ability to perform physical work, including lifting and carrying tools, parts, and equipment.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Familiarity with fuel dispensers, underground storage tank systems, leak-detection systems, piping, or petroleum equipment.
  • Basic electrical, mechanical, plumbing, or equipment-repair experience.
  • Familiarity with environmental or fuel-system compliance requirements.
  • Relevant industry certifications or willingness to obtain required certifications.
  • Strong willingness to learn and develop technical skills in fuel-system inspection, maintenance, and compliance.

Working Conditions

This position primarily involves working outdoors at fuel stations and other petroleum-related facilities. Employees may be exposed to fuel vapors, petroleum products, machinery, confined or restricted work areas, noise, and varying weather conditions.

Employees are required to follow all established safety procedures and properly use personal protective equipment (PPE) when performing job duties.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, kneel, climb, reach, and work in awkward or confined positions.
  • Ability to lift and carry tools, parts, equipment, and other materials as required.
  • Ability to safely operate and use hand and power tools.
  • Ability to work around fuel storage and dispensing equipment while following established safety procedures.
  • Ability to perform repetitive physical tasks associated with inspection, maintenance, and repair activities.

If you like wild growth and working with happy, enthusiastic over-achievers, you'll enjoy your career with us!

title: Staff Software Engineer
description:
Finstro is building a new Credit Decisioning Engine and the pipeline that runs our internal credit workflow. It is the first of several major builds on the roadmap, and this role is the senior technical builder across them. Expect your scope to move with it: credit workflow tooling, integration with core lending and ledger systems, and the data services that feed risk and reporting. This is a hands-on individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Engineering. You set the architecture, then you build it - you will be in the code, in the design reviews and in the production dashboards.

We are looking for someone who is pragmatic rather than dogmatic. The work is greenfield, so the constraints come from the domain rather than from legacy: credit decisions are consequential, they are reviewed long after they are made, and from December 2026 they sit under explicit regulatory expectations about how they are explained. Designing for that from the first commit is the core of the job. This is the first Staff hire into a new Sydney engineering team.

About Finstro

Finstro is a fast-growing non-bank lender, providing businesses with cash flow, flexibility and confidence every step of the way. We go beyond rigid product silos and understand speed is only a part of the answer.

Since 2012, we’ve supported the growth aspirations of over 6,000 businesses through over $2.5b of funded transactions.

If you have energy, ambition and want to work for a dynamic, rapid growth, FinTech business, there are exciting opportunities to advance your career by joining our global team.

Principal Accountabilities

• Architecture and technical direction. Own the design of the engine and the services around it: boundaries, orchestration, what gets versioned. In twelve months, it is live on real volume, and the team can extend it without you.

• Modular data acquisition. Credit bureaus, banking and open banking feeds, accounting platforms, identity and fraud providers plug in behind stable interfaces. Adding or replacing one never touches decision logic.

• Credit policy as a versioned asset. Design how rules, policies and models are expressed, versioned, tested and released, so Credit and Risk move at their own pace and policy ships independently of the platform.

• Correctness, auditability and replay. Any decision can be reconstructed with the inputs used and the policy version applied. Proposed changes are shadow run and backtested against history before they go live.

• Observability built in. Instrumentation is part of building a component, not a later phase. From telemetry alone: which sources were called, which policy version applied, what was decided, and what it cost in third-party data. You own the latency and availability objectives.

• Standards and technical leadership. Define how we build, test, deploy and run services in this domain, then hold the line through review and working examples. Mentoring is valued, though we hire for technical depth first.

Key Skills Required

To excel in this role you will need strong hands-on backend engineering with real depth in distributed service design, and the judgement to make architectural decisions that hold up under audit years later. You are pragmatic rather than dogmatic, and comfortable being the person who both sets the direction and writes the code. Because this is the first Staff hire into a new team, you will need to work well without an established playbook: choosing the stack, setting the standards, and writing things down clearly enough that others can build on them. Fluency across backend languages (Java, Go, TypeScript or Node), AWS, infrastructure as code, observability and integration-heavy engineering is expected, as is the ability to explain technical risk and trade-offs to Credit, Risk and executive audiences.

Position Requirements

  • Strong hands-on backend engineering with real depth in distributed service design. Java, Go, TypeScript and Node are all in play; the stack is still open, and your view will shape it.

  • Designing and operating services on AWS, built cloud native and defined as code.

  • Demonstrated ownership of production observability: instrumentation strategy, metrics and distributed tracing, service level objectives, alert design, and diagnosis under time pressure.

  • Integration-heavy engineering: third-party APIs with uneven reliability, contract and schema management, versioning, and graceful degradation when a dependency fails.

  • A testing strategy that goes past unit tests: contract testing, deterministic replay of production scenarios, and evidence that a change is safe before it reaches customers.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, from engineers through to executives, including teams across time zones.

  • Effective use of AI coding tools, with a clear view of where their output can and cannot be trusted.

Preferred

  • Financial services or lending domain experience: banking, non-bank lending, payments, credit risk or core financial infrastructure.

  • Credit decisioning, scorecards, rules engines or risk platforms.

  • Designing for audit and privacy by default: data lineage, access control and retention.

  • Australian obligations relevant to lending: the Privacy Act and credit reporting, the automated decision-making transparency requirements commencing December 2026, and the Consumer Data Right.

  • A regulated or audited environment (ISO 27001, SOC 2, PCI DSS or APRA-aligned).

Working Arrangement

The role is based in our Sydney CBD office five days a week for the first six months while the team and its ways of working are established, moving to a hybrid agreement afterwards.

title: Maintenance Shift Lead
description:

We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.

As part of a hardworking team of specialists, you will lead the maintenance team in ensuring all production assets are maintained to OEM/company standards by coordinating and overseeing preventative maintenance schedules, and directing detailed troubleshooting and repair activities for plant equipment.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead, mentor, and supervise the equipment maintenance team responsible for preventive and corrective maintenance on a variety of industrial equipment, including robots, welders, furnaces, lasers, multi-axis mills, lathes, VTLs, and more.

  • Oversee and direct troubleshooting, repair, and ongoing maintenance of complex electrical control systems, including PLCs, HMIs, sensors, and VFDs.

  • Manage work requests, assign tasks to maintenance technicians, and ensure timely completion of work orders.

  • Coordinate emergency and unscheduled repairs, including managing overtime or shift coverage as necessary to maintain operational readiness.

  • Schedule, prioritize, and assign orders to meet operational and production deadlines.

  • Promote 5S principles of organizing and sustaining efficient and presentable team workspaces

  • Manage team performance, provide regular feedback and coaching, set near and long term goals, and conduct performance evaluations to support the professional growth and effectiveness of maintenance team members.

  • Champion and enforce safety procedures, practices, and training to ensure a safe industrial environment for all team members.

  • Administer and ensure accurate record-keeping within the Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS).

Qualifications:

  • Passion for our mission: Millions of people living and working in space!

  • Completion of secondary education (High School Diploma or GED) required.

  • Minimum of 3+ years’ supervisory or team leadership experience in a maintenance or industrial environment.

  • Minimum 6 years’ hands-on experience in a multi-skilled maintenance role.

  • Read and interpret electrical schematics, ladder logic diagrams, and P&IDs.

  • Experience with VFDs, servo drives, HMI interfaces, and industrial instrumentation.

  • Familiarity with NEC, NFPA 70E, and general electrical safety practices.

  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, with proven ability to foster teamwork and positive culture.

  • Strong self-motivation and organizational skills; able to prioritize and manage multiple projects.

  • Adaptable to changing priorities and capable of thriving in a fast-paced environment.

  • Ability to earn trust, maintain positive and professional relationships, and contribute to a culture of inclusion.

  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Desired:

  • Background in robotic systems, CNC equipment, and predictive maintenance technologies

  • Proficiency in PLC troubleshooting (Studio 5000, TIA Portal, etc.).

  • Fanuc, Haas, Siemens and Heidenhain controls experience

  • Experience operating heavy lifting equipment such as overhead cranes and forklifts around flight critical hardware

  • Experience with root cause analysis and continuous improvement methodologies.

  • A.S. degree in relevant technical field (Mechanical, Electrical, Automation, or related technology) preferred.

Additional Requirements:

  • Ability to perform physical tasks, including standing, kneeling, crouching, twisting, and working in confined spaces.

  • Capability to regularly climb stairs or ladders throughout the shift.

  • Ability to lift materials up to 25 lbs unassisted as part of daily duties.

  • Willingness to work overtime and weekends as needed to support operations.

At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


Background Check

  • Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
  • Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

Benefits

title: SQL Server Database Administrator (Azure-Hosted Environment)
description:
Remote Employee BPO has an outstanding opportunity for you!


﻿

Role: ﻿SQL Server Database Administrator (Azure-Hosted Environment)

Compensation: Competitive Basic Salary

Benefits: HMO plus 2 Free Dependents, P1,500 Rice Allowance.

Work Schedule: 5-day work week, 10:00 p.m. 7:00 a.m. Philippine time

Work Setup: Work From Home

﻿

ABOUT THE ROLE

We are looking for an experienced SQL Server Database Administrator to join our engineering team. In this role, you will own the health, performance, and integrity of our database infrastructure across both on-premises and Azure environments. A core focus of this position is building and maintaining automated data quality and accuracy monitoring systems — ensuring our data pipelines stay clean, consistent, and trustworthy at scale. You will partner closely with developers and product managers to deliver reliable data solutions that power our customer-facing products.
﻿
﻿﻿

WHAT YOU WILL WORK ON

Design and drive elegant solutions to complex backend and data architecture challenges.

Own data quality end-to-end — build automated validation pipelines, anomaly detection routines, and reconciliation processes that proactively surface data accuracy issues before they reach customers.

Develop and maintain PowerShell scripts to automate monitoring, alerting, and remediation workflows across the data platform.

Evaluate tooling and technologies to shape the future of our data infrastructure — we value open-minded, forward-thinking approaches.

Leverage the full Azure ecosystem — including Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, and Automation Accounts — to streamline and modernize backend operations.

Collaborate with product managers and development teams to build and support new customer-facing features. Contribute to continuous improvement of backend data processes and database DevOps practices.

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES



Database Administration

﻿

  • Manage and administer SQL Server databases across on-premises and Azure environments.
  • Configure, maintain, and optimize database servers and associated processes.
  • Monitor system health and performance; proactively identify and resolve issues in real time.
  • Ensure high levels of availability, performance, sustainability, and security across all database systems.
  • Execute scheduled maintenance and support after-hours release deployment activities as needed.
  • Partner with the Senior DBA to scope and close out database-related projects.





Data Quality & Accuracy Monitoring

﻿

  • Design and implement automated data validation frameworks to continuously verify accuracy, completeness, and consistency across databases and data pipelines.
  • Build alerting and reporting systems that flag data anomalies, unexpected nulls, referential integrity violations, or statistical drift in near real time.
  • Develop reconciliation routines that cross-check data between source systems, staging layers, and downstream consumers.
  • Create and maintain data quality dashboards and audit trails to support operational visibility and compliance requirements.
  • Collaborate with engineering and data teams to define data quality SLAs and enforce them through automated controls.


﻿

Automation & Scripting

  • Automate recurring maintenance tasks, monitoring checks, and remediation workflows using PowerShell, Python, and SQL Agent jobs.
  • Refine and document automation scripts; maintain version control via Git.
  • Support database CI/CD pipelines and schema migration tooling in collaboration with DevOps.


Development Collaboration

  • Assist developers with query tuning, schema refinement, and resolution of concurrency (deadlock) issues.
  • Optimize stored procedures and functions in collaboration with the development team.

REQUIREMENTS & QUALIFICATIONS



Core Database Skills

  • Proven experience in a SQL Server DBA or equivalent role.
  • Hands-on experience with Microsoft Azure, including Azure SQL Managed Instance.
  • Proficiency with SQL Server 2016+ (2019,2022 and/or 2025 strongly preferred).
  • Demonstrated expertise in Performance Tuning and Optimization (PTO).
  • Solid knowledge of backup strategies, restore procedures, and recovery models.
  • Experience implementing High Availability (HA) and Disaster Recovery (DR) solutions for SQL Server.
  • Experience with SQL Server Data Replication and Clustering.
  • Familiarity with SQL Server CLR assemblies.
  • Experience administering Windows Server environments, including Active Directory.







Data Quality & Automation

  • Experience building or maintaining automated data validation, reconciliation, or data quality monitoring systems.
  • Proficiency in PowerShell scripting for database automation, alerting, and administrative workflows.
  • Working knowledge of Python for data quality scripting, pipeline automation, or ETL support.
  • Familiarity with Azure Monitor, Log Analytics workspaces, and alert rule configuration.
  • Understanding of data quality dimensions: accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, and uniqueness.

Professional Skills

  • Strong sense of ownership with a commitment to quality and its impact on business outcomes.
  • Excellent analytical and critical problem-solving skills under pressure.
  • Collaborative team player with strong time-management and communication skills.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with dbt (data build tool) or similar data transformation/testing frameworks.
  • Familiarity with Azure Data Factory, Synapse Analytics, or Microsoft Fabric for pipeline orchestration.
  • Experience with Great Expectations, Soda, or custom-built data quality frameworks.
  • Knowledge of database security features: Dynamic Data Masking, Always Encrypted, Transparent Data Encryption (TDE), and row-level security.
  • Experience with database CI/CD tooling such as Flyway, Liquibase, or Redgate.
  • Elasticsearch experience.
  • Microsoft certifications: MCTS, MCITP, DP-300 (Azure Database Administrator Associate), and/or MVP designation.

title: MRP Planner
description:
Role Summary

The MRP Planner is responsible for ensuring material and execution readiness to support production schedules and customer delivery commitments. This role converts the approved master schedule into an executable plan by managing material availability, supplier commitments, inventory, capacity constraints, and shipment forecasts.

Working cross-functionally with Buyers, Production Controllers, Manufacturing, and Sales Support Representatives (SSRs), the MRP Planner identifies risks, drives recovery actions, and ensures production plans can be executed on time and in alignment with customer requirements.

Responsibilities

  • Manage material readiness and shipment forecasts to support production execution and customer delivery performance.
  • Review MRP outputs, inventory positions, supplier commitments, and planning exceptions to identify and mitigate supply risks.
  • Evaluate material and capacity readiness, lead shortage management activities, and coordinate recovery actions to support work order release, production execution, and customer delivery commitments.
  • Lead shortage management and coordinate recovery actions for material, supplier, and capacity constraints.
  • Partner with Buyers, Production Controllers, Manufacturing, and SSRs to resolve shortages, delays, and execution constraints.
  • Monitor and communicate risks that may impact production schedules, customer commitments, or inventory performance.
  • Maintain planning data within the ERP system, including lead times, order policies, safety stock levels, and other planning parameters.
  • Support inventory accuracy, engineering changes, new product introductions, and supplier transitions.
  • Participate in SIOP and operational review processes, providing visibility into material and capacity risks.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives that reduce shortages, expedites, schedule disruptions, and planning exceptions.
  • Perform all work in accordance with Flowserve safety, quality, compliance, and operational excellence standards.

​Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Business, Engineering, or a related field; equivalent experience may be considered.
  • 3+ years of experience in material planning, MRP planning, production control, or supply chain operations within a manufacturing environment.
  • Experience using ERP systems to manage material requirements, inventory, purchase orders, and supplier commitments.
  • Knowledge of MRP, inventory management, capacity planning, and supply-demand balancing principles.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and proficiency with ERP reporting tools.
  • Effective communication and collaboration skills in a cross-functional manufacturing environment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • APICS/ASCM CPIM certification or active pursuit of certification.
  • Experience with SAP S/4HANA.
  • Experience in engineer-to-order, configure-to-order, make-to-order, or other complex manufacturing environments.
  • Knowledge of SIOP/S&OP, Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, and structured problem-solving methodologies.

title: Quality Inspector
description:
Work Model: This is a fully onsite role, with work performed at your designated Regal Rexnord office.

____________________

Thomson Power Systems (a Regal Rexnord company) is a leading manufacturer of electrical products and systems for use in the Power Generation Industry for over 50 years. As we are expanding into a new facility near Arlington, TX, we're seeking an exceptional quality inspector to work closely with our Quality Supervisor and the other coworkers to build and grow this new facility.

We are seeking a Quality Inspector to support quality assurance activities within our electrical panel and switchgear manufacturing operations. In this role, you will perform in-process and final inspections, ensure product compliance with quality standards, support continuous improvement initiatives, and help maintain ISO 9001 quality system requirements. The Quality Inspector partners closely with production, engineering, and quality teams to drive customer satisfaction, reduce defects, and support operational excellence.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Minimum three (3) years of manufacturing experience in electrical panel, switchgear, power distribution equipment, or a related electrical assembly environment.
  • Working knowledge of ISO 9001 quality management system requirements and quality documentation practices.
  • Ability to read and interpret electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, engineering drawings, and bills of material (BOMs).
  • Hands-on experience using inspection and test equipment including:
    • Multimeters
    • Calipers
    • Torque meters
    • Torque wrenches
    • Impact tools
  • Experience identifying defects, investigating root causes, and supporting corrective actions.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to troubleshoot quality issues in a manufacturing environment.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Demonstrated commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement.
  • Ability to uphold Regal Rexnord values including Integrity, Responsibility, Customer Success, Performance, Passion to Win, and Sense of Urgency.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Technical diploma, certificate, or associate degree in Electrical Technology, Manufacturing Technology, Quality Assurance, or a related field.
  • Experience supporting UL, customer, or third-party quality audits.
  • Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Experience utilizing quality tools such as:
    • 5S
    • Kaizen
    • SPC (Statistical Process Control)
    • FMEA
    • 8D Problem Solving
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications.
  • Experience using Power BI dashboards and quality performance reporting tools.

Key Responsibilities

Inspection & Quality Control

  • Perform in-process, final, and receiving inspections as required.
  • Create, review, and maintain inspection reports, quality checklists, and final acceptance documentation.
  • Verify products meet engineering specifications, customer requirements, and quality standards.
  • Troubleshoot quality concerns identified during inspections and support corrective action implementation.

Quality Assurance & Compliance

  • Maintain and enforce quality control procedures for assembly, testing, and finished goods operations.
  • Collaborate with engineering to interpret drawings, schematics, wiring diagrams, and BOMs.
  • Support ISO 9001 compliance activities, UL inspections, customer audits, and internal quality audits.
  • Maintain accurate inspection records and quality documentation.

Continuous Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to improve inspection methods, processes, and quality systems.
  • Monitor quality metrics including first-pass yield, defect trends, and rework rates.
  • Issue corrective actions and participate in root cause investigations.
  • Support Lean Manufacturing and Regal Business System initiatives.

Training & Team Support

  • Assist in onboarding and training new inspectors and production associates on quality standards, inspection practices, and safety requirements.
  • Promote a culture of quality awareness throughout the facility.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Production, Engineering, and Operations teams.

Safety & Equipment Management

  • Ensure all inspection activities are performed in accordance with electrical safety standards and company policies.
  • Maintain calibration records for measuring and inspection equipment.
  • Report unsafe conditions and support continuous improvement of workplace safety practices.

Key Competencies

  • Quality Inspection & Verification
  • ISO 9001 Knowledge
  • Root Cause Analysis
  • Attention to Detail
  • Electrical Print Reading
  • Problem Solving
  • Continuous Improvement Mindset
  • Communication & Collaboration
  • Documentation Accuracy
  • Leadership & Team Support

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, squat, kneel, and perform repetitive motions throughout the workday.
  • Ability to frequently lift and move materials up to 35 pounds and occasionally up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to safely use inspection and testing tools and equipment.
  • Ability to work in a manufacturing environment around electrical equipment and production operations

Benefits

  • Spending accounts (HSA, Health Care FSA and Dependent Care FSA)
  • Paid Time Off and Holidays
  • 401k Retirement Plan with Matching Employer Contributions

The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controls, actuators, drives, and precision motors, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision control in surgical tools.

  • Experience working with an interconnected mix of software systems, back-end processes, and integration functionality – including transactional systems, business intelligence and reports, and data integration pipelines via both traditional ETL and modern application programming interface (API) or message-queue approaches.
  • Experience with tools and capabilities such as Gitlab (including runners, pipelines, and API access), Jenkins, Atlassian (Jira/Confluence), OpenID Connect (OIDC), and scripting languages (ex. Bash, JavaScript, Python, Groovy, PowerShell).
  • Exceptional interpersonal, problem-solving, and trade-off analysis skills – particularly cross-team coordination where an architecture change has an impact to multiple sub-systems.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Enterprise logistics and supply chain experience, particularly medical logistics exposure related to inventory and cataloging, life-cycle management/tracking, and related industry/regulatory standards – and an understanding of logistics-related challenges as they relate to software system design and improvement.
  • Experience with the AWS GovCloud environment and managing architecture that spans a mix of existing legacy/migrating systems and cloud-based software.
  • Experience with API integration between Atlassian and Gitlab.
  • Experience or certification with the SAFe, CI/CD approaches, and advanced DevOps practices.
  • Compliance with DoDM 8140.03 Core KSATs under DCWF Work Role 627 (DevSecOps Specialist – Intermediate): Skill in: Conducting vulnerabilities scans; Recognizing vulnerabilities in information systems; Developing operations-based testing scenarios. Ability to: Identify systemic security issues based on the analysis of vulnerability and configuration data; Conduct vulnerability scans and recognize vulnerability in security systems; Develop curriculum for use within a virtual environment. Knowledge of: Systems testing and evaluation methods; Systems security testing and evaluation methods; Known vulnerabilities from alerts, advisories, errata, and bulletins; The systems engineering process; IT risk management policies, requirements, and procedures; Platforms for managing containerized workloads and services; Threat modeling, risk assessment techniques, and current best practices; How security impacts each development phase; The steps for release to higher levels of integration testing, certification activities, and/or operation; Every stage in the software project lifecycle, from initial design and build to rollout and maintenance

The person in this position will need to be able to operate a computer and other office productivity machinery, such as a calculator, copy machine and computer printer.

title: Counsel
description:
Summary

Cosm operates immersive venues at scale, which means a workforce that spans corporate staff, salaried operators, and a large hourly and event-based population across multiple states. This role is the lawyer for all of it — the employment advice, the policies and training that keep problems from starting, and the disputes that arise anyway.
We are looking for a litigator trained at a major law firm and whose instinct is own matters personally rather than forwarding them.
Posted at two levels. We will calibrate title, scope, and compensation to the experience of the person we hire.

Responsibilities

Disputes and Litigation

Own employment disputes, arbitration, and litigation end to end —running strategy and execution yourself rather than routing everything out. You will direct outside counsel where a matter warrants it, and control strategy, scope, budget, and quality.
Handle the commercial, consumer, premises, and vendor disputes a fast-growing company generates, and know when a matter genuinely needs a specialist.

The Venues

Design and remediate the practices that drive wage and hour exposure.
Serve as legal advisor to Security and Operations on guest incidents, ejection and use-of-force protocols, guard vendor contracting, premises liability, and incident documentation.
Advise on worker classification and the contingent, seasonal, and event workforce models venue and production operations depend on, including traditional labor matters as they arise.

Employment, Compensation, and Mobility

Own the policies, handbooks, and workplace procedures across every jurisdiction Cosm operates in, and build training that actually reaches hourly venue staff, not just corporate managers.
Advise on sales commission plans and executive compensation arrangements.
Maintain the employment document suite: offer letters, employment and separation agreements, contractor agreements, and restrictive covenants.
Manage immigration and global mobility with specialist counsel as Cosm expands, and serve as day-to-day counsel on hiring, discipline, accommodations, leaves, and employee relations.

Where This Role Grows
This seat has potential to grow into ownership of the compliance and ethics program — code of conduct, the reporting hotline and investigations governance, conflicts and gifts policy, third-party diligence, and enterprise-wide training.

Requirements:

Big law litigation training. Four plus years of practice, with substantial time as a litigator at a major law firm. This is the primary filter for the role.
Self-managed litigation. A record of running matters personally — pleadings, discovery, depositions, motion practice, mediation — not only supervising others who do.
California employment depth. Wage and hour, FEHA, PAGA, and Cal/OSHA, with the ability to extend that judgment to other states.
Operator’s instinct. Comfortable on a venue floor talking to general managers and hourly staff, and able to turn legal risk into guidance an operator can act on.
Preferred. In-house experience at a multi-site operating business — entertainment, hospitality, live events, retail, or similar — and any exposure to compliance and ethics program work.

This position is based near Cosm’s Los Angeles area office. Cosm values in-person collaboration, and the role requires regular presence at the LA office and at Cosm venues. Occasional travel to other Cosm locations is required.

This role is performed primarily in an office environment, requiring extended periods working at a computer and communicating by phone, video conference, and in writing. The role also requires periodic presence at Cosm venues, including active operating environments, and occasional travel. Cosm provides reasonable accommodations to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this position.

The annualized base salary range for this position in California is $140,000 to $190,000. The base salary offered will factor in internal equity and may also vary depending on the candidate's geographic region, job-related knowledge, skills, and relevant experience, among other factors.

About this role:

REP is hiring a Systems Administrator to own the technology the company runs on: our Microsoft 365 tenant, identity and access, 200+ Windows and macOS endpoints, the network across all sites, and the dozens of software platforms the business relies on daily. You'll be the primary technical resource for the organization and accountable for keeping systems up, secure, and recoverable.

The role is split between service and engineering. Service means responding to a broken laptop, a new hire first day, a down time clock on the warehouse floor, or a store associate who can't ring a sale. Engineering means deploying config and policy via tested scripts, automating identity lifecycle from our HRIS, tuning application-control and network policy, and eliminating recurring manual requests for good.

We're growing, and this is an opportunity to support our employees across our four sites in our retail stores and additional distribution centers (California, Colorado, and Pennsylvania). Support can't scale by adding headcount; we need someone who builds leverage instead.

You'll report to the Manager of IT Operations and work alongside our Systems, Web Development, and AI/Data teams, our outsourced SOC, and regional IT/network partners. This is an on-site role at our Colorado HQ, with occasional travel to distribution centers and retail locations.

Essential Functions:

Microsoft 365, Identity and Access Administration

  • Administer REP’s Microsoft 365 tenant — Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive and Teams — including tenant configuration, service health, mail flow and message hygiene, retention and data governance. Administer Entra ID as a controlled lifecycle: user and group lifecycle, role-based access, licensing, Conditional Access, MFA and password less methods, and SSO/SAML/SCIM integrations for enterprise applications. Maintain least privileged standards and run periodic access reviews.

Endpoint Management and Device Lifecycle

  • Own the complete device lifecycle for 200+ Windows and macOS endpoints plus the iPadOS and kiosk fleet: Windows Autopilot and Apple Business Manager/ADE enrollment, Intune configuration profiles and compliance policies, application packaging and deployment, driver and OS patch rings, BitLocker and File Vault encryption with key escrow, procurement, imaging, refresh, secure decommissioning, hardware standards and asset tracking, and equipment provisioning and shipping to remote employees. Deliver fleet-wide changes through tested, version-controlled scripts using staged rollout and documented rollback.

Endpoint Security, RMM, and Security Operations

  • Own the remote monitoring and management and application-control platforms (Ninja One and Threat Locker) end to end - deployment and agent health, policy creation and tuning, allowlisting and elevation request handling, remote support sessions, automated patching and script execution. Serve as primary point of contact for REP’s outsourced SOC: triage, investigate and remediate escalated alerts such as impossible travel, anomalous sign-in and unusual IP activity; coordinate containment and document findings; support endpoint protection coverage and hygiene alongside the SOC-managed Sentinel One instance. Issue third-party and API credentials only against a governed register with defined owner, scope and expiration.

Network, SASE, and Site Infrastructure

  • Own REP’s Cato Networks SASE environment - site and endpoint client deployment, firewall and security policy, SD-WAN across locations, QoS and traffic shaping, VPN and remote access, and network performance monitoring and troubleshooting. Manage on-premises infrastructure across REP facilities: wireless access points and coverage, network switching and structured cabling, printers and print management including distribution-center label printers and print/pack station technology, time clocks and scanners, and conference-room and AV technology.

DNS, Email Security, and Data Protection

  • Own DNS for the corporate domain and the website, including records and domain configuration. Manage email authentication (SPF, DKIM and DMARC), quarantine review and release, and investigation of user-reported phishing and suspicious messages. Administer backup and recovery for Microsoft 365 data - Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams - through REP’s third-party backup platform and maintain protection for on-premises creative storage; monitor coverage and job health, perform periodic restore testing, and document recovery procedures.

Automation and SaaS Platform Administration

  • Design and build automations that eliminate manual IT work, with particular focus on identity lifecycle automation driven from the Rippling HRIS - automated onboarding, role and department changes, and same-day offboarding across all connected platforms - using PowerShell, the Microsoft Graph API and native platform integrations. Serve as technical administrator for REP’s SaaS portfolio: provisioning and deprovisioning, permission structures, group and role assignment and access auditing, and maintenance of the tenant register (named administrators, break-glass access, license counts and renewal dates). Partner with business system owners such as NetSuite and Shopify who manage day-to-day platform configuration, while retaining ownership of access and identity governance.

End-User Support, Documentation and Enablement

  • Serve as the primary technical resource for the organization across tier 1 through tier 3 - from account and hardware requests to complex platform, network and security troubleshooting - for corporate, distribution center and, as stores open, retail staff. Manage the ticket queue, set response expectations and drive issues to resolution. Act as a technical point of contact with platform vendors, resellers and service providers, driving support cases, vendor on-site work, and warranty and RMA logistics. Maintain documentation of infrastructure, configurations, integrations and runbooks; contribute to IT policy, standards and business-continuity and disaster-recovery planning; and deliver security awareness, phishing simulation and user enablement.

What You Will Bring:

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

  • Microsoft 365 and Entra ID: hands-on tenant administration including Exchange Online, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams; Conditional Access, MFA and passwordless, licensing, and SSO/SAML/SCIM application integrations.
  • Endpoint management at scale: Microsoft Intune for both Windows and macOS, including Autopilot, Apple Business Manager/ADE, compliance policies, application deployment and patch management.
  • RMM and endpoint security tooling: NinjaOne or comparable RMM; application allowlisting and zero-trust endpoint control (ThreatLocker or comparable); endpoint protection / EDR.
  • Scripting and automation: PowerShell strongly preferred; Microsoft Graph API and HRIS-driven identity automation (Rippling or similar) highly valued; comfort working in version control
  • Networking and SASE: routing, switching, wireless, VLANs, firewall policy, VPN, SD-WAN and QoS; experience with a SASE platform (Cato Networks preferred) is a strong plus.
  • DNS and email security: DNS administration for production domains, SPF, DKIM and DMARC, quarantine management and phishing investigation workflows.
  • Backup and recovery: third-party backup for Microsoft 365 workloads, restore testing and documented recovery procedures.
  • SaaS administration: multi-tenant business application administration, license management, access auditing, and governance of API keys and service accounts.
  • Service management: ticketing / ITSM platforms, knowledge base and runbook authoring, and reporting on service volume, deflection and compliance.
  • Workplace and operational hardware: iPad and kiosk fleets, time clocks, barcode scanners, label and print/pack station printers, conference-room AV and point-of-sale hardware.
  • Ability to work autonomously as the primary technical resource, prioritizing across competing requests and owning issues from intake through resolution.
  • Understanding core security operations concepts, including endpoint protection, identity-based threat detection, phishing and account-compromise response, and least-privilege access.
  • Ability to read, analyze and interpret technical procedures, professional journals and governmental regulations; to write reports, business correspondence and procedure manuals; and to present information and respond to questions from managers, employees and vendors.
  • Ability to solve practical problems and deal with a variety of concrete variables in situations where only limited standardization exists, and to interpret instructions furnished in written, oral, diagram or schedule form.

Travel:

  • Occasional after-hours and weekend work for maintenance windows, site cutovers, deployments and incident response

Education and/or Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in information technology, computer science or a related field preferred; an equivalent combination of education and directly related experience is accepted in place of a degree.
  • 5–8 years of progressive systems administration or IT infrastructure experience, including at least 3 years administering a mixed Windows and macOS fleet and a Microsoft 365 / Entra ID tenant.
  • Demonstrated experience deploying configuration or scripts fleet-wide across more than one operating system, including staged rollout, testing and rollback.
  • Demonstrated experience administering an identity lifecycle end to end — provisioning, entitlement and deprovisioning you can verify across a directory and multiple SaaS platform.
  • Demonstrated ownership of production network or security infrastructure — firewall or SASE policy, DNS for a production domain, or an equivalent high-blast-radius system.
  • Experience supporting multi-site, distribution center, retail or shop-floor populations preferred.
  • Certifications preferred but not required: Microsoft MS-900, MD-102 or SC-300; Jamf, CompTIA A+, Network+ or Security+; comparable endpoint, identity or networking certifications will also be considered.

What's in it for You:

title: Biomedical Engineering Lead
description:
MANTECH seeks a motivated, career and customer-oriented Biomedical Engineering Lead to join our team. This role offers remote flexibility, with the potential for either a hybrid or fully remote arrangement depending on final operational needs, alongside periodic travel for key meetings and projects.


The Biomedical Engineering Lead will oversee modality and device inventories, acquisition workflow mapping, Application Entity (AE) title and network readiness, Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) modality worklist integration, and medical device cybersecurity alignment across enterprise healthcare settings.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead modality and imaging device inventory audits, site surveys, and acquisition workflow mapping across hospital and enterprise healthcare facilities.

  • Direct Application Entity (AE) title configuration, network readiness, DICOM Modality Worklist (MWL) integration, and edge-device connectivity workflows.

  • Coordinate modality cutover strategies in close collaboration with deployment leads, local Biomedical Engineering, and Clinical Engineering teams.

  • Manage medical device cybersecurity inputs, risk documentation, and hardening standards in alignment with federal platform security requirements.

  • Support radiology and cardiology acquisition workflows to ensure seamless clinical data flow between imaging modalities and enterprise systems.

  • Serve as the primary liaison between modality equipment vendors, service engineers, and technical infrastructure teams during system rollouts.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in technical discipline with 10+ years of healthcare IT experience, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.

  • Hands-on experience with imaging modality integration, DICOM Modality Worklists (MWL), and AE title/network configuration.

  • Experience conducting imaging device inventory assessments, site surveys, and modality cutover support across enterprise healthcare networks or regional Veterans Integrated Service Networks (VISN).

  • Technical experience developing medical device cybersecurity documentation and supporting risk mitigation protocols.

  • Operational awareness of radiology and cardiology acquisition workflows and modality vendor service frameworks.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Active Certified Clinical Engineer (CCE) certification or equivalent professional credentials.

  • Certified Biomedical Equipment Technician (CBET), Certified Radiology Equipment Specialist (CRES), or related specialized certifications.

  • Knowledge of health informatics, medical imaging architecture, or enterprise healthcare IT systems.

  • Experience supporting federal healthcare systems (e.g., Department of Veterans Affairs, Defense Health Agency), enterprise Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology Architecture (VistA) Imaging, or regional network deployments.

  • Familiarity with cloud environments (such as VA Enterprise Cloud [VAEC], AWS, or Azure) and federal healthcare cybersecurity frameworks.

Clearance Requirements:

  • U.S. Citizenship is required.

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Department of Veterans Affairs Moderate Risk Background Investigation (BI) or Public Trust clearance.

Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.

  • Needs to occasionally move about inside the office and clinical spaces to access equipment and engage with site teams.

  • Frequently communicates with co-workers, management, and government stakeholders, which may involve delivering technical briefings; must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.

title: Planner GRZ, Naarderheem, Naarden
description:
Hij gaat over. 2 keer. En nog een keer. ‘Alsjeblieft..’ hoor je de planner in jezelf denken. ‘’Met Marjon..!’’ zegt plots een stem aan de andere kant van de lijn. Je legt snel je vraag voor. ‘’Kun je vanavond werken? Dan kan ik je er donderdag vanaf halen.’’ Om de puzzel van je planning weer kloppend te maken, is het vaak geven en nemen. Marjon vindt het prima. Opgelost dus. Voor vandaag dan.

Naarderheem is gespecialiseerd in geriatrische revalidatiezorg (GRZ) in een nieuw gebouw, met nieuwe teams. Een mooie kans om direct een goed rooster neer te zetten, en de teams hierbij te helpen.

Wij zijn op zoek naar een ervaren Planner die het team, bestaande uit twee planners, voor 28 uur komt versterken.

Er bestaat geen opleiding voor dit werk. Er is geen 'trucje' dat je kunt leren. Ben je planner, dan ben je veel meer dan dat. Collega's kloppen met van alles bij me aan. Soms met problemen, of privé dingen. Behalve het vele puzzelen, is het dus vooral ook heel sociaal werk. En dat maakt het alleen maar nóg interessanter.’’

Monique van den Velden - Planner

Wat ga je doen?

Een Planner maakt de basisroosters voor de medewerkers van de zorg en facilitair op de lange termijn, maar is ook betrokken bij acute bezettingsproblemen. Je bent in staat om de uitdagende puzzel te leggen, en zo goed als mogelijk te voldoen aan alle vele wensen en eisen. Je werkt samen met collega’s van zorg en facilitair, maar hebt ook regelmatig contact met de leidinggevende. Het is een uitdagende baan, zowel op inhoud als in het contact met de verschillende disciplines. Je bent in staat om met druk om te gaan, je ziet een probleem als een kans of mogelijkheid. Als planner heb je een uniek totaaloverzicht over wat alle collega’s kunnen en willen. En mede dankzij de dashboards waarmee je werkt, kun je op voorhand adviseren over mogelijke problemen in personeelsplanning en ziekteverzuim. Tot zover het gedeelte dat je wél kunt voorzien.

Monique zei het al: er is geen ‘trucje’. Regelmatig zal je last-minute gaten in jouw vakkundig gemaakte planning moeten dichten. Goede communicatie is dan een must. Soms heb je geen blijde boodschap voor iemand. Dan moet je een ‘nee’ kunnen verkopen. Een andere keer moet je empathisch en creatief zijn om iemand uit de brand te helpen. En telkens voel je aan wat de beste manier is om er samen uit te komen. Altijd samen. Want een leuk en gezond rooster, blijft hoe dan ook het uitgangspunt.

Wat breng je mee?

  • Een MBO-4 diploma en HBO werk- en denkniveau;

  • Ervaring in een soortgelijke functie en bij voorkeur ervaring met de applicatie InPlanning.;

  • Betrouwbaarheid en mensenkennis (en -kunde);

  • Je staat stevig in je schoenen en gaat makkelijk met (nieuwe) software om;

  • Een Verklaring Omtrent het Gedrag (VOG) (dit regelen wij voor je).

Wat mag je van ons verwachten?

  • Salaris van € 2.811,51 tot € 3.864,43 per maand bij een fulltime dienstverband (CAO VVT, FWG 40);

  • Behalve vakantiegeld in het voorjaar, ontvang je ook een eindejaarsuitkering in november;

  • Mogelijkheden voor persoonlijke ontwikkeling en uitdaging, bijvoorbeeld via onze Vivium Academy.

We zijn trots op #teamvivium en dat laten we graag blijken!

Als Vivium-collega profiteer je daarom van fijne extra’s:

  • Een reiskostenvergoeding die beter is dan de CAO;

  • Korting op leuke uitstapjes en producten;

  • Belastingvoordeel op bijvoorbeeld een e-bike, fiets, elektrische scooter en laptop/tablet;

  • En ook op een fitnessabonnement en waardebonnen van , Fashioncheque en Coolblue;

En nog veel meer slimme extra’s.

Check de Vivium Voordelen, de keuze is aan jou!

Enthousiast?

Mooi: we horen graag van je! Heb je eerst nog vragen, of wil je meer informatie over deze vacature? Neem dan contact met ons op via onze Recruiters 035-6924039 of via de mail werkenbij@vivium.nl.

Ben je er al uit? Fijn: druk op de sollicitatie knop en vertel ons kort wat je als Planner bij ons wilt toevoegen.

title: Senior Analyst, Private Equity
description:

As part of a growing and dynamic investment team, the Senior Analyst, Private Equity will play a key role in all areas of the development of UPP’s Private Markets strategy and Private Equity portfolio. Reporting to the Director, Private Equity Lead, the Senior Analyst, Private Equity will be responsible in providing high-quality analytical support and expertise to the organization.

Assist in the development of UPP’s Private Markets investment strategy on an on-going basis.
Provide analysis, research, and support to all parts of the Private Markets portfolio.
Provide input on valuations, risks, and performance on ongoing private market investments that ensures UPP has up-to-date knowledge.
Participate in meetings with external investors and partners and contribute to developing a long-term pipeline of potential investments with partners.
Assist in assessing new investment opportunities and management of existing portfolio investments
Support in due diligence on potential investments, including but not limited to financial modelling, financial accounting, transaction structuring, internal and external stakeholder management, legal compliance, ESG factors and regulations.

Possessing or pursuing an MBA, CFA, CPA, CBV, CAIA or any other relevant professional designation would be an asset.
Minimum of 2-3 years of professional experience in the private markets or related industry with interest in pursuing a career in private markets
Well-developed Excel modelling capabilities considered an asset
Able to work in a multi-faceted stakeholder environment and aspire confidence in a broad range of constituencies through a proactive, respectful, and accessible communication style.

ATTRIBUTES

High degree of self-motivation and professionalism.
Ability to prioritize and manage multiple projects in a time sensitive manner.
Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and completeness
Excellent relationship building and conflict resolution skills.
Demonstrated leadership abilities.
Excellent interpersonal and verbal communication skills.
A collaborative approach to understand and respond to organizational needs and partner with various organizational and control functions.
High degree of professional ethics and integrity.
Strong commercial and strategic judgment.
Alignment with UPP’s desire to be a leader in Responsible Investing, ESG, and climate change.

title: Resident Services Officer
company: Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea
description:
As a Resident Services Officer you will provide front-line support across housing and neighbourhood services, ensuring residents receive timely, high-quality assistance through face-to-face, phone, email, and virtual channels, while upholding the Council’s values and working collaboratively with internal teams.

Working Style

In this role, you’ll be based in the Borough five days a week, playing a key front-line role in serving the local community. Whether you're supporting residents face-to-face at reception, handling tenancy queries, or coordinating essential services like mutual exchanges and Right to Buy applications, you’ll be part of a dedicated team committed to delivering responsive, respectful and high-quality support. This is a varied and people-focused role where your ability to listen, act with empathy, and work collaboratively will help ensure residents feel heard, supported and connected to the services they need.

What you'll be doing

As a Resident Services Officer, you’ll be at the heart of neighbourhood housing services, providing a welcoming and responsive first point of contact for residents. Whether face-to-face at reception, over the phone, or via email, your role is to ensure that every resident receives a high standard of service with empathy, efficiency and professionalism. You’ll support a wide range of housing management functions from mutual exchanges and tenancy visits to Right to Buy applications, ensuring that residents are guided through processes clearly and confidently.

Day-to-day, you can expect a varied workload. You’ll manage reception services, triage enquiries, coordinate estate inspections, estate parking queries and support tenancy sign-ups. You’ll also handle administrative tasks such as processing post, managing CRM queues, and preparing data for subject access or court requests. Your role will involve close collaboration with Neighbourhood Management teams, helping to monitor performance, escalate issues, and support new starters. You’ll also play a key role in maintaining estate information, managing parking queries, and ensuring compliance with safety and housing standards.

This is a role for someone who thrives in a fast-paced, resident-facing environment and is passionate about delivering services that reflect the Council’s values of respect, integrity, and community focus. You’ll be part of a team that works together to make a real difference in the lives of local residents, ensuring they feel heard, supported, and connected to the services they need.

For further information on the role, please take a look at the Job Description and Person Specification.

What you'll bring

The ideal candidate for the Resident Services Officer role will have a strong foundation in customer service and administrative support, ideally within a housing or public service environment. They should be confident working independently as well as collaboratively within a team. A proactive attitude, attention to detail, and the ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-paced setting are essential.

Key skills include excellent written and verbal communication, proficiency in using technology, and the ability to maintain confidentiality. Candidates should be approachable, adaptable to change, and capable of supporting and maintaining administrative systems. Experience in minute-taking, handling enquiries, and delivering services with empathy and professionalism is highly valued. The role also requires a commitment to the Council’s values, putting communities first, respect, integrity, and working together and an understanding of equal opportunities and inclusive service delivery.

About Us

The Neighbourhood Management team plays a vital role in delivering frontline housing services across the Royal Borough of Kensington and Chelsea. As part of Housing Management Services, the team is responsible for ensuring that residents receive high-quality, responsive support in all aspects of their tenancy and neighbourhood experience. This includes managing reception services, coordinating tenancy processes such as mutual exchanges and Right to Buy applications, and handling enquiries with empathy and efficiency. The team acts as a bridge between residents and the wider Council, ensuring that queries are triaged effectively and services are delivered in line with the Council’s values of respect, integrity, and community focus.

The importance of this service lies in its direct impact on residents’ daily lives. By maintaining clear communication, prompt service delivery, and collaborative working across departments, the team helps foster trust and satisfaction within the community. Their work supports tenancy sustainment, estate safety, and access to essential services, contributing to the overall wellbeing of residents and the smooth operation of housing across the Borough. In doing so, the team embodies the Council’s commitment to putting communities first and ensuring that every resident feels heard, respected and supported.

Interviews will be conducted in person only on the 8th October 2026

title: Senior Data Analyst – Cybersecurity GRC & Data Operations 3672722 (Jersey City, NJ)
description:

Join the cybersecurity data organization of a major global financial institution supporting enterprise governance, risk, and compliance initiatives. This team works at the intersection of cyber risk, data management, and technology, helping transform information from multiple enterprise systems into reliable data that supports security governance and decision-making. title: Psychological Eligibility Specialist
description:
Why Join EML?


An Award-Winning Celebratory Culture That Recognises You

giving you more control over your time and work life balance.

Our deep expertise, purpose‑driven work and development pathways help you build a long‑term career in a field where your skills will always be in demand. EML’s investment in AI-powered technology is designed to reduce admin, giving you more time to focus on making a real difference in people’s lives.



Make a real difference in people's lives with EML


Are you passionate about helping people get their lives back after injury or illness?
As Australia’s largest specialist in personal injury claims management, our sole focus is helping people return to work safely and confidently after a workplace incident.

The IfNSW business unit is looking for a Psychological Eligibility Specialist to join our newly established Psychological Eligibility team to support high-quality, timely decision-making on psychological injury claims within the new legislative and regulatory framework.

The Psychological Eligibility Specialists sit at the centre of our new approach to supporting psychological injury claims under the new legislative and regulatory framework implemented on 1 July 2026 and will give you the opportunity to influence decision-making standards across the Insurance for NSW Scheme.

We’re now welcoming applications for a Psychological Eligibility Specialist to join our supportive, purpose‑driven team in Sydney. This will be a Fulltime Secondment until 25 June 2027. This is deeply meaningful work where your empathy, problem‑solving and commitment have a profound impact every single day.

What You’ll Be Doing

  • Build specialised capability in early psychological injury claim assessment
  • Work closely with Case Managers to uplift their skills and confidence in applying new legislative requirements – particularly in relation to liability decision-making
  • Contribute to the way legislation is interpreted and applied, ensuring consistency across all agencies and CSPs and improving overall outcomes for the scheme
  • you will play a critical and active role in conducting early initial reviews of psychological injury claims, leading and endorsing liability decision-making within a shortened liability determination period
  • contributing to the uplift of skills and capability of our frontline teams to apply these new elements of legislation.
  • You may also work closely and engage with, relevant NSW government agencies to support shared understanding and interpretation of legislative requirements.

What We’re Looking For

  • To apply for this role you will have experience from one of the following roles: Team Leader, Technical Specialist, Technical and Injury Management Specialist, Case Manager Level 3 or 4 (NI) Senior Case Manager (IfNSW)
  • Advanced knowledge of workers’ compensation, injury management, and claims processes
  • Excellent stakeholder management, including liaising with injured workers, employers, medical professionals, and insurers
  • Confidence in providing guidance, coaching, and technical support to others

Why You’ll Love Being Part of EML


You’ll enjoy a range of benefits designed to support your wellbeing, growth and success:


  • Hybrid work options for better balance.
  • Fitness Passport providing heavily discounted access to your local gyms, pools and fitness facilities.
  • Discounts at 350+ retailers via RewardsHub plus discounts with corporate banking, super and private health insurance partners.
  • Corporate wellbeing program, including gym and health insurance discounts.
  • Comprehensive learning and development tailored to help you grow.
  • More than a traditional Employee Assistance Program, our EAP provides access to professional medical advice and safety features for our employees and their families
  • Company-wide celebration events that keep us connected.
  • Annual incentive scheme + regular salary reviews.

Ready to Make an Impact?


If you're looking for a purposeful, people‑focused career with stability, balance and a culture that celebrates you we would love to hear from you.


Apply now and help people get their lives back.

title: Marketing Data Analyst, Fandango
description:
Fandango and Rotten Tomatoes help millions of people decide what to watch — discovering movies, buying tickets, and streaming at home. The Fandango Analytics team sits at the center of those decisions. We measure how audiences discover, buy, and watch, and we turn that understanding into the choices that shape our products, our content, and how we grow. The best work on this team is the analysis that makes a decision obvious.

About the role:

We're looking for a Marketing Analyst to own the recurring, fast-turnaround analytics that keep our partnership marketing running — the reporting, data pulls, campaign validation, and promotional tracking our partners depend on. This role is built for someone who takes pride in accuracy and reliability under real deadlines, and who wants to make repetitive work disappear: a core part of your first year is using AI to automate these deliverables so the work gets faster and you spend more of your time on recommendations and highlighting opportunities.

What you'll accomplish:

  • Partners get answers fast, and they're accurate. You become the dependable owner of time-sensitive reporting, so marketing teams stop waiting and stop worrying about accuracy.
  • Repetitive work gets automated away. You use AI tools and agents to convert manual reporting, data pulls, and validation into automated workflows — and you measurably reduce the time these take.
  • Campaign performance is visible. You deliver placement, traffic, and campaign performance reporting across our sites and apps quickly enough to matter while campaigns are live.
  • Promotional programs are tracked accurately. Redemptions, costs, and partner obligations are reconciled and reliable, so nobody discovers a problem after the fact.
  • Reporting comes with signal, not just numbers. You flag what changed, what looks unusual, and where there's an opportunity — so partners know where to act.
  • Our processes get more consistent. You standardize and document recurring work so it's repeatable and doesn't depend on one person's memory.

What you'll bring:

  • 2+ years of analytics experience, ideally supporting marketing or a consumer business.
  • Strong SQL skills and real reporting discipline, with solid QA and validation habits.
  • A builder's mindset for automation — comfort applying AI tools to streamline workflows, or eagerness to learn quickly.
  • The ability to communicate findings clearly and in ways that resonate with non-technical stakeholders.
  • Proven experience with having a positive impact on roadmap and KPIs with action-oriented recommendations.

Additional Information:

  • Hybrid: This position has been designated as hybrid, generally contributing from the office a minimum of three days per week. Subject to change based on business need.
  • This position is eligible for company sponsored benefits, including medical, dental and vision insurance, 401(k), paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and a variety of other discounts and perks.
  • Salary range: $70,000 - $90,000
