title: Software Engineer
description:
Job description

As a BHS Software Engineer, you take ownership of baggage handling applications, production support, system integration and configuration for international airport installations. You work on mission-critical airport systems, solve complex operational issues and contribute to the reliability of baggage handling operations while collaborating with airport stakeholders, equipment vendors and international project teams.

At Equans, we believe that diverse talents strengthen our teams. We actively build an inclusive work environment where everyone feels welcome, can be themselves, and we encourage everyone to apply.

Your work location: Machelen.

Zoom on the job:
  • act as the primary maintenance engineer for baggage handling applications across international airport sites
  • diagnose and resolve production incidents including display issues, sorting problems, flight data discrepancies and system performance issues
  • perform root cause analysis on complex software issues related to baggage messaging, sortation control and workflow processing
  • prepare and present maintenance reports to airport stakeholders
  • collaborate with on-site technicians, airport IT teams and third-party equipment suppliers to resolve cross-system issues
  • lead the technical integration between EDAS software and third-party baggage handling systems
  • develop and maintain connectors between BHS applications and industrial equipment such as sorters, conveyors and scanners
  • configure security settings, resolve communication protocol issues and ensure reliable production data flows
  • configure and maintain baggage tracking, sortation and reconciliation systems
  • design and test high-availability and redundancy configurations
  • provide 2nd and 3rd line support across the EDAS BHS application suite
  • work with message brokers, IATA messaging standards and real-time data processing pipelines
  • work with industrial communication protocols including OPC UA and IATA 1745 BSM messaging
  • maintain sortation allocation interfaces for real-time baggage routing
  • troubleshoot workflow engines, message broker integrations and sortation logic
  • integrate systems with airline departure control systems and baggage reconciliation platforms
  • maintain technical documentation including configuration documents, integration specifications, troubleshooting guides and operational runbooks
  • document connector behaviour, deployment procedures and redundancy configurations
  • contribute to knowledge sharing and the internal knowledge base
  • identify recurring issues and implement permanent improvements
  • contribute to software stabilisation initiatives across the application portfolio
  • participate in test environment development and virtual airport test platforms
  • contribute to software refactoring activities to improve maintainability and code quality
Profile Come as you are, ideally with:
  • bachelor's or master's degree in computer science, software engineering, industrial automation or a related technical field, or equivalent professional experience
  • minimum 3 years of experience in software engineering, systems integration or technical support within an industrial, logistics, transport or 24/7 production environment
  • experience with baggage handling applications, baggage tracking, sortation and reconciliation systems
  • solid knowledge of OPC UA, IATA 1745 BSM, SITA messaging, MQTT, AMQP and system integration concepts
  • strong debugging and root cause analysis skills across application, database, network and protocol layers
  • experience with C# (.NET Framework/.NET Core), Python, PowerShell or Bash
  • knowledge of SQL Server, PostgreSQL, stored procedures, database performance tuning and data migration processes
  • experience with Windows Server and Linux (Red Hat Enterprise Linux/CentOS) administration
  • familiarity with VMware, Hyper-V, VPN, RDP, SSH and secure remote connectivity
  • experience with Git, GitLab, GitHub, CI/CD concepts, Docker, Jira and Confluence
  • understanding of network troubleshooting, firewalls, TLS/SSL and industrial network segmentation
  • knowledge of baggage handling architecture, SAC systems, BMR, airline DCS integration and IATA airport operations standards
  • able to produce clear technical documentation and communicate effectively with customers, partners and colleagues
  • organised and comfortable managing activities across multiple sites and projects
  • collaborative approach with the ability to work independently when required
  • knowledge of French (both written and spoken — valuable for communication with many airport stakeholders)
Offer What if you became BHS Software Engineer at Equans?

For you this means:

  • a market rate salary in line with your education and experience
  • interesting training and career opportunities
  • group insurance, hospitalization insurance
  • eco vouchers, meal vouchers, representation allowance, 13th month, holiday pay
  • electrical lease car, bicycle lease plan
  • smartphone with subscription, internet fee
  • additional paid leave, seniority leave, homeworking
  • discounts through Benefits@Work (culture, sports, travel, and more)

Greystar is a leading, fully integrated global real estate platform offering expertise in property management, investment management, development, and construction services in institutional-quality rental housing. title: LSS MU - Director Engineering
description:
Dematic has an immediate need for a Director of Engineering who will lead the Engineering function of the Modifications and Upgrades Business Unit for the United States. This role is part of the North America Lifecycle Solutions and Services team (commonly referred to as Aftermarket) that works to support our existing customer sites with modifications and upgrades to their systems based on our proven experience to help improve their safety, lower their costs and be more productive through all phases of the system’s lifecycle. Because of the large installed base of Dematic equipment and the breadth of solutions portfolio that Dematic designs, manufactures and/or integrates, this team delivers many projects with many different end customers from retail store distribution to food & beverage manufacturers to e-commerce. Typical projects that our team completes include updating PLC controls, rebuilding linear sorters, replacing worn components on Automated Storage and Retrieval Systems, or growing the capacity of a shuttle system by adding aisles. Work schedules are also highly variably with most onsite work happening over weekends and holidays around the clock to limit customer operational impact.

The Director leads a department of approximately 100 Mechanical and Controls, promoting a safe work environment, best in class customer satisfaction, outstanding employee experience and predictable financial results. Responsibility spans roughly $300M of business across 250+ active projects and reports to the Sr. Director of Engineering of Modification and Upgrades.

description:

Job Description

Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

Quality Assurance Specialist

Reporting to the Senior Manager Quality, the QA specialist for the Amgen Advanced Assembly and Final Product Operations facility will provide quality oversight support of the design, installation, commissioning & qualification of business software applications and automated systems. This can cover a wide range of quality processes that drive and govern operations in manufacturing, warehousing and quality assurance for the local site and the Amgen network. The QA specialist will also provide quality oversight for the manufacturing and warehouse digital operations.

This role will require local presence at the New Albany facility near Columbus, Ohio.

What you will do

Let’s do this! Let’s change the world! At Amgen, we are committed to being science-based and follow a continuous learning approach to advancing science, driving discovery and igniting innovation that works to help reduce disease. It is in this context that we endorse an inclusive and diverse workforce that helps fuel scientific innovation and problem solving, leading to better scientific solutions that benefit both patients and society.

A key aspect of this role is to apply problem solving skills to ensure quality and compliance to ALCOA++ and GMP regulations for all area operations and associated processes. You will provide Quality oversight of the development and implementation of the digital advancement opportunities for the facility and will lead the digital Quality strategy for the facility.

  • Support and represent Quality during audits and inspections; may directly interact with regulatory agencies during on-site inspections.

  • Support Lean Transformation and Operational Excellence initiatives

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The Quality professional we seek is a dynamic, flexible and driven individual with these qualifications.

Doctorate degree

OR

Master’s degree and 2 years of Quality and/or Manufacturing experience

Or

Bachelor’s degree and 4 years of Quality and/or Manufacturing experience

Or

Or

High school diploma / GED and 10 years of Quality and/or Manufacturing experience

  • Educated in a science, computer science, engineering field with 5 years of experience in GMP operations, ICHs, 21 CFR Part 11, EU Annex 11 and similarly regulated industry

  • Affinity with digital innovation, data sciences and Quality engineering

  • Computer systems validation knowledge and experience with Automated Systems, Electronic Batch Record, Electronic Quality Management System, IIOT, Digital Control Tower, Advanced Analytics. etc.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, Power Point, Project, Access, and Visio; Adobe

  • Acrobat; database related platforms; knowledge of Trackwise, PAS-X, Vault Quality Docs, SAP, LIMS etc.

  • Experience in review/approval validation documentation

  • Skilled in technical writing and critical reasoning

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, ability to work in a team matrix environment and establish relationships with partners

  • Great attention to detail and high degree of accuracy in task fulfillment and GMP documentation

  • Ability to complete tasks autonomously, providing updates to senior management, and identifying potential issues

  • Demonstrated ability in problem solving and experience in managing Root Cause Analysis / Deviation investigations

  • Experience working with dynamic cross-functional teams and demonstrate abilities in decision making

  • Strong organizational skills, including ability to follow assignments through to completion

  • Strong leadership capabilities and experience applying GMP requirements in an operational setting

  • Ability to independently interact with various levels, drives tasks to completion, and is a self-starter.

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

title: Peer Recovery Coach
description:
The Talent Acquisition department hires qualified candidates to fill positions which contribute to the overall strategic success of Howard University. Hiring staff “for fit” makes significant contributions to Howard University’s overall mission.

At Howard University, we prioritize well-being and professional growth.

Here is what we offer:

  • Health & Wellness: Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus mental health support
  • Work-Life Balance: PTO, paid holidays, flexible work arrangements
  • Financial Wellness: Competitive salary, 403(b) with company match
  • Professional Development: Ongoing training, tuition reimbursement, and career advancement paths
  • Additional Perks: Wellness programs, commuter benefits, and a vibrant company culture

Join Howard University and thrive with us!

BASIC FUNCTION:

The Peer Recovery Coach provides non-clinical services intended to aid patients in establishing recovery from a high risk of alcohol and drug use problems. The Peer Recovery Coach will work as part of the Howard University Urban Health Initiative team to provide peer support and motivation to encourage patients who are seeking treatment for alcohol or drug dependency and addiction issues. The Peer Recovery Coach will assist in completing referrals to treatment services and developing service plans to promote successful linkage to treatment services. Services will be provided at Howard University and in the community with appropriate follow-up.

SUPERVISORY ACCOUNTABILITY:

This position does not involve any supervisory responsibilities.

NATURE AND SCOPE:

Internal contacts include Research Administrative Services, the IRB, GHUCCTS/The Clinical Research Unit, and other healthcare professionals within the hospital. External contacts include sponsor representatives, community-based partner organizations, and other local healthcare professionals.

PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTABILITIES:

  • Conducts brief interventions to patients who, screen positive for alcohol and/or drug use.
  • Identifies patient’s history of drug/alcohol use, treatment history, motivation to change behavior and other needs for community support services.
  • Identifies patient’s readiness to change and uses motivational interviewing techniques and other communication skills to support a plan for reducing or eliminating harmful drug and/or alcohol use.
  • Works with program staff and case managers to identify community support services.
  • Assists patient and family with understanding how to utilize these community services.
  • Assists patients in linking to community support services and substance treatment services, including securing appointments and transportation.
  • Acts as a peer support at medication-assisted therapy appointments as appropriate to facilitate attainment of goals.
  • Provides family members with recovery support materials.
  • Provides telephone and community outreach to patients to assist with linkages and continued peer support.
  • Models coping techniques and self-help strategies.
  • Participates in trainings to continually gain new skills.
  • Attends required staff and other meetings.
  • Completes required documentation and other reports
  • Acts as a resource to other clinical team members on recovery support.
  • Consults with staff as requested, even if the patient does not screen positive.
  • Notifies case management staff before visiting the patient.
  • Telephones treatment providers to verify the patient showed up for the appointment and follows up by telephone with any patient that misses an appointment.

CORE COMPETENCIES:

  • The Peer Recovery Coach must demonstrate excellent interpersonal skills, the ability to relate to patients and health professionals, as well as an ability to develop professional working relationships with partner agencies.
  • The candidate must possess excellent listening, verbal and written communication skills, as well as good problem-solving skills.
  • The incumbent must be able to read, interpret documents and write routine reports.
  • Basic computer skills are required. In addition, the candidate must demonstrate a willingness to learn and an interest in acquiring new skills.

MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS:

High school diploma or G.E.D. is required. The candidate must be actively engaged in his/her own recovery program with a minimum of three years of demonstrated personal recovery and sustained abstinence from alcohol and/or drug use

Compliance Salary Range Disclosure

$20.00-$22.00 per hour

title: Product Owner
description:
## **About the Opportunity**

Job Type: Permanent

Application Deadline: 30 September 2026

**Job Description**

**Title** Product Owner

**Department**      AMP Platform, Research & Sustainability

**Location** Dublin

**Reports To** Associate Director, Business Analyst

**Level** 6

We are proud to have been helping our clients build better financial futures, for over 50 years. How have we achieved this? By working together - and supporting each other - all over the world. So, join our Asset Management Platform (AMP) Delivery team and feel part of something bigger.

**About your team**

AMP Delivery is responsible for the design and delivery of all changes in business process and/or technology solutions that support the growth for Fidelity’s Global Investment Solutions & Services business. We partner with Investment Management, Asset Management Operations and Distribution teams across London, Hong Kong, Tokyo, Toronto, Australia, Singapore, and China.

The Research & Sustainability team delivers strategic initiatives that enhance investment decision-making through modern research workflows, investment data platforms, sustainability capabilities, advanced analytics, and AI-powered solutions. We are increasingly leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), frontier AI models, and agentic workflows to transform how investment professionals discover insights, conduct research, and make investment decisions across Equities, Fixed Income, and Multi-Asset.

**About your role**

Fidelity is investing in several strategic programmes to transform the way investment professionals discover insights, conduct research, manage portfolios, and deliver superior client outcomes.

As a Product Owner within the Research & Sustainability team, you will shape the vision, strategy and delivery of AI-powered products that transform how investment professionals discover insights, conduct research and make investment decisions. Working closely with Portfolio Managers, Research Analysts, Sustainability teams, Architects and Engineers, you will define and deliver next-generation capabilities leveraging Generative AI, agentic workflows and advanced analytics to create measurable business value across global investment teams.

**Key Responsibilities**

In the role, you will:

- Shape and drive the roadmap and prioritisation of AI-powered products and capabilities supporting Research & Sustainability workflows.
- Partner with Portfolio Managers, Research Analysts, Sustainability teams and senior stakeholders to identify opportunities that improve investment decision-making, research productivity and workflow efficiency.
- Lead the transformation of research and sustainability workflows through Generative AI, agentic workflows, advanced analytics and modern investment data platforms.
- Define and prioritise product requirements, success metrics and business outcomes, ensuring solutions deliver measurable value, user adoption and operational efficiency.
- Collaborate with Product Managers, Architects, Engineers and Data Scientists to design and deliver scalable, secure and reusable AI-enabled solutions.
- Shape future-state operating models and drive the adoption of AI-enabled ways of working across global investment teams.
- Ensure solutions comply with enterprise architecture, data governance, regulatory requirements and Responsible AI standards.
- Assess emerging technologies, AI capabilities and external partners to support Fidelity's strategic investment technology agenda.
- Lead end-to-end business analysis across complex AI and investment change initiatives, translating business needs into target-state processes, capabilities and requirements while managing dependencies across business, data and technology teams.

**About you**

With a solid background in the analysis, design and implementation of complex investment management technology solutions, you’re the specialist we need. You bring:

- Experience delivering technology, product or transformation initiatives within Investment Management, covering Research, Sustainability and Portfolio Management.
- Proven experience leading enterprise-scale AI, digital or front-office transformation programmes, from strategy and business case through delivery, adoption and value realisation.
- Strong understanding of research, sustainability, portfolio management and investment decision-making workflows, including investment data, holdings, benchmarks and fund look-through capabilities.
- Proven experience applying Generative AI, LLMs, agentic workflows and knowledge discovery platforms to solve complex investment workflow challenges, with demonstrable business outcomes.
- Demonstrated experience leading strategic capabilities or products, including strategy development, portfolio prioritisation, investment planning, governance and value realisation.
- Good understanding of sustainability and stewardship processes, including ESG research, proxy voting, sustainable investing regulations (e.g. SFDR, SDR) and ESG reporting.
- Strong stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence senior investment, business and technology leaders across global teams.
- Knowledge of investment data providers and platforms, such as Bloomberg, FactSet, MSCI and Morningstar, as well as similar research ecosystems.
- Excellent communication, problem-solving and collaboration skills, with experience leading cross-functional teams in a global environment.
- Strong commercial acumen, with the ability to define product success measures and demonstrate business value from technology and AI investments.
- Degree-level education; CFA, FRM, CIPM or related professional qualifications would be advantageous.

You'll play a key role in shaping the next generation of investment management capabilities by combining product leadership, investment domain expertise and AI-driven innovation. Working with colleagues across multiple regions and asset classes, you'll help deliver solutions that enable better investment decisions, improve operational efficiency, and create long-term value for our clients.

**Feel rewarded**

For starters, we’ll offer you a comprehensive benefits package. We’ll value your wellbeing and support your development. And we’ll be as flexible as we can about where and when you work – finding a balance that works for all of us. It’s all part of our commitment to making you feel motivated by the work you do and happy to be part of our team.

For more about our work, our approach to dynamic working and how you could build your future here, visit careers.fidelityinternational.com.

Want to join something GREAT and make a difference?
The Department of Natural Resources (DNR) has an exciting opportunity within the Information Technology Division. DNR is looking for an experienced IT Business Analyst who enjoys working with people, solving complex problems, and improving enterprise systems that support our agency’s statewide mission. In this journey-level role, you will collaborate with business partners, project managers, and developers to analyze business processes, document requirements, design workflows, and help deliver reliable, user-focused technology solutions. Duties

  • Analyze and improve business processes and workflows.
  • Create clear BA artifacts such as functional specs, data flow diagrams, process maps, and user stories.

  • Support project managers with communication, change analysis, and issue resolution.
  • Conduct research and provide recommendations that guide project and system design.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Business Analysis, or other related field AND four (4) years of relevant Information Technology experience;

  • Experience performing the following functions:

    • Leading business analysis for IT projects.
    • Providing customer or technical support in information technology.
Required Competencies:
  • Accustomed to using traditional BA and office productivity tools at a professional level: MS Project, Excel, Word, Visio, and PowerPoint.
  • Work creatively and analytically in a problem-solving environment, demonstrating teamwork, innovation, and excellence.

  • Adapt to shifting priorities, demands, and timelines while problem-solving
  • Commitment to fostering and supporting an environment that honors diversity, equity, inclusion, and environmental justice practices.

  • Certification in Business Analysis or Project Management.

At DNR, we value diversity and inclusion and are committed to hiring the best candidate for the job. Don’t let doubts stop you from applying for this position. If you have any questions about the qualifications, please email us at DNRrecruiting@dnr.wa.gov.

title: Project Director (Power Generation)
description:
About Ameren Missouri

Ameren Missouri has been providing electric and gas service for more than 100 years, and our electric rates are among the lowest in the nation. Ameren Missouri's mission is to power the quality of life for our 1.2 million electric and 132,000 natural gas customers in central and eastern Missouri. Our service area covers 64 counties and more than 500 communities including the greater St. Louis area.

Our benefits include:

  • Medical coverage on date of hire

  • 100% employer paid cash balance pension plan

  • 401(k) with company match fully vested on date of hire

  • Long Term Incentive Plan

  • Option to enroll in Deferred Compensation

  • Minimum of 15 days paid vacation and 12 paid holidays

  • Paid parental leave and family caregiver leave

Visit our Benefits & Perks Page for more information on benefits provided to regular full-time employees. ​

About The Position

The Project Director (Power Generation) is accountable for the West Alton combined cycle power generation project, leading the owner's team and holding end-to-end responsibility for safety, quality, cost, schedule, scope, and risk performance across all three combined cycle gas turbine (CCGT) units, from early development through engineering, procurement, construction, and commissioning. This role serves as the senior project leader, with full accountability for project safety, quality, cost, schedule, scope, and risk performance. The Project Director serves as Ameren’s primary project decision-maker and executive interface, ensuring alignment among internal stakeholders, external partners, regulatory requirements, and business objectives to deliver predictable, integrated project outcomes.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Champion a strong safety culture by ensuring all work is planned and executed with safety as the highest priority, promoting compliance with company safety standards and regulatory requirements, identifying and mitigating risks, and holding self and others accountable for maintaining a safe and healthy work environment.
  • Provide overall leadership and accountability for the development and execution of the combined cycle power generation project, with full responsibility for safety, quality, cost, schedule, scope and risk performance outcomes across the project lifecycle.
  • Manage and direct project team by providing communication, coordination and follow-up to meet project goals and objectives; ensure project scope, schedule, and budget are clearly defined and understood.
  • Serve as the representative and day-to-day point of contact with the contractors (the engineer of record, the constructor, and the OEM), directing execution strategy, resolving issues, and ensuring alignment with contractual, regulatory, and company requirements. Provide oversight into the development of execution plans, project schedules, work packages and monitor production to ensure quality, timely and cost-effective project completion. Lead and coordinate cross-functional internal stakeholders (engineering, transmission, legal, tax, etc.) to deliver an integrated project solution that supports broader business objectives.
  • Own contract management and administration for the project's agreements with the engineer of record, the constructor, and the OEM, ensuring work is executed in accordance with contractual terms and that safety, quality, cost, schedule, scope, and risk performance obligations are met.
  • Monitor and analyze project cost forecasts, schedules, and risk exposure, taking proactive corrective action to address variances and protect financial and schedule commitments.
  • Establish and define the project organization, project staffing requirements, and coordinate staffing with supporting organization managers, aligning internal and external resources to meet project needs.
  • Provide oversight of change and risk management, establishing formal change control and risk processes to identify, quantify, and mitigate project risks, evaluate and approve changes, and protect the integrity of approved scope, cost, and schedule baselines.
  • Conduct regular project inspections and advise project supervision of work progress, quality of work and safety conditions requiring attention.
  • Facilitate executive-level reporting and governance, communicating project status, risks, and recommendations to senior leadership to support informed decision-making.
  • Drive continuous improvement and lessons learned across project phases to strengthen execution practices and inform future combined cycle.
  • Support regulatory filings with the Missouri Public Service Commission and other regulatory commissions.
  • Monitor project purchasing activities to ensure quality material and timely delivery at competitive costs.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree from an accredited university is required, preferably in engineering, construction management, business, or related field.

  • 10+ years of relevant experience in construction project management or execution required. Specific experience in leading large, complex, capital construction projects, team building, budgeting, forecasting, schedule management, and financial reporting preferred. Experience with CCGT or fully reimbursable power generation projects in the U.S. is preferred.

  • 5 years of progressively responsible project delivery experience is preferred, demonstrating advancement through roles of increasing scope and accountability such as cost and schedule controls, project engineering, and project management.

  • 5+ years of supervisory experience and/or high-level team/project leadership are required. Direct supervisory experience is preferred. Track record of leading multi-party owner's teams and senior contractor relationships preferred.

  • Project Management Professional (PMP) certification and/or Master's degree is preferred. Professional Engineering (PE) license in the State of Missouri is preferred.

In addition to the above qualifications, the successful candidate will demonstrate:

  • Strong competency and experience with project/construction management processes and tools required.
  • Demonstrated leadership and ability to work effectively with various stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Executive presence and stakeholder management at the board and regulator level is preferred.
  • Strong verbal, written, and presentation communication skills
  • Ability to work effectively with competing priorities and stressful situations required. An understanding of project controls, contracting, scheduling, progress measurement, risk assessment, change management, cost control and estimating process and planning. Strong command of construction in a non-lump-sum model is preferred.

Additional Information:

Ameren’s selection process includes a series of interviews and may include a leadership assessment process. Specific details will be provided to qualified candidates.

Compensation Range:

$165,100.00 - $255,900.00

At Ameren, base salary is one component of a competitive compensation package for employees. Our pay ranges are broad to allow for movement within our organization and to accommodate different skill sets and levels of expertise. We take into consideration a variety of factors including, but not limited to, skills, abilities, experience, education, credentials, and internal equity when determining the base salary offered. Roles are eligible for additional rewards including annual incentive payments based on individual and company performance. Director and above positions also include a Long-Term Incentive Plan and the option to enroll in a Deferred Compensation Plan.

title: Sr. Communication Operations Engineer
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

The role is part of the In-Space Systems business unit, which is focused on addressing two of the most compelling challenges in spaceflight today: space infrastructure and increasing mobility on-orbit.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of the Blue National Security (BNS) Business Unit, which is focused on delivering resilient, mission-critical space capabilities, including Blue Ring, to support national defense and objectives. With Blue Ring, our customers are empowered to achieve operational advantage across cislunar and Earth orbit domains, redefine mission flexibility, and pursue bold new concepts that were once beyond reach.

As a Senior Communication Operations Engineer focused on Ground Operations supporting Blue Ring spacecraft, you will be the technical authority Responsible for integration and ongoing operations of the communications interfaces between ground systems and on-orbit assets. You will own the hands-on work of communications planning and the technical integration of diverse ground networks into operations. This role requires a deep technical expert who can develop, document, and validate the critical ground operations processes that will ensure robust and reliable communication is maintained with on-orbit assets.

Join us in enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth — passion for our mission is required!

Special Mentions

  • This role requires occasional periods of shift work and on-call availability during mission-critical phases, anomaly resolution, and key customer milestones.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead the operational integration of commercial, government, and civil antenna networks, including the Deep Space Network, into the Blue Ring ground system, ensuring compatibility and readiness.
  • Establish and document the ground operations procedures, flight rules, and CONOPS required for reliable space-to-ground communications.
  • Develop and execute comprehensive communication plans for Blue Ring missions, including contact scheduling, data link budgeting, and network resource allocation.
  • Define technical requirements for the ground software alongside mission systems teams to support robust, automated ground communication operations.
  • Support and build the execution of pre-flight validation and testing for the end-to-end communication system, from the spacecraft to the ground network and maintain capabilities throughout mission life.
  • Serve as a senior technical contributor during real-time mission operations, responsible for the health and performance of the ground communications system.
  • Perform deep-dive analysis of communication system telemetry to troubleshoot anomalies, assess performance, and drive system improvements throughout on-orbit operations.
  • Collaborate with mission management to translate customer needs into actionable communication service plans and operational concepts.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in aerospace, mechanical, software engineering, or other engineering discipline.
  • 8+ years of demonstrated experience in on-orbit spacecraft mission operations or ground operations.
  • Experience with scheduling, integrating, and/or operating remote ground terminals for satellite operations.
  • Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with other engineering disciplines.
  • Experience with developing and managing ground segment requirements.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to disseminate critical technical information effectively and clearly.
  • Demonstrated technical leadership ability.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in a technical field.
  • Active or eligible for Top Secret / Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) clearance.
  • Deep technical knowledge in Space-to-Ground Communication Systems (RF, Ground Stations, Modems, Antenna Systems).
  • Experience with NASA ground operations and scheduling resources, including the Deep Space Network (DSN).
  • Familiarity with NASA standards and operations protocols.
  • Demonstrated experience building and commissioning mission-critical ground systems, processes, or operational teams from the ground up.
  • Technical knowledge in spacecraft systems engineering (avionics, propulsion, attitude control, life support systems, thermal and power control systems).
  • Proficiency in coding or scripting languages.
  • Experience with government or defense space programs and associated customer relationship management.

title: Senior Roadway Engineer / Project Manager
description:
Senior Roadway Engineer / Project Manager
Tampa, Florida
Infrastructure Consulting & Engineering, LLC (ICE) is seeking an experienced Senior Roadway Engineer / Project Manager to join our Tampa, Florida office. This position will play a key role in designing and delivering roadway and transportation projects for the Florida Department of Transportation (FDOT), local governments, and other public-sector clients throughout Florida.
The successful candidate will have a strong roadway design background, demonstrated FDOT experience, and the ability to lead projects from concept development through final Plans, Specifications, and Estimates (PS&E). This individual will manage and coordinate roadway design assignments, oversee project schedules and budgets, provide technical leadership to design staff, maintain strong client relationships, and help support the continued growth of ICE's transportation practice in Florida.
Qualifications / Requirements
Minimum required qualifications include:
  • Bachelor's degree in Civil Engineering from an accredited college or university.
  • Licensed Professional Engineer (PE) in the State of Florida.
  • Minimum of 10 years of progressive roadway/highway design experience, including preparation and delivery of PS&E packages.
  • Demonstrated FDOT roadway design experience, including familiarity with FDOT design standards, procedures, criteria, specifications, and plans preparation requirements.
  • Experience with roadway geometric design, horizontal and vertical alignments, intersections, signing and pavement markings, maintenance of traffic coordination, drainage coordination, utilities, and other disciplines associated with roadway design.
  • Proficiency in AutoCAD Civil 3D and OpenRoads Designer, along with familiarity with current FDOT CADD standards and workflows.
  • Experience reviewing engineering calculations, plans, specifications, quantities, estimates, and technical documents for accuracy, constructability, and compliance with applicable standards.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and the ability to effectively lead and work within multidisciplinary project teams.
Preferred qualifications include:
  • Experience managing FDOT roadway projects.
  • Experience delivering projects for counties, municipalities, and other transportation agencies.
  • Demonstrated project management experience involving scopes, fees, schedules, budgets, staffing, subconsultants, and client coordination.
  • Experience with alternative delivery methods, including Design-Build, where applicable.
  • Knowledge of FDOT project development, permitting, utility coordination, right-of-way, drainage, traffic, and related transportation disciplines.
  • Established relationships with FDOT and/or local government transportation professionals.
  • Experience preparing scopes of work, fee proposals, letters of interest, and other materials supporting transportation project pursuits.
Key Responsibilities
  • Serve as Project Manager and/or Roadway Design Lead for local agency transportation projects and FDOT.
  • Manage and oversee roadway design projects from initial concept through final PS&E delivery.
  • Lead the development of roadway plans, specifications, quantities, cost estimates, technical reports, and supporting design documentation.
  • Manage concurrent projects and assignments while maintaining project schedule, budget, quality, and client expectations.
  • Coordinate roadway design with drainage, structures, traffic, utilities, environmental, survey, geotechnical, right-of-way, and other project disciplines.
  • Apply FDOT or local government design criteria, manuals, standards, specifications, and CADD requirements to project development and design.
  • Review contract drawings, calculations, specifications, and estimates to confirm design accuracy, constructability, consistency, and compliance with ICE's Quality Management procedures.
  • Develop project scopes, work plans, schedules, staffing plans, and fee estimates.
  • Monitor project financial performance, budgets, schedules, invoicing, and progress toward established milestones.
  • Coordinate and manage subconsultants as necessary to meet project requirements.
  • Ensure projects are appropriately staffed and provide direction to other team engineers, designers, and technical staff.
  • Mentor and support the professional development of junior engineers and roadway design staff.
  • Maintain effective communication and strong working relationships with clients, agency staff, subconsultants, contractors, and project stakeholders.
  • Participate in client meetings, project presentations, design reviews, and field visits as required.
  • Assist with identification and pursuit of transportation opportunities, including preparation of scopes, fee proposals, technical approaches, and qualifications packages.
  • Support ICE's continued growth with FDOT and local government clients throughout Florida.
Leadership Expectations
As a senior member of the Tampa transportation team, this position will be expected to:
  • Provide technical leadership and guidance to roadway engineering and design staff.
  • Promote consistent application of ICE and FDOT design and quality standards.
  • Assist with workload planning and allocation of project resources.
  • Identify staffing needs and participate in recruitment and development of roadway personnel.
  • Foster a collaborative, professional, and team-oriented work environment.
  • Support coordination and sharing of technical resources among ICE offices as appropriate.
Physical Demands
This position predominantly involves work at a computer workstation, with occasional standing and walking. The employee may occasionally lift lightweight office supplies and materials, typically not exceeding 20 pounds.
Periodic field visits may be required. During field activities, the employee may encounter construction environments involving traffic, noise, dust, uneven terrain, changing temperatures, and other typical roadway and construction-site conditions.
Expected Hours of Work
ICE offices are generally open from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday through Friday, with an unpaid lunch hour. Work schedules may vary based on project requirements, client needs, and project deadlines. Occasional evening, nighttime, or weekend work may be required for field activities, meetings, or project delivery.
Compensation
Salary and overall compensation will be commensurate with the selected candidate's education, professional experience, technical expertise, project management background, certifications, and other qualifications. ICE strives to provide competitive compensation reflective of the candidate's experience and contributions to the organization. ICE will discuss specific compensation details during the interview and selection process.
About ICE
Infrastructure Consulting & Engineering, LLC (ICE) is a multidisciplinary transportation design and consulting firm providing engineering, planning, construction management, and related professional services to public-sector clients throughout Florida and across the United States.
ICE's transportation professionals provide expertise in roadway and highway design, bridges and structures, traffic engineering, transportation planning, drainage and hydrology, geotechnical engineering, construction engineering and inspection, and other infrastructure disciplines. Our approach combines the technical resources and capabilities of a large multidisciplinary firm with responsive, hands-on service tailored to each client and project.
ICE is committed to delivering innovative, practical transportation solutions while maintaining a strong focus on quality, client service, safety, collaboration, and employee professional development.
At ICE, we value diverse perspectives, innovative thinking, and personal initiative. Our leadership is committed to your growth and well-being, creating an environment where everyone can thrive.
Here’s what you can expect at ICE:
· Amongst the industry’s best pay and benefits.
· Professional development and clear paths for career growth.
· A collaborative, supportive team of skilled professionals.
· Opportunities to work on impactful infrastructure/Aviation projects that shape and connect communities.
· Ability to play a vital role in shaping the future of this organization.
ICE is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace and encourage qualified veterans and individuals with disabilities to apply. We do not discriminate based on any protected status in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. Applicants with disabilities or limited English proficiency may contact Human Resources for assistance at 803-822-0333 or careers@ice-eng.com. title: Secretaris van de Commissie Omgevingskwaliteit in Zeeland (32-40 uur)
description:
Jij ziet in één oogopslag wat een bouwplan sterker maakt. Als secretaris van enkele Commissies Omgevingskwaliteit (voorheen welstands- en monumentencommissie) ben jij de inhoudelijke spil tussen initiatiefnemers, ontwerpers en ambtenaren van de gemeente. Op zoek naar een vakinhoudelijke adviesfunctie met concrete impact op onze leefomgeving? Dan is dit jouw kans!

Over de functie

Je bent een ervaren (restauratie)architect, stedenbouwkundige of ruimtelijk professional met een scherp oog voor ontwerp en omgeving. Samen met je commissieleden adviseer je over de ruimtelijke kwaliteit van bouwplannen en ontwikkelingen. Als secretaris schrijf jij de adviezen die namens de commissie uitgebracht worden. Je zorgt dat de adviezen goed onderbouwd zijn, vakinhoudelijk correct en begrijpelijk. Door jouw mondelinge en schriftelijke communicatiestijl voelt de vergunning aanvrager zich gehoord en vooruitgeholpen. Met duidelijke en oplossingsgerichte adviezen draag je bij aan het snel en soepel doorlopen van het vergunningentraject. Juist in deze tijd van grote bouwopgaven in ons land is er grote behoefte aan versnelling mét kwaliteit.

Je verdiept je in de inhoudelijke beoordelingskaders waarop de commissie haar advisering baseert, zoals omgevingsvisie, beeldkwaliteit en erfgoedbeleid in de gemeenten waar je adviseert. Deze onderwerpen vormen een belangrijk onderdeel van het werk en bieden veel ruimte om je verder in het vak te ontwikkelen. Ook de verschillen tussen gemeenten, hun eigen beleid en de manier waarop ruimtelijke kwaliteit lokaal invulling krijgt, maken het werk inhoudelijk interessant.

In deze zelfstandige, inhoudelijke rol ben jij de verbindende schakel tussen een gemeentelijke adviescommissie omgevingskwaliteit en Dorp, Stad en Land. Je werkt regelmatig op locatie in de gemeenten waar jij secretaris bent en één of twee dagen per week op het kantoor van Dorp, Stad en Land in het Groothandelsgebouw in Rotterdam. Op kantoor werk je adviezen uit en bespreek je complexe casussen met je collega secretarissen. Samen houden jullie het niveau van onze advisering hoog.

Wat ga je doen?

  • Inhoudelijk adviseren: Als secretaris in een commissie verzorgd door Dorp, Stad en Land ben je mede-adviserend commissielid. Je analyseert bouwplannen en ruimtelijke vraagstukken en adviseert over de ruimtelijke kwaliteit van vergunningaanvragen. Je overlegt met architecten en opdrachtgevers en vertaalt dit naar een onderbouwd advies namens de commissie.

  • Schrijven van adviezen: Je zorgt ervoor dat de adviezen van de commissie duidelijk, oplossingsgericht en juridisch correct opgeschreven worden. De adviezen verwerk je in onze Adviesbank, het digitale systeem van Dorp, Stad en Land voor professionele en effectieve samenwerking met de bij ons aangesloten gemeenten.

  • Verbinden, samenwerken en ontwikkelingen signaleren: Je brengt verschillende belangen bij elkaar en werkt samen met collega's en externe professionals. Je volgt ontwikkelingen in architectuur, stedenbouw en erfgoed en deelt relevante inzichten.

Wie ben jij?

Je bent een inhoudelijk sterke professional die graag verder kijkt dan het ontwerp alleen. Je hebt een goed ontwikkeld ruimtelijk inzicht, bent nieuwsgierig naar wat er speelt in de leefomgeving en het effect op bewoners en gemeenschap en onderbouwt een inhoudelijk oordeel helder en overtuigend. Je bent zelfstandig, zorgvuldig en organisatiesensitief en schakelt moeiteloos tussen inhoud, proces en belangen. Je bent kritisch, maar vooral constructief: je benoemt niet alleen wanneer iets niet goed is, maar draagt ook bij aan een passende en realistische oplossing.

Verder neem je mee:

  • Wo werk- en denkniveau en enkele jaren relevante werkervaring, bijvoorbeeld als (restauratie)architect, stedenbouwkundige, landschapsarchitect of erfgoed deskundige.

  • Ervaring met het snel doorgronden van bouwtekeningen, ontwerpen en ruimtelijke vraagstukken.

  • Uitstekende mondelinge en schriftelijke uitdrukkingsvaardigheid en het vermogen om complexe informatie te vertalen naar concrete en toegankelijke adviezen.

  • Kennis van de Omgevingswet, het vergunningenproces en gemeentelijk beleid, of de bereidheid om je hierin verder te verdiepen.

  • Een goed gevoel voor bestuurlijke en maatschappelijke verhoudingen en kennis van architectuur, erfgoed en stedenbouw.

Ervaring als (uitvoerend) secretaris van een commissie omgevingskwaliteit, welstandscommissie, of monumentencommissie is een pre.

Herken je jezelf in een groot deel van dit profiel, maar twijfel je of je aan alles voldoet? Solliciteer dan toch, we gaan graag met je in gesprek.

Wat bieden wij jou?

Werken bij Dorp, Stad en Land betekent impact maken vanuit een prachtig rijksmonument: het Groothandelsgebouw, direct naast Rotterdam Centraal. Je komt terecht in een betrokken, warm en deskundig team waar ruimte is voor eigen initiatief en vakmanschap. Je zit dicht op actuele ruimtelijke ontwikkelingen, spreekt met architecten, opdrachtgevers en overheden, en ziet jouw adviezen terug in bouwplannen die onze leefomgeving daadwerkelijk vormgeven. Je werkt zelfstandig, maar staat er nooit alleen voor: je werkt samen met deskundige collega's en een breed netwerk van professionals.

Daarboven bieden we uitstekende arbeidsvoorwaarden:

  • Salaris: Wij volgen qua salarissen de cao voor architectenbureaus.

  • Pensioen: Een 100% premievrij pensioen. Wij betalen de volledige premie voor je.

  • Vakantie: Maar liefst 30 vakantiedagen bij een volledige werkweek.

  • Verder onder andere een tantième (winstuitkering) afhankelijk van ons resultaat en een volledige vergoeding van je OV-reiskosten (2e klasse).

  • Dienstverband: 32-40 uur per week.

Wie zijn wij?

Bij Dorp, Stad en Land werken we aan thema's die ertoe doen. Wij zetten ons in voor het behouden en versterken van de leefomgeving in Zuid-Holland, Zeeland en Noord-Brabant op het gebied van architectuur, erfgoed, stedenbouw en landschap. Ons vakgebied gaat uiteindelijk niet over stenen, maar over de maatschappij en alles wat daarin leeft. Een aangename leefomgeving is er namelijk voor iedereen.

Dorp, Stad en Land is sinds 1929 een onafhankelijke non-profit kennisorganisatie voor momenteel 66 gemeenten in het westen en zuiden van Nederland. Met een team van 24 vaste medewerkers en circa 65 freelance professionals zetten wij ons dagelijks in voor het maatschappelijke belang van een aangename en aantrekkelijke leefomgeving. In 2025 hebben wij 18.000 adviezen over 12.500 vergunningaanvragen uitgebracht.

Belangrijke data & procedure

  • Reageren kan tot en met: 4 oktober 2026.

  • Terugkoppeling: uiterlijk in de week van 5 oktober 2026 hoor je of je bent uitgenodigd.

  • Eerste gesprek: woensdag 14 oktober 2026.

  • Tweede gesprek: dinsdag 20 oktober 2026.

Solliciteren of meer weten?

Enthousiast? Solliciteer direct via de sollicitatiebutton en stuur ons je gerichte motivatiebrief en cv.

Heb je nog vragen over de functie? Neem gerust contact op met Irene Keur via i.keur@dorpstadenland.nl of 06-53452305.

title: Staff Software Engineer - Experience
description:
Who We Are & What We Do

At Helix, our mission is simple: to help everyone improve their lives through their DNA. Ready to make a real-world impact with your skills? At Helix, we're transforming healthcare by making genomics a standard of care. We partner with health systems and life science companies to accelerate the integration of genomic data into clinical practice. Join us in building a future where healthcare is personalized, proactive, and powered by genomics.

Your Career Path & Development

We are committed to your long-term growth. We invest in you through:
  • Cutting-Edge AI Tooling: We equip our engineers to innovate at speed. You'll have full access to GitHub Copilot, frontier models (like Claude and OpenAI), Gemini, and other new tools as they emerge, all supported by our dedicated internal AI team.
  • Continuous Learning: Sharpen your skills with full access to the entire Udemy learning database.
  • Internal Mentorship: Learn from experts across our global team through tech demos, pair programming, and collaborative projects.
  • Clear Advancement: We provide a framework for you to grow from one role to the next, with clear expectations and support from your manager.
  • Travel: Opportunities to travel to the US for collaboration with our global teams.

What is special about this role?
The Helix Experience Team builds the software platform and user experiences that guide patients and providers through their entire genetics journey, from enrollment through results delivery. As a Staff Software Engineer, you will set the technical direction for this platform and shape engineering standards across the organization.

As a Staff Software Engineer - Experience, you will:
  • Guide and define the strategic technical direction for the Experience platform and wider Engineering organization.
  • Shape how Helix Engineering utilizes AI and advance our AI development best practices.
  • Direct AI agents to automate entire engineering workflows, including codifying our prompt libraries and context frameworks.
  • Design, architect, and implement software systems for our genomic applications and services, with a focus on the patient and provider experience.
  • Drive complex, ambiguous projects from scoping to production with autonomy, owning the design, architecture and implementation strategy.
  • Collaborate and lead cross-functional work with product managers, designers, user experience researchers, scientists, and our business leaders to drive meaningful outcomes to the business.
  • Shape the engineering standards, delivery practices, and quality bars within all of Engineering.
  • Serve as a dedicated technical mentor, helping grow our next generation of technical leaders.
  • Champion durable solutions that eliminate entire categories of technical debt and raise reliability.

About you:
  • 10+ years of equivalent professional experience as a Software Engineer, with a track record of impact at scale.
  • A strong product engineering mindset, with technical decisions anchored in customer and business outcomes.
  • Operates with a high degree of autonomy, identifies problems before they're escalated and drives them to resolution proactively.
  • Experience implementing and a passion for driving AI adoption in engineering workflows, with a proven ability to build automated safeguards and evaluations that validate AI-generated code at scale.
  • Proficiency with distributed systems built on cloud infrastructure such as AWS, GCP, or Azure.
  • Deep full-stack expertise, proficient in a backend language such as Go, Java, Python, Scala, or Rust.
  • Familiarity and experience developing and maintaining SPA’s on frameworks such as React, Next.js, Vue.js or similar using TypeScript/JavaScript.
  • A track record of raising the technical standards and practices of engineers beyond your immediate team or department.
  • Adaptable in a fast-paced startup environment where priorities may change quickly and frequently.
  • Fluent in English, both written and spoken.

Pluses:
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or a related field.
  • Familiarity with regulated software systems in any industry, such as HIPAA, ISO, or FDA.
  • Experience designing and architecting event-driven architectures.
  • Experience with AWS serverless infrastructure.
  • Experience in the life sciences, healthcare, or genomics domain.

What We Offer: A Commitment to Your Success

We take care of our team with benefits that provide flexibility and support for your growth—what we call prestaciones superiores a las de la ley.
  • Competitive Compensation: A strong base salary plus an annual performance bonus.
    • Expected Helix Base: $126,417-$170,979 MXN/monthly
    • Expected Helix Discretionary Annual Bonus: 10% of your annual salary
  • Comprehensive Health: 100% employer-paid premium for our Bronze Family Health Insurance plan, with eligibility from your first day.
  • Allowances & Stipends:
    • Home Office Stipend: we will reimburse up to $500 USD for essential workspace items, so you are fully equipped to perform your best.
    • Phone Allowance: 700 MXP monthly.
    • In-Office Perks: 80 MXP daily for transport and 250 MXP daily for snacks on office days.
    • Generous Time Off: Flexible vacation policy plus all national holidays.
  • Hybrid & Remote Flexibility:
    • Hybrid: Our office is located at WeWork - Varsovia, Mexico City. We gather intentionally in our office space once per week to work on things like pair programming/live collaboration, skillshare sessions, social segments, team lunches, and volunteering opportunities. Juárez, Cuauhtémoc, CDMX.
    • Remote (for team members living 80 km or more outside Mexico City): We'll invite you to our CDMX office 3-6 times a year for key training and team meetings. These visits are a great chance to connect in person and strengthen our Helix community. Helix cover travel and accommodation.

Expected Interview Process:

1) Initial Screen 2) Technical Interviews 3)Leadership Interviews 4) Final Loop

What To Expect During Your Onboarding Week:

We want to make sure your first week is spent learning the foundations. You will be invited to live orientation sessions and spend time with your hiring manager developing your individual roadmap to success. This experience will include sessions that cover your benefits, security & privacy training, an introduction to the OKR framework used at Helix and our communication tools and norms.

What To Expect During Your First 90 days:

First 5 days: You’ll spend time learning the Helix way, completing training and onboarding for your roles, and getting introduced to your team and relevant stakeholders. You’ll also gain a deeper understanding of our customers, our products, the impact we make in the lives of our communities, and how to thrive at Helix through participation in Helix U.

Day 5 - 30: You’ll spend time contributing to projects, deeply familiarizing yourself with team and company processes, and developing a deeper understanding of Helix’s products, services and capabilities.

Day 30 - 90: You’ll build your OKRs with your manager, start to take ownership of projects and initiatives on your team, and begin to demonstrate your impact on the Helix mission.

To learn how Helix collects, uses, and protects your personal information during the recruitment process, please review our Privacy Notice.


Helix is proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and committed to providing employment opportunities regardless of race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, genetic information, marital status, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, pregnancy, childbirth and breastfeeding, age, sexual orientation, military or veteran status, or any other protected classification, in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws.

description:

Description

At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.

Northrop Grumman’s Space Sector is seeking a Flight Inspector – Level 2 or Level 3 to join our team in Promontory, UT.

Northrop Grumman Space Systems is seeking a Flight Inspector Level 2 or Level 3 to join our Receiving Inspection Team in Promontory, UT. This position sits at the front-line of our flight hardware quality gate, ensuring that all incoming material — from EEE components to complex assemblies — meets contractual, configuration, and documentation requirements before acceptance into production. If you bring disciplined inspection execution, a systems mindset, and direct experience with AS9100 or SQAR environments, we want to hear from you.

Job responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following:

  • Collect representative samples in accordance with engineering, regulatory, and laboratory requirements.

  • Verify material identification and ensure traceability during the fabrication and testing process.

  • Maintain the cleanliness and organization of tools, areas, and equipment.

  • Ensure all materials are properly labeled and stored following engineering and planning requirements.

  • Communicate any inconsistencies, deviations, or safety concerns to appropriate personnel.

  • Adhere to safety and hygiene standards, including the use of personal protective equipment (PPE).

  • Support inspections, and continuous improvement initiatives.

  • Maintain laboratory infrastructure including sample preparation and equipment set-ups and breakdown.

  • Maintain neat and accurate records to company standards.

  • Work with LIMS, Quality, and inventory databases to track material and test results.

  • Candidate will be expected to maintain a high standard of operational discipline to support clean, safe, and efficient operations.

  • Excellent time management and organizational skills.

  • Strong hands-on work ethic and can-do attitude.

  • Demonstrated attention to detail.

  • Must be disciplined to follow detailed instructions and comply to procedures.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience with SAP inspection type codes or equivalent ERP receiving/inspection module

Background in quality assurance, supplier quality, or incoming inspection in an aerospace or defense manufacturing environment

title: Multimedia Content Designer II
description:
If you’re passionate about building a better future for individuals, communities, and our country—and you’re committed to working hard to play your part in building that future—consider WGU as the next step in your career.

Driven by a mission to expand access to higher education through online, competency-based degree programs, WGU is also committed to being a great place to work for a diverse workforce of student-focused professionals. The university has pioneered a new way to learn in the 21st century, one that has received praise from academic, industry, government, and media leaders. Whatever your role, working for WGU gives you a part to play in helping students graduate, creating a better tomorrow for themselves and their families.

The salary range for this position takes into account the wide range of factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets; experience and training; licensure and certifications; and other business and organizational needs.

At WGU, it is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the range for their position, and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current range is:

Grade: Professional 308

Pay Range: $75,200.00 - $112,700.00

Job Description

The Multimedia Content Designer II will create engaging user-facing media for online and mobile delivery, including illustrations, animation, video, and audio. This individual will work as part of an agile design team to select and design appropriate digital content that’s fit for purpose, iterate on the design, and ultimately develop production-ready media for inclusion in eLearning courses and modules. The Multimedia Content Designer II must be an innovative thinker willing to deliver creative solutions with a quick turnaround time. They will work with a team versed learning experience design, front- and back-end development, and writing—together creating transformational experiences for students, faculty, and other end users.

What You'll Do:

  • Participates in cross-functional, agile design team to develop engaging, effective learning experiences.

  • Creates media in all forms; polished visual images, audio files that meet the project's objectives, animations with sophistication that shows advanced skill.

  • Consults with team/project leads, experience designers and others and ensures media are aligned with desired product goals and outcomes.

  • Can clearly describe how and why the media meets objectives, messaging, and requirements.

  • Understands the role of media in relation to learning science and applies it consistently; when is it best to use animation over stills, photography over illustration, abstract patterns versus realistic images.

  • Requests both informal and structured feedback from various sources, including team/project leads, experience designers and users, and makes adjustments accordingly.

  • Rapidly produce multiple possible approaches for usability testing, AB testing and stakeholder presentations.

  • Works with development team to ensure technical feasibility of designs; works with front-end developers to leverage the latest widely adopted HTML/CSS capabilities and SVG as appropriate.

  • Produces final media optimized for web and mobile delivery.

  • Ensures learning design and content development are completed on time and within budget and meet standards of quality.

  • Collaborates with peers to apply and drive best-practices in media production.

  • Shares knowledge with others by providing instruction, tips, templates for learning creation and editing techniques.

  • Models leadership and professionalism.

  • Develops and maintains a collaborative relationship with all appropriate internal and external stakeholders.

  • Stays current with design trends and emerging media technologies.

  • Reviews student feedback and provides recommendations for design enhancements.

  • Performs other related duties as assigned.


Knowledge, Skill and Abilities You'll Need to Be Successful:

  • Expert in design, layout, and visual communication.

  • Experience in multimedia design and production for web, mobile and/or eLearning including still graphics, animation, audio and video.

  • Understanding of HTML 5 and CSS 3 as it applies across different browsers and screen resolutions.

  • Expert-level proficiency with the Adobe Creative Suite, video and audio editing software, and other design and multimedia production tools.

  • Excellent written, oral, presentation, and interpersonal skills.

  • Ability to work collaboratively and creatively in a fast-paced, agile environment.

  • Conceptual knowledge of web/software development.

  • Strong attention to detail and a feeling of pride and ownership over the quality of our product.

  • Approaches job tasks and projects with a mindset of continuous learning and improvement, improving skills and sophistication, self-motivated to learn new skills.



What You'll Bring (Minimum Qualifications):

  • Bachelor’s degree and 2+ years of related experience (e.g., graphic design, multimedia content creation, marketing, advertising, or other relevant disciplines), or an advanced degree without experience.​

  • Portfolio or Work Samples Required: A portfolio or relevant work samples must be submitted with the application to demonstrate proficiency in multimedia content design.

Bonus Points For (Preferred Qualifications):

  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously and adapt to a fast-paced environment.

  • Experience in media production for education.

Physical Requirements:

  • Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer.

  • Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.

Visa Sponsorship:

While we welcome applicants from all backgrounds, WGU is not able to provide visa sponsorship for this role.

This position requires occasional travel of up to 20%, including required attendance at designated company summits (typically one to two per year). Additional travel may include conferences, visits to company locations, and other business-related events as needed. Additional travel may be assigned as needed to support business requirements.

Full-Time Regular Positions (classified as regular and working 40 standard weekly hours): This is a full-time, regular position (classified for 40 standard weekly hours) that is eligible for bonuses; medical, dental, vision, telehealth and mental healthcare; health savings account and flexible spending account; basic and voluntary life insurance; disability coverage; accident, critical illness and hospital indemnity supplemental coverages; legal and identity theft coverage; retirement savings plan; wellbeing program; discounted WGU tuition; and flexible paid time off for rest and relaxation with no need for accrual, flexible paid sick time with no need for accrual, 11 paid holidays, and other paid leaves, including up to 12 weeks of parental leave.

title: Quality Control Technician II
description:
The Quality Technician II is responsible for in process, formal inspections for all specific trade systems and accuracy control activities at all stages of construction. The role is responsible to ensure specifications, class rules, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and work instructions are implemented at each stage of construction. The Technician develops the Inspection and Test Plan for the specific operation, trade area or system.

Note: This position qualifies for an optional hybrid work schedule after 90 days of onsite work and onboarding. Employee will be subject to the terms of the Flexible Work Policy Agreement.

What you'll do

  • Reviews specifications, class rules, work instructions and SOPs to determine trade specific quality requirements for each contract.
  • Develops new construction and repair projects’ Inspection and Test Plans for trade specific systems. Ensures plans are implemented in accordance with contract requirements.
  • Performs daily in-process quality inspections of trade specific work. Documents and communicates results to responsible supervisors.
  • Perform accuracy control activities for new construction and repair projects at Seaspan Shipyards.
  • Produce s and sign s final inspection reports that are deliverable as objective quality evidence to the customer.
  • Performs receiving inspection of components, mechanical and electrical systems, steel, and pipe.
  • Attends formal inspections with customers and regulatory bodies. Documents all defects, nonconformities and provides results to responsible supervisors and Customer/Class as required.
  • Works with trade and area supervisors to improve in-process quality.
  • Performs gap analyses of procedures, work instructions and forms for trade specific systems. Communicates results to respective area and assists in developing and modifying procedures, work instructions and forms as required.
  • Maintains quality files for trade specific area.
  • Performs periodic audits of trade specific suppliers to ensure compliance with contract requirements.
  • Performs additional duties as assigned.

What you'll bring

  • Diploma in relevant discipline (Marine, Mechanical Naval Architect, Electrical Engineering or Geomatics /equivalent Surveying measuring background preferred) or Red Seal Trades Certificates, or CWB CSA W178.2 Level 1 Welding Inspector, or NACE Level I Paint Inspector.
  • 5-8 years’ experience in shipyards or complex manufacturing industry, or an equivalent combination of education and experience, or 5-8 years’ experience as a welding inspector of steel structure and piping fabrication, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Technical understanding of NDT techniques and their application to meet contract, regulatory and statutory requirements for trade specific systems.
  • Prior Quality/Accuracy Control or Quality Assurance experience is desirable.
  • Formal quality assurance certifications desirable.
  • Understanding of the fabrication, installation, commissioning and testing of trade specific systems.
  • Proficient in the use of Total Stations, Laser Scanning, Laser Trackers.
  • Competent in the use of Survey Software, particularly Spatial Analyzer.
  • Working knowledge of quality control and inspection procedures.
  • Ability to develop Quality Plans and Inspection and Test Plans (ITPs).
  • Technical skills including an understanding of quality techniques, their application to shipbuilding and the ability to read and interpret technical specification and drawings.
  • Ability to read material test report and understand chemical / physical requirements for steel.
  • Strong Communication skills and customer service focus.
  • Technical writing skills.
  • Advanced computer skills including MS Office Suite (Outlook/ Word/ Excel/ PowerPoint), Visio, SharePoint, AutoCAD & Rhinoceros.
  • Ability to multi-task, prioritize and problem solve.
  • Good judgment and reasoning skills.
  • Ability to work with limited direction.

Why you'll love working here

  • This is a full-time, permanent position. With multiple operations and long-term projects, Seaspan employees enjoy job stability as we look ahead to build ships for decades to come.
  • In addition to an annual bonus and pension plan matching, this role provides you with a very competitive salary in line with the successful candidate’s experience.
  • We also provide the best-in-class health and wellness benefits package for this position, including things such as extended health care (i.e. paramedical services for massage therapy, speech therapy, mental health coverage, physiotherapy, and more), dental care, vision care, life insurance, medical leave coverage, parental leave coverage, $500 personal spending account, and an Employee Family Assistance Program (EFAP).
  • Free on-site gym
  • This position qualifies for an optional hybrid work schedule.
  • Parking is included and to assist those that are using transit, we operate a complimentary shuttle bus Monday through Friday with various pick up and drop off points around North Vancouver.

#LI-CV1

title: 1026 - Full Stack Developer (React & Python) · Sr · Remote · LATAM
description:
Disclaimer – Must read: Commitment & Focus

This role requires full-time dedication, with clear priority given to Darwoft projects during the established working hours. It is not compatible with other full-time professional engagements. Any additional professional activities must be disclosed in advance and must not interfere with the responsibilities or working hours of this role.

Darwoft is a software factory delivering custom software solutions and IT staff augmentation services to international clients, primarily in the United States and Latin America. We partner with startups and scale-up companies to build high-impact digital products, combining technical excellence with a people-first culture built on long-term relationships and collaborative work.

Senior Fullstack Engineer (Frontend-Focused) — Contractor LATAM

General Information

  • Location: Remote, LATAM
