title: Director of Transportation Services
company: Alabama Institute for Deaf and Blind
description:
Candidates who are Blind or Visually Impaired and/or Deaf or Hard of Hearing are encouraged to apply for this position and may be given preference in hiring as federal laws permit. Information related to disability is not required and, if disclosed voluntarily, will be used only in AIDB’s efforts to create opportunities for individuals with exceptionalities. Non-disclosure will not subject any applicant to adverse treatment.


Position: Director of Transportation Services

Location: Talladega, Alabama

ABOUT ALABAMA INSTITUTE FOR DEAF AND BLIND (AIDB)

Alabama Institute for Deaf and Blind (AIDB) is the world’s most comprehensive education, rehabilitation, and service program serving individuals of all ages who are Deaf, Blind, DeafBlind, multidisabled, and their families. Founded in 1858, AIDB serves more than 30,000 infants, toddlers, children, adults, and senior citizens with hearing and vision loss throughout Alabama each year.

Our services span a lifetime and include five campuses in Talladega, a statewide network of regional centers, Early Intervention services, traditional and nontraditional educational opportunities in residential, day, and outreach settings, and a manufacturing facility known as Alabama Industries for the Blind (AIB), the state’s largest employer of adults who are Blind. AIDB’s three K-12 schools — Alabama School for the Blind, Alabama School for the Deaf, and Helen Keller School of Alabama — provide specialized educational services that empower students to achieve their full potential.

Our employees are among the organization’s most valuable assets and resources. We share a commitment to leveling the playing field for all. Our mission makes AIDB a unique place to work.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Alabama Institute for Deaf and Blind (AIDB) is seeking an experienced, strategic, and safety-focused Director of Transportation Services to lead, modernize, and oversee our statewide transportation network. Reporting to executive leadership, the Director is responsible for the overall administration of AIDB’s transportation system—ensuring safe, reliable, and efficient transit for students, consumers, staff, and programs across Alabama.

This critical leadership role oversees daily route operations, fleet maintenance, safety and regulatory compliance, departmental budgeting, and a dedicated team of drivers and support staff. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in educational or public fleet management, a proactive approach to risk management, and a deep commitment to supporting AIDB’s mission of serving individuals who are deaf, blind, or multi-disabled.


HOW YOU WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

As the Director of Transportation Services, your work directly connects AIDB’s students and consumers to education, independence, and opportunity every single day. By building a gold-standard safety culture, modernizing route efficiency, and maintaining a top-tier fleet, you will ensure our statewide network operates with total reliability. Your leadership will directly empower a dedicated team of drivers, give families peace of mind, and safeguard the vital transportation system that makes AIDB’s life-changing mission possible across Alabama.


BASIC QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's Degree – OR - five years of professional experience in transportation operations, pupil transportation, fleet management, safety, or logistics.
  • Valid CDL Class B with passenger and school bus endorsement
  • Clean driving record and insurable under AIDB’s carrier
  • Five years of supervisory experience
  • Must meet suitability/background requirements for employment

POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES

Operations & Strategic Planning

  • Direct daily statewide transportation services, optimizing routes, schedules, and vehicle allocation to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient transit for all programs.
  • Develop and maintain contingency plans for service disruptions, weather emergencies, breakdowns, and staffing shortages.
  • Coordinate student loading/unloading safety protocols in collaboration with school and program leadership.

Safety, Compliance & Risk Management

  • Ensure strict adherence to all federal, state, and local laws, regulations, and AIDB policies governing educational transport and commercial drivers.
  • Implement a robust safety education program for drivers, staff, and students; oversee pre-employment, random, and post-accident drug screening programs.
  • Conduct thorough investigations of accidents, incidents, and safety complaints, implementing corrective measures as needed.

Fleet Management & Maintenance

  • Administer a preventative maintenance program for all AIDB-owned vehicles to guarantee mechanical safety and extend fleet longevity.
  • Oversee vendor relationships, vehicle repairs, state inspections, fuel monitoring, and fleet replacement scheduling.

Personnel Management & Training

  • Supervise the hiring, training, assignment, and performance evaluation of all transportation staff and bus drivers.
  • Monitor and maintain current records for CDLs, driver certifications, safety qualifications, and mandatory ongoing training.

Budgetary & Financial Analysis

  • Track operational metrics, analyze cost patterns (fuel, repairs, mileage), and assist in budget planning to drive efficiency.
  • Prepare comprehensive operational reports to support organizational decision-making and continuous improvement.

Stakeholder Relations & Organizational Support

  • Serve as the primary liaison for transportation services, addressing parent, staff, and agency inquiries promptly and professionally.
  • Support AIDB’s core mission, maintaining strict confidentiality and fostering an inclusive environment tailored to individuals who are deaf, blind, or have sensory needs.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Transportation & Fleet Operations: Demonstrate knowledge of school/educational transportation systems, including routing, scheduling, fleet maintenance, and emergency response planning.
  • Regulatory Compliance & Safety: Comprehensive understanding of federal, state, and local safety standards, CDL certifications, driver qualification requirements, and drug/alcohol testing protocols.
  • Leadership & Supervision: Proven ability to recruit, train, evaluate, and mentor transportation personnel while fostering a culture of safety and accountability.
  • Financial & Data Analysis: Skilled in managing operational budgets, evaluating fleet performance data, controlling costs, and optimizing route efficiency.
  • Communication & Collaboration: Exceptional interpersonal skills to partner effectively with administrators, staff, families, and diverse community stakeholders.
  • Communication Requirement: Must obtain Sign Language Proficiency at the SURVIVAL level within 24 months of employment.


Upon offer of employment, the applicant must submit to a fingerprint background check at an agency designated and paid by AIDB. This job description describes the general nature and level of work performed by employees assigned to this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all job goals, qualifications, and responsibilities, and the employee may be required to perform other related duties as assigned.

title: Postdoctoral Fellow - Te Kura Mātauranga Pāngarau | Department of Mathematics  - 12 months fixed term
description:
Te Whiwhinga mahi | The opportunity

We’re looking for a Postdoctoral Research Fellow to join the Marsden-funded research project, “Quantifying energy dependence phenomena for rough scatterers.”

This project works lies in the pure/applied mathematics interface and aims to quantify the dependence of scattering properties on energy using semiclassical analysis. The successful candidate will work with principal investigator Melissa Tacy on the project at the University of Auckland and interact with the international associate investigators Simon Chandler-Wilde (Reading) and Julie Rowlett (Chalmers). Candidates are encouraged to contact Tacy directly to learn more about the project before applying.

This position comes with NZD10,000 travel allocation, and there are further opportunities to apply for more travel support within the department.

There is a possibility of extension of the period of employment to take up teaching roles within the Department of Mathematics.

Ngā Haepapa Matua | Key Responsibilities (not limited to):

This is an opportunity to build your research profile within a supportive and internationally connected mathematics environment. You’ll:

  • Undertake high-quality research in mathematics, with a focus on analysis.
  • Develop and contribute to research outputs, including publications in reputable journals and conference proceedings.
  • Contribute to the wider research environment through activities such as seminars, events, peer review and academic service.
  • Develop your own research portfolio, with the potential to attract future external funding and postgraduate students.
  • Contribute to teaching activities, which may include lectures, tutorials, seminars, teaching coordination, assessment and co-supervision of students.

You’ll work closely with Melissa Tacy on the project and have opportunities to engage with researchers internationally.

For more detailed information, review this position description

This is a full-time (40 hrs per week) 12-month fixed-term role

The remuneration is $92,213 per annum

He kōrero mōu | About you

We’re looking for someone who has:

  • Completed, or is very close to completing, a PhD in Mathematics with a research focus in analysis, with your thesis examined before the fellowship start date.
  • Research experience in analysis.
  • The ability to work independently and contribute positively to a collaborative research environment.

Experience in one or more of the following would be advantageous:

  • Semiclassical analysis
  • Numerical analysis
  • Spectral theory
  • Theory of partial differential equations (PDEs)

This opportunity is open to researchers within 0–5 years of PhD award, allowing for career breaks.

Ngā āhuatanga kei a mātou | What we offer

The University of Auckland is New Zealand's leading University and maintains significant computational, laboratory, and analytic facilities. Auckland is frequently rated as one of the world's most liveable cities.

The University is committed to providing an excellent working environment through the following:

  • Flexible employment practices (including working from home and flexible hours)
  • Up to 6.75% company superannuation scheme
  • A competitive salary with five weeks' annual leave
  • Opportunity for Research and Study Leave

In addition, we also offer career development programs, discounted car parking, a generous parental leave allowance, childcare, and other discounts on internal and external services.

For more information, please visit Staff Benefits.

Me pēhea te tuku tono | How to apply

Applications must be submitted online by the closing date of 16th October 2026 to be considered.

The application must include:

  • Cover Letter and CV, including a list of publications and preprints, a summary of teaching and service contributions, and the names of some people who can provide academic references.

Please reach out to Melissa Tacy (Senior Lecturer - Mathematics) via melissa.tacy@auckland.ac.nz for a confidential conversation. Please note we are happy to answer your questions, but we do not accept applications by email.

Applications are strongly encouraged from under-represented groups, such as women, Māori, and Pacific mathematicians.

title: Commercial Marketplace Strategy and Operations Intern (Summer 2027)
description:
About Zipline

Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products.

Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations.

Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe.

We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds.

About the Commercial Marketplace Team

The Commercial Marketplace team runs the operating system that connects site-level conditions to commercial action. We track marketplace health across each site, cohort, and metro, balancing demand, selection, customer experience, capacity, utilization, and profitability. By partnering with Product, Operations, Marketing, Finance, and Sales, we identify the right levers - such as prioritization, promotions, pricing, and demand shaping - and help turn them into scalable programs. Our work helps Zipline grow healthy marketplaces while protecting service quality and making the best use of scarce operational and commercial resources. What makes the team special is its combination of quantitative analysis, marketplace judgment, and hands-on execution.

The Role

As a Commercial Marketplace Strategy & Operations Intern, you will help answer questions like what is happening at a site, which sites are best suited for a given growth program, and where capacity or customer experience constraints may limit growth. You’ll use data to prepare readouts, surface opportunities, test hypotheses, and support decisions across Commercial, Operations, Marketing, Product, Finance, and Utilization. You will learn how marketplace levers such as selection, partner prioritization, pricing, promotions, and demand shaping work together in a real delivery network. Your analyses will inform decisions that improve marketplace health, help scale what works, and expand reliable access to goods.

What You'll Do

  • Evaluate and build the playbook for marketplace levers such as pricing, promotions, partner prioritization, pricing, promotions, budget allocation, demand shaping, and customer-experience protection.
  • Analyze site and cohort performance to identify where to prioritize sales resources, marketing actions, product rollouts, operational playbooks, or other growth programs.
  • Build and maintain recurring reports and dashboards, partnering with Analytics as needed to improve visibility into site, cohort, and metro performance.
  • Support daily and weekly site-level performance readouts across marketplace health, growth, efficiency, utilization, fulfillment, customer outcomes, and profitability.
  • Monitor aircraft availability, fulfillment throughput, throttling, and operational constraints; surface risks that could affect growth plans or customer experience.
  • Partner with Commercial, Operations, Marketing, Product, Finance, and Utilization to turn insights into action, measure results, and scale what works.

What You'll Bring

  • Currently enrolled in a master’s degree program.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with experience using spreadsheets or similar tools to organize, analyze, and communicate data.
  • Ability to investigate performance at different levels of detail - from a single site to a cohort or metro - and turn findings into a clear recommendation.
  • Clear, concise written and verbal communication skills, including comfort presenting findings to cross-functional partners.
  • A collaborative, self-directed working style and curiosity about marketplaces, logistics, and how technology can improve access to goods.
  • Able to work full-time onsite in South San Francisco for the duration of the Summer 2027 internship.

What Else You Should Know

This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). Zipline is unable to sponsor work visas for applicants to this position.

The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements.

Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period.

Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities.

Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process.

Voluntary Self-Identification

For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file.

As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

title: Databricks Administrator
description:
Are you ready to join a growing team that puts a premium on productivity and has an award-winning culture centered around transforming talented employees into effective business leaders? Then BHG Financial is the place for you.

With healthcare in our heritage, we soon expanded  to serve high-earning professionals in many  other industries, providing all with leading-edge financial solutions, including our extensive network of community banks.
 
Today, BHG Financial has firmly established  its legacy as a leader in the financial services space. Therefore, it is essential to factor those in when making responsible lending decisions. Our continued focus on data, analytics, and proprietary modeling has enabled faster funding for our customers.  
 
From business to personal loans to relationships with community banks, the country’s top professionals and business owners rely on us for our exceptional financial solutions and concierge service to continue their success and legacy.

What You'll Do
Configure, maintain, and administer Azure Databricks workspaces and clusters across development, staging, and production environments. 
Monitor cluster health, performance metrics, resource utilization, and platform availability. 
Optimize cluster, SQL warehouse, and workspace configurations for performance and cost efficiency. 
Manage workspace governance, including job scheduling, notebook organization, audit logging, and operational standards. 
Administer user access, workspace permissions, SQL warehouse configurations, and group-based security controls. 
Troubleshoot infrastructure issues, performance bottlenecks, connectivity problems, and workload failures. 
Support disaster recovery and high-availability planning, validation, and operational readiness for Databricks workloads. 
Collaborate with data engineering teams to establish Databricks usage standards, support workload reliability, troubleshoot platform issues, optimize Delta Lake performance, and promote governed platform adoption. 
Administer and enforce security policies, RBAC, encryption standards, and access controls. 
Maintain documentation and runbooks for operational procedures. 
Support capacity planning, cost optimization, and platform improvement initiatives. 

Security Governance 

Maintain security governance standards for Azure Databricks in a financial services environment, including RBAC, least-privilege access, privileged access controls, and group-based permissions. 
Administer Unity Catalog permissions, metastore access, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, and external locations to enforce governed data access. 
Manage workspace permissions, admin roles, service principals, groups, SCIM provisioning, and Microsoft Entra ID integration to support secure identity governance. 
Configure and review compute policies, cluster permissions, instance pool access, SQL warehouse permissions, and job ownership to reduce unnecessary privilege and control platform usage. 
Oversee secrets management, token usage, storage credential access, and Key Vault-backed configurations to protect sensitive financial, customer, and operational data. 
Coordinate recurring access reviews, access certification, and timely remediation of excessive, inappropriate, or outdated permissions to support internal control requirements. 
Review Databricks audit logs, security events, access changes, and control findings to identify risks, policy exceptions, segregation-of-duties concerns, and required remediation actions. 
Support audit and regulatory readiness by maintaining evidence for access controls, configuration standards, policy enforcement, operational procedures, and change management activities. 
Partner with cybersecurity, compliance, risk, infrastructure, and data governance teams to align Databricks controls with financial services security, privacy, and compliance expectations.

What You'll Need
5+ years of experience administering cloud-based data platforms or analytics environments, with a focus on operational support, governance, and reliability. 
3+ years of hands-on experience administering Azure Databricks workspaces, Unity Catalog, clusters, jobs, SQL warehouses, and platform settings. 
Strong experience managing Databricks users, groups, workspace permissions, admin roles, service principals, SCIM provisioning, and Microsoft Entra ID integration. 
Experience administering Unity Catalog, including metastores, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, permissions, storage credentials, and external locations. 
Ability to configure and maintain compute policies, cluster permissions, instance pools, SQL warehouses, job ownership, and platform usage controls. 
Experience monitoring Databricks platform health, cluster performance, job execution, workload failures, audit logs, and resource utilization. 
Strong troubleshooting skills for Databricks platform issues, Spark workloads, connectivity problems, permission errors, and performance bottlenecks. 
Working knowledge of Python, SQL, PowerShell, Databricks CLI, REST APIs, and automation practices used to support platform administration. 
Experience supporting operational controls, access reviews, audit evidence, change management, runbooks, and platform documentation. 
Knowledge of Databricks security governance, RBAC, least privilege, encryption, secrets management, audit readiness, and secure data access patterns. 
Understanding of Azure networking and security concepts, including private endpoints, firewalls, network security groups, storage access, Key Vault, and secure connectivity. 
Experience partnering with data engineering teams to support reliable pipelines, workload troubleshooting, performance tuning, platform standards, and secure Databricks operations.
Travel requirement: All roles require travel during the first 6 months of employment to attend the BHG Oars in Experience. After the initial 6 months, ongoing travel is expected at approximately ~5% annually for periodic team on-sites, team meetings, and cross-functional collaboration.
Work Authorization: This role is not eligible for employer-provided immigration sponsorship. To be considered, applicants must already possess valid U.S. work authorization that will not require sponsorship now or in the future.

Technical Skills & Technologies 

Databricks Platform Administration: Workspaces, workspace settings, admin console, clusters, jobs, notebooks, SQL warehouses, instance pools, compute policies, and audit logs. 
Unity Catalog Administration: Metastores, catalogs, schemas, tables, volumes, permissions, storage credentials, external locations, and governed data access. 
Identity and Access Management: Users, groups, service principals, workspace permissions, admin roles, RBAC, SCIM provisioning, Microsoft Entra ID integration, and least-privilege access controls. 
Security and Governance: Secrets management, token usage, encryption, Key Vault-backed configurations, access reviews, audit evidence, policy enforcement, and regulatory readiness. 
Monitoring and Troubleshooting: Cluster health, job failures, SQL warehouse performance, Spark workload issues, audit log review, resource utilization, connectivity issues, and performance bottlenecks. 
Automation and Administration Tools: Databricks CLI, REST APIs, Terraform awareness, Python, PowerShell, SQL, runbooks, operational scripts, and platform documentation. 
Azure Platform Integration: Azure Storage, Key Vault, private endpoints, virtual networks, firewalls, network security groups, Azure Monitor, Log Analytics, and secure connectivity patterns. 

Preferred Qualifications 

Databricks Platform Administrator certification or equivalent hands-on Azure Databricks administration experience. 
Experience administering Unity Catalog, workspace security, compute policies, SQL warehouses, service principals, audit logs, and platform governance controls. 
Experience supporting Databricks in financial services or another regulated environment with strong audit, access review, and compliance requirements. 
Experience creating runbooks, operational standards, monitoring procedures, access review processes, and administrator documentation for Databricks environments. 
Background in database administration, cloud platform administration, or data platform operations supporting enterprise analytics workloads.

title: Platform Authorization Lead
description:
MANTECH seeks a motivated, career and customer-oriented Platform Authorization Lead to join our team. This role offers remote flexibility, with the potential for either a hybrid or fully remote arrangement depending on final operational needs, alongside periodic travel for key meetings and projects.


The Platform & Authorization Lead in Healthcare IT coordinates with operational leadership on release, change, monitoring, patching, vulnerability remediation, and operational evidence. In this role, you will own the program's hosting posture, VA Enterprise Cloud (VAEC) and Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP) alignment, Authority to Operate (ATO) strategy, disaster recovery, high availability, and security control implementation across cloud boundaries.


Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Lead the cloud hosting posture, driving alignment with VAEC, FedRAMP, and High-baseline ATO security requirements.

  • Design and implement Software as a Service (SaaS) boundary architectures, control inheritance frameworks, Disaster Recovery (DR), and High Availability (HA) patterns to ensure infrastructure resilience.

  • Develop, maintain, and manage Risk Management Framework (RMF) Body of Evidence (BOE) packages and security authorization documentation.

  • Translate complex federal security and authorization mandates into operational, deployable workflows and platform architectures.

  • Coordinate daily with release, change, and operations teams to oversee continuous monitoring, patching, vulnerability remediation, and operational compliance evidence.

  • Collaborate with government security stakeholders and accreditation authorities to guide system architecture through formal assessment and authorization cycles.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in technical discipline with 10+ years of healthcare IT experience, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience.

  • Active Certified Information Systems Security Professional (CISSP) certification or equivalent senior cybersecurity credentials.

  • Experience managing RMF BOE packages for VAEC, FedRAMP, or equivalent High-baseline ATO systems.

  • Technical expertise in designing resilient cloud architectures, including DR/HA strategies, control inheritance, and security boundary definitions.

  • Fluency translating federal security controls and authorization standards into operational infrastructure implementations.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience securing and authorizing clinical SaaS solutions, hosted enterprise healthcare IT platforms, or sensitive federal environments.

  • Master's degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, or Computer Engineering.

  • Knowledge of Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) security policies and VAEC cloud architecture patterns.

  • Experience with automated compliance scanning, continuous monitoring tools, and security remediation platforms.

Clearance Requirements:

  • U.S. Citizenship is required.

  • Must be able to obtain and maintain a Department of Veterans Affairs Moderate Risk Background Investigation (BI) or Public Trust clearance.

Physical Requirements:

  • Must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time.

  • Needs to occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, and engage with team members.

  • Frequently communicates with co-workers, management, and government stakeholders, which may involve delivering technical security presentations; must be able to exchange accurate information in these situations.

location: Central - United States; West Coast - United States
description:
GAQ227R127

Databricks is seeking an experienced, highly strategic leader to serve as Director of Order to Revenue Compliance. As Databricks continues to scale, protecting our usage-based revenue engine requires dedicated fiduciary oversight at the intersection of product metering, billing systems, and financial accounting. In this key player/coach leadership role, you will lead a specialized team bridging the gap between raw product metering and financial ground truth. You will oversee usage execution, establish product launch controls, direct partner royalty reconciliations, oversee compliance with partnership arrangements, and serve as the primary compliance lead for usage-related SOX controls and audits.

Primary Responsibilities

  • Strategic Team Leadership: Lead, coach, and scale a high-performing team consisting of two functional leads covering Partnerships / Royalty, Money/Engineering Compliance, and Issue Resolution. Actively uphold our culture principles and leadership essentials in daily execution.
  • Usage & Revenue Fiduciary Oversight: Serve as the primary business and compliance oversight body responsible for ensuring all usage-related, financially impacting processes are accurate, complete, SOX-compliant, and validated prior to customer billing and revenue conversion.
  • Partner Agreement & Royalty Governance: Assume complete ownership of outbound/inbound royalty reporting, executions, and complex reconciliations (e.g., Azure/Microsoft, AWS, GCP, SAP). Eliminate manual operational risks, ingestion lag, timing mismatches, and contract-period attribution issues.
  • Cross-Functional System Controls & "Two-in-the-Box" Execution: Partner closely with Engineering (Money Team) and Finance Data Systems (FDS) prior to product launches to validate metering, pricing models, SKU additions, and billing logic against business intent.
  • Audit Ownership & Technical Accounting: Act as the primary audit lead for external audit, internal audit, and executive stakeholders regarding platform consumption calculations and monetization structures.
  • Remediation & Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Oversee the categorization and resolution of usage issues (Types 1–3), standardize refund SLAs/credits, and drive mandatory cross-functional RCAs with Engineering to prevent systemic metering bugs.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Education & Certification: Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related technical field; CPA license preferred.
  • Experience: 12+ years of relevant experience, including extensive experience in revenue accounting, IT audit, and SOX control frameworks.
  • Domain Expertise: Familiarity with ASC 606, specifically applied to consumption-based/usage-based revenue models, SaaS, and complex partner royalty agreements.
  • Leadership & Cross-Functional Influence: Proven track record of managing managers or functional leads while directly collaborating with executive leadership across Engineering, Sales Operations, FP&A, and external auditors.
  • Technical & Analytical Acumen: Ability to bridge technical systems (product metering engines, SQL/data pipelines, sub-ledgers) with accounting rules and complex contract terms.

title: Senior Manager – KinetiX Hardware Engineering
description:
Role Overview

The Senior Manager, KinetiX Hardware Engineering, is a hands-on technical leader responsible for both leading and actively contributing to the development of the KinetiX inspection system hardware. This role leads a multi-disciplinary hardware engineering team, including electronics, mechanical, and optical engineering, while also serving as a technical project leader coordinating execution with software engineering, manufacturing, and production teams.

This position combines people leadership, system-level technical ownership, and day-to-day engineering involvement. The Senior Manager remains close to the design work, architecture decisions, and technical tradeoffs while ensuring disciplined execution across hardware, software, and production interfaces.

Key Responsibilities

Hands-On Multi-Disciplinary Technical Leadership

  • Lead and integrate electronics, mechanical, and optical engineering disciplines into cohesive hardware solutions.
  • Actively contribute to system architecture, design reviews, and key technical decisions across hardware subsystems.
  • Drive integration of sensors, optics, electronics, mechanics, and enclosures into complete inspection systems.
  • Serve as the primary technical escalation point for complex cross-disciplinary and system-level issues.
  • Own the hardware organization budget, including planning, forecasting, cost control, and investment prioritization to support strategic and operational goals

Technical Project Management & Coordination

  • Provide technical project leadership for hardware development efforts, working closely with software and production teams.
  • Lead and coordinate product certification and manage the process to maintain updated documentation for applicable certifications, including CE and other applicable certifications.
  • Coordinate hardware/software integration milestones, dependencies, and readiness for production.
  • Partner with program and project managers to ensure technical execution aligns with schedule, cost, and quality goals.
  • Support bid, tender, and product definition activities by assessing technical feasibility, risks, and resource needs.

People & Team Leadership

  • Lead, mentor, and develop engineers across electronics, mechanical, and optical disciplines.
  • Balance hands-on technical contribution with coaching and delegation to grow team capability.
  • Set clear technical priorities, execution expectations, and accountability.
  • Build and maintain a strong engineering culture focused on ownership, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Product Development & Lifecycle Ownership

  • Drive hardware development from concept through production and sustaining.
  • Own hardware Bills of Materials (BOMs), approved configurations, and option structures.
  • Govern engineering change control across hardware disciplines and lifecycle phases.
  • Lead root-cause analysis and corrective actions for hardware issues found in production or the field.

Manufacturing & Production Interface

  • Work closely with manufacturing, supply chain, and quality teams to ensure design for manufacturability (DFM) and design for serviceability (DFS).
  • Support production readiness, first builds, and issue resolution during ramp-up.
  • Ensure hardware designs are robust, repeatable, and scalable for global production.

Quality, Risk & Continuous Improvement

  • Establish and track hardware quality, reliability, and delivery metrics.
  • Identify technical risks early and drive mitigation plans.
  • Standardize designs, documentation, and engineering processes to reduce complexity and customization.
  • Champion lessons learned and continuous improvement across hardware development.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Civil, Electrical, or Industrial Engineering (or related field).
  • 8+ years of experience in hardware or systems engineering.
  • 3+ years of experience leading multi‑discipline engineering teams.
  • Strong hands‑on background in electro‑mechanical and/or optical systems.
  • Experience coordinating hardware development with software and manufacturing teams.
  • Experience with BOM ownership, configuration management, and engineering change control.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to lead without losing technical depth.
  • Project management training or experience

Preferred Skills

  • Experience in machine vision, optics, sensing systems, or industrial inspection platforms.
  • Prior role combining technical leadership and project execution responsibilities.
  • Experience supporting production ramp-up and sustaining engineering.
  • Systems-level thinker comfortable working across hardware and software boundaries.

Performance Metrics

  • Hardware quality, reliability, and field performance.
  • On-time delivery of hardware engineering milestones.
  • Effectiveness of hardware/software/production coordination.
  • Reduction in late-stage design changes and rework.
  • Team capability growth, engagement, and retention.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of the Lunar Permanence business unit, which develops Blue Origin’s Blue Moon landers and related products. To further Blue Origin's mission of millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth, we are building sustainable infrastructure for our transport of crew and cargo from Earth to the lunar surface.

As a Test Engineer working with a hardworking team of specialists, technicians, and engineers, you'll help design, build, and commission electrical test equipment to test fluid components for our lunar lander program, Blue Moon - . You will design/configure data acquisition systems and/or control systems specifically focused for testing space-grade fluids and thermal components. You will support the Lunar Permanence Core Components Test team through development, acceptance, and qualification testing of flight hardware for the space vehicles.

This is a hands-on position where you will apply broad multi-disciplinary engineering (electrical/electronic, fluids, thermal, mechanical) knowledge, skills, and methods to positively impact safe human spaceflight. This position will be part of the core factory startup and onboarding team responsible for building the operations and manufacturing staff, fitting out the building, and creating the process flow/work instructions/etc. from the ground up. You will help ensure the successful launch of a world-class manufacturing operation by verifying the quality of incoming materials and supplier-provided components. Through inspections, documentation review, and supplier quality support activities, you will help prevent defects, improve supplier performance, and protect product quality throughout the manufacturing process.

What will you do?

  • Perform incoming inspections of raw materials, purchased components, and supplier-provided assemblies.

  • Inspect electrical and electromechanical components, including wiring harnesses, electrical panels, enclosures, and assembled parts.

  • Verify compliance to engineering drawings, specifications, inspection plans, and quality requirements.

  • Review supplier documentation, including Certificates of Conformance (CoC), test reports, inspection reports, and traceability records.

  • Support supplier corrective action activities and root cause investigations.

  • Maintain inspection records, sampling plans, and quality documentation.

  • Support development of inspection procedures, work instructions, and quality processes in a startup manufacturing environment.

  • Provide quality support for production activities during second shift.

  • Ensure compliance with all safety, quality, and regulatory requirements.

How will you get here?

Education

  • High School Diploma or GED required.

  • Associate degree or technical certification in Quality, Manufacturing, Engineering Technology, Electronics, or a related field preferred.

Experience

  • 2+ years of experience in Quality Inspection, Quality Assurance, Supplier Quality, or Quality Control within a manufacturing environment.

  • Experience performing incoming inspection activities and material acceptance decisions.

  • Experience supporting electrical, electronic, electro-mechanical, or industrial manufacturing processes preferred.

  • Experience with SAP QM, SAP MM, or related ERP systems preferred.

  • Experience working with large form-factor manufacturing, industrial equipment, electrical assemblies, power systems, heavy equipment, or complex assemblies is highly preferred.

  • Experience supporting startup manufacturing operations is a plus.

Knowledge, Skills, Abilities

  • Strong blueprint reading and technical drawing interpretation skills.

  • Working knowledge of GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing).

  • Proficiency using inspection and metrology equipment including calipers, micrometers, gauges, and precision measurement tools.

  • Experience with MRB processes, nonconforming material control, and material disposition activities.

  • Familiarity with quality management systems such as ISO 9001.

  • Experience with root cause analysis, corrective actions, and 8D problem-solving methodologies.

  • Strong attention to detail and ability to identify defects and quality concerns.

  • Strong organizational, analytical, and problem-solving skills.

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced manufacturing environment.

  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and quality documentation systems.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience inspecting electrical assemblies, wiring harnesses, panel assemblies, enclosures, medium-voltage systems, low-voltage systems, or high-power electronic assemblies.

  • Experience operating coordinate measuring machines (CMM) or other advanced metrology equipment.

  • Knowledge of supplier quality processes, supplier audits, and supplier performance improvement activities.

  • Experience supporting quality systems and process development in a startup or greenfield manufacturing environment.

title: Senior Cyber Threat Analyst
description:
MANTECH seeks a motivated, career and customer-oriented Senior Cyber Threat Analyst to join our team in Denver, CO.

Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

  • Conducting proactive threat hunts to uncover previously undetected adversary behavior, performing in-depth host and network log analysis, and delivering systematic threat assessments
  • Managing cyber intelligence requirements and focusing cyber intelligence collection efforts; identifying emerging cyber technologies, capabilities, or weapons which pose a threat to US or Allied systems
  • Producing comprehensive cybersecurity reports, providing sourced and summarized threat intelligence, outlining threat hunt findings and limitations, and presenting recommendations to system owners, cyber defenders, and policy makers
  • Researching known adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures (TTPs) to identify foundational components, isolate associated host or network events, and enable threat mitigation, detection, and response
  • Creating custom cybersecurity dashboards to monitor host and network activity, enabling rapid identification of successful and unsuccessful intrusion attempts
  • Performing analysis, correlation, and attribution of incidents to Advanced Persistent Threat (APT) groups
  • Conducting research and analysis of APT infrastructure and malicious binaries, external cyber threat intelligence reporting, and production

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree or 4+ additional years of cyber experience in lieu of a degree
  • 5+ years of cybersecurity experience
  • IAT Level II certification (GSEC, Security+, SSCP, or CCNA-Security)
  • Experience with related security technology or disciplines such as Incidents and Warnings Management, Cybersecurity Operations, or Cybersecurity Engineering
  • Demonstrated experience conducting proactive threat hunts across host, network, endpoint, and security telemetry.
  • Experience analyzing system, network, endpoint, and security logs to identify anomalous activity, Indicators of Compromise (IOCs), and adversary behavior.
  • Experience conducting cyber threat intelligence analysis, including assessing adversary capabilities, intent, infrastructure, and potential impact.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Familiarity with SIEM and security analytics platforms such as Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, Elastic, or similar technologies.
  • Experience using threat intelligence frameworks, standards, and methodologies such as MITRE ATT&CK, Cyber Kill Chain or related frameworks.
  • Experience creating custom detection signatures, analytic rules, correlation logic, or threat-hunting queries.
  • Experience developing custom cybersecurity dashboards and visualizations to monitor host, network, and security activity.

Clearance Requirements:

  • Must have an active TS/SCI w/Polygraph

Physical Requirements:

  • The person in this position must be able to remain in a stationary position 50% of the time. Occasionally move about inside the office to access file cabinets, office machinery, or to communicate with co-workers, management, and customers, via email, phone, and or virtual communication, which may involve delivering presentations.

title: Software Development Engineer in Test

You will work closely with software engineers, product owners, architects, and subject matter experts to understand product functionality, design effective test strategies, and build robust automation frameworks. This role offers an exciting opportunity to work on complex, high-volume distributed systems while contributing to automation, quality engineering, and continuous delivery practices.

System & Domain Expertise: Gain deep knowledge of product requirements, architecture, code flows, and Asset Management/Post-Trade processing to inform development and quality processes.

Collaboration & Design Input: Participate in design discussions, contribute to Agile ceremonies (sprints, planning, retrospectives), and provide recommendations on testability and quality improvements across the lifecycle.

Infrastructure & Cross-Functional Teamwork: Collaborate with development, infrastructure, and release teams to ensure continuous product quality.

Process, Research & Leadership: Research modern testing methodologies, maintain accurate documentation and status reporting, and assist with technical interviews and hiring.

What we’re looking for:

Education, Core QA & Agile Skills: Bachelor’s degree in CS, Engineering, or IT with 2-5 years of SDET/QA experience, emphasizing expertise in software testing methodologies, API performance testing using JMeter, QA best practices, database testing, SQL, and data validation, supported by excellent analytical, problem-solving, and stakeholder collaboration skills in Agile/Scrum environments.

Automation Tech Stack: Demonstrates hands-on proficiency in building scalable automation solutions using Java or Python, Playwright, JavaScript, and BDD frameworks, coupled with the ability to effectively troubleshoot complex distributed applications.

GenAI & AI Ecosystem Proficiency: Possesses specialized experience testing Generative AI, LLMs, AI Agents, Chatbots, Copilots, Prompt Engineering, and RAG solutions (including AI response validation/evaluation), with deep familiarity in the Model Context Protocol (MCP), Agentic AI frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI, Semantic Kernel, LangGraph), Vector Databases, Semantic Search, and major AI platforms (Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Foundry, OpenAI, Claude, and Google Gemini).

Infrastructure, Cloud & CI/CD: Proficiency with public cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and containerization technologies like Docker and Kubernetes, combined with exposure to CI/CD tooling including Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions, or Azure DevOps Pipelines.

System Architecture & Testing: A solid understanding of service-oriented and event-driven architecture patterns, supported by proven experience in testing high-volume, distributed systems.

Domain & Emerging Technology: Knowledge of Web 3.0 concepts, Distributed Ledger Technologies, or Blockchain ecosystems, alongside operational exposure to Asset Management, Post-Trade Processing, Financial Markets, or Reference Data platforms.

title: Document Preparation Assistant
description:
Document Preparation Assistant (Full- Time Contract)
South Vancouver, BC

We are seeking a highly organized and detail-oriented Document Preparation Assistant to join Wesgroup’s records digitization project through the end of 2027. Reporting to the Manager, Office Services, you will play an important role in transforming our physical records into an organized and accessible digital archive, with responsibility for document preparation, scanning, quality control and file organization.
In this hands-on role, you will prepare documents for scanning by organizing files, removing fasteners, sorting records, and ensuring materials are ready for digitization. This position involves high-volume document handling and is ideal for someone who enjoys structured work, takes pride in accuracy, and thrives in a fast-paced environment where attention to detail matters.

ABOUT WESGROUP

Wesgroup started as a family business in British Columbia seventy years ago and today is one of Western Canada’s largest private real estate companies with a diversified portfolio spanning across residential and commercial real estate. Wesgroup owns and manages over 4.4 million square feet of commercial and multi-family real estate and has built almost 10,000 homes in communities across BC. With the active projects in our development pipeline, the portfolio is forecasted to grow to 6.7 million square feet by the end of 2031.

Our operations are vertically integrated, encompassing land acquisition, development, construction, finance, design, marketing, sales, leasing, and property management. We have a long history of looking forward and we are dedicated to conducting business in line with our values of adaptability, accountability, relationships, and observing The Golden Rule without fail.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

Prepare documents for scanning by removing staples, paper clips, bindings, and other fasteners.
Sort, organize, label, and prepare files and bankers' boxes according to established processes.
Verify documents are complete, organized, and in the correct sequence before digitization.
Maintain a high degree of accuracy and quality while processing large volumes of records.

Handle confidential and sensitive information in accordance with company policies.
Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work environment.
Lift, carry, and move bankers' boxes weighing up to 40 lbs.
Work effectively in a warehouse or records storage environment.
Provide occasional backup support to the Document Control team as required.

WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR

Exceptional attention to detail and ability to follow established procedures.

Comfortable performing repetitive tasks while maintaining a high level of quality.

Organized, dependable, and able to work independently with minimal supervision.
Strong time management skills and ability to maintain productivity while meeting deadlines.
Able to perform the physical requirements of the role, including standing for extended periods and lifting bankers' boxes weighing up to 40 lbs.
Reliable, punctual, and committed to successfully completing the full contract term.
Previous experience with records management, filing, document preparation, or administrative support is an asset, but not required.

COMPENSATION & REWARDS

The expected hourly salary range for this role is $ 19 – 20 per hour. Actual salary offered will depend on individual experience and qualifications for the role.
Opportunity to earn a performance bonus based on the achievement of key project milestones and successful completion of the full contract term.
Access to Wesgroup’s extended benefits program to support your health and wellbeing.

WHY JOIN WESGROUP

A Great Place to Work® Certified organization recognized for fostering a supportive, inclusive, and inspiring workplace culture.

title: Principal Scientist (Director), Clinical Research, Immunology
description:
Job Description

The Clinical Director (Principal Scientist) has primary responsibility for the strategic planning and directing clinical research activities involving investigational compounds in Immunology. With a focus on late-stage development, the Clinical Director will manage the entire cycle of clinical development, including determination of appropriate disease indications to pursue and subsequent study design, initiation, execution, monitoring, analysis, regulatory filing, and publication.

Specifically, The Clinical Director May Be Responsible For:

  • Evaluating pre-clinical and translational work for the purpose of generating the early clinical development plan and Investigational New Drug applications.
  • Providing clinical development support of business development assessments of external opportunities to grow the Immunology Pipeline
  • Developing clinical development strategies for investigational drugs and planning clinical trials (design, operational plans, settings) based on these clinical development strategies
  • Monitoring and managing the conduct of ongoing or new clinical trials for investigational drugs
  • Analyzing and summarizing the clinical findings from studies to support decisions regarding safety and efficacy as well as new drug applications, clinical study reports, or publication; and
  • Participation in internal and joint internal/external research project teams relevant to the development of new compounds


The Clinical Director may:
Supervise the activities of Clinical Scientists in the execution of clinical studies. Work closely with a cross-functional group of experts in commercialization, regulatory affairs, statistics, and manufacturing to manage clinical development projects; and assist the Senior Director, Associate Vice-President/Vice-President and Product Development Team Lead in ensuring that appropriate corporate personnel is informed of the progress of studies of our company and competitors' drugs and internal and external expert opinion on scientific questions relevant to his/her areas of responsibility.


The Clinical Director is responsible for maintaining a strong scientific fund of knowledge by:

  • Maintaining awareness of scientific developments within his/her area of expertise, in terms of new scientific findings, research methodologies
  • Identification of scientifically and operationally strong investigators who can assist in the development of our company's investigational drugs in Immunology
  • Establishing collaborative relationships with external experts in Rheumatology diseases, particularly those whose research focus and expertise can inform and assist the evaluation of the company's investigational drugs
  • Attending appropriate scientific meetings to maintain his or her competency and to maintain awareness of research activities in his/her area of responsibility.


To accomplish these goals, the Clinical Director may:

  • Author detailed development documents, presentations, budgets, and position papers for internal and external audiences
  • Facilitate collaborations with external researchers around the world
  • Travel on company business about twenty (20) percent of the time to manage future or ongoing clinical research projects.

Qualifications


Education

  • M.D., D.O., M.D./Ph.D, or D.O./Ph.D.

Required education and experience

  • Minimum of 5 years of clinical and/or development experience (academia, clinical medicine, and/or corporate clinical development).
  • Demonstrated record of scientific scholarship and achievement
  • Prior experience in design and execution of phase 2 or 3 clinical trials in rheumatologic diseases is preferred
  • Strong interpersonal skills, as well as the ability to work collaboratively in a cross-functional team environment

Required Skills:

Clinical Development, Clinical Research, Clinical Trial Planning, Cross-Functional Teamwork, Immunology, Rheumatology

title: Lead Infrastructure & DevOps
description:
1. Infrastructure & OS Management

  • Manage and maintain Linux-based systems (Rocky Linux, CentOS, RHEL) in production and staging environments.
  • Perform kernel patching, security updates, and system hardening following industry best practices.
  • Troubleshoot and debug complex OS-level issues (performance, memory, I/O, kernel panics).
  • Manage and support Windows Server environments where applicable.

2. Security & Compliance

  • Perform regular security scanning and vulnerability assessments using tools like Nessus, Qualys, or OpenVAS.
  • Conduct code security scans (SAST/DAST) and integrate them into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Configure and maintain LDAP authentication for centralized access management.
  • Ensure all systems comply with internal security policies and external regulatory standards.
  • Implement and manage WAF (Web Application Firewall) configurations to protect against OWASP Top 10 threats.

3. Automation & Configuration Management

  • Write and maintain Ansible playbooks for automated provisioning, patching, and configuration management.
  • Manage GitHub Enterprise repositories, branching strategies, and CI/CD workflows (GitHub Actions preferred).
  • Develop automation scripts using Python, Shell, or Go to reduce toil and improve operational efficiency.

4. Application & Web Server Management

  • Configure and maintain Apache and Nginx web servers, including performance tuning and reverse proxy setup.
  • Troubleshoot web server logs, SSL/TLS issues, and load balancing configurations.

5. Container Orchestration & Cloud-Native Technologies

  • Deploy, manage, and scale applications on Kubernetes clusters (EKS, AKS, or on-prem).
  • Build and maintain Docker images with secure base layers and minimal attack surfaces.
  • Monitor cluster health, resource usage, and implement auto-scaling policies.

6. Monitoring & Incident Management

  • Deploy and maintain monitoring tools (Prometheus, Grafana, Datadog, or ELK stack).
  • Define SLIs, SLOs, and error budgets; drive blameless post-mortems.
  • Participate in on-call rotations and lead incident response efforts.

What Qualifies You

  • 8+ years in SRE, DevOps, or Systems Engineering roles.
  • Experience with Terraform or other IaC tools.
  • Familiarity with service mesh (Istio/Linkerd) and CNI plugins (Calico/Cilium) or similar.
  • Understanding of zero-trust networking and SSO integrations.
  • Certifications: RHCE, CKA, or CISSP are a plus.

OS: Expert in Rocky Linux, CentOS, RHEL (6+ years); Windows Server experience

Security: WAF, vulnerability scanning, LDAP, OS hardening, kernel patching

Automation: Ansible (playbooks, roles, AWX/Tower), Python/Shell scripting

CI/CD/SCM: GitHub Enterprise administration, GitHub Actions, branch protection rules

Containers: Docker (build/security scanning), Kubernetes (deployment, networking, storage)

Web Servers: Apache, Nginx (configuration, SSL, reverse proxy)

Monitoring: Prometheus, Grafana, ELK, or commercial tools (Datadog/New Relic)

Code Security: SAST/DAST tools (SonarQube, Snyk, Checkmarx)

Soft Skills & Cultural Fit

  • Strong communication and documentation skills.
  • Ability to mentor junior engineers and conduct technical interviews.
  • Collaborative mindset with DevOps/DevSecOps philosophy.
  • Calm under pressure during incidents; drive for continuous improvement.

Each team is structured to have one or two portfolio managers (PMs) who determine investment strategy and manager selection. The associates and senior associates work alongside the PMs to produce performance reports and presentations, provide exceptional client service and assist with building client portfolios.

In your work, you will learn about the financial markets, asset allocation, portfolio construction and various investment managers across a wide range of asset classes, including cash, fixed income, equities, hedge funds, private equity, venture capital, and real assets. You also could participate in special projects, such as asset class deep dives, portfolio reviews, and spending analyses. In addition, you may help to coordinate complex estate-planning transactions such as transfers of interest, partnership distributions, and charitable gifting. You will also learn to manage risk across client relationships by closely adhering to firm and regulatory policy, procedures, and processes.

You will work with a small number of clients and provide high quality client service, with frequent interactions with clients, family office staff, tax advisers and investment managers. Associates are an integral part of the team and could join both internal investment meetings as well as client meetings.

Associates typically spend their days completing independent work for clients, primarily using Excel and PowerPoint, as well as other software programs including Addepar and Salesforce. We will provide training on these programs, but a working knowledge is always a great start. Most importantly, we are looking for smart and dedicated team players who are eager to learn and contribute.

What Success Looks Like:

  • Within your first 30 days, you will participate in a robust training program to learn more about the firm, Pathstone’s investing strategy and reporting systems, and join your client teams.
  • Within your first 90 days, you will assist your teams with portfolio reporting, financial analyses and producing client presentations. You will work closely with our Data Operations team on data review, and work with our Investment Operations team to facilitate the execution of transactions for your clients, while providing outstanding client service.
  • Within your first year, you will have completed several quarterly cycles of portfolio reporting and presentations, built meaningful relationships with your client teams and portfolio managers, and have had the opportunity to be involved in several firm-enhancing initiatives, from our various committees to recruiting, training, and mentorship.

You Are a Great Fit If You:

  • Have a bachelor’s degree and less than two years of work experience.
  • Have an interest in financial markets and client service.
  • Enjoy working collaboratively and problem-solving in a diverse team environment where accountability and initiative are required.
  • Possess a keen interest in developing deep knowledge of client service, portfolio management, investments, and financial markets.
  • Value and model the attributes that make our firm great: collaboration, excellence, good judgement, initiative, innovation, integrity, and leadership.
  • Are an intellectually curious, creative problem-solver who is not afraid to ask questions.
  • Demonstrate strong oral and written communication skills as well as the desire and ability to provide excellent client service.
  • Possess top-notch organizational skills and a strong ability to balance time-sensitive priorities while maintaining a high level of attention to detail.
  • Thrive in a fast-paced, deadline-oriented environment with multiple supervisors.
  • Prioritize operating ethically and professionally, demonstrate a strong sense of integrity, and consistently exercise good judgement.
  • Welcome feedback and are quick to act upon it.
  • Operate with a positive, proactive, “no-job-is-too-small” attitude.
  • Demonstrate proficiency in Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint and Word.
  • Are comfortable with and able to quickly learn new technology platforms.
  • Are interested in learning how to use and optimize AI for day-to-day workflows in a creative manner.
  • Professionals from all majors, experiences, and backgrounds are invited to apply.

Pay Transparency: Pathstone’s expected starting base compensation for the position as of the time of posting is $65,000 – $90,000 per year. The actual base compensation selected for this role will be set based on a variety of factors, including (but not limited to) experience, education, specialty and training. The successful candidate(s) may also be eligible for a discretionary bonus award.

Visa Sponsorship: Please note, we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for the position offered. Accordingly, we are unable to hire individuals who require, or will require, employment visa sponsorship either now or in the future.

Pathstone is proud to be an equal opportunity employer.

In posing the application screening questions, we are seeking to understand how your personal experiences have informed and reflect your interest and fit for this role. To ensure authentic responses, we ask that candidates are thoughtful when using AI tools (such as Chat GPT) to compose answers to the application screening questions.

As you explore opportunities, know that Pathstone communicates with candidates exclusively through an @pathstone.com email address. We do not make unsolicited job offers, and we will never ask for personal or financial information through email or web forms. If you receive outreach that appears to be from Pathstone but originates from a different domain, please disregard it.

title: IT Analyst & Project Manager
description:
Job Title:

IT Analyst & Project Manager

Job Summary:

The IT Analyst and Project Manager plays a critical role in supporting the University of San Francisco’s (USF) technology and security objectives that align with USF’s mission, goals, and objectives. This hybrid position combines analytical, administrative, logistical support, and project management responsibilities in technical and security assessments and enterprise architecture operations.

This role requires strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to coordinate and execute multiple projects simultaneously in a dynamic higher education environment. Using ITS' methodology to plan, execute, and close projects within the project's scope, schedule, and budget, and meet the quality standards set by the sponsor.

Full Job Description:

Reporting to the Associate Director Enterprise Architecture, this role will collaborate across USF departments, third-party contractors and consultants. They will support the New Technology Assessment (NTA) process which entails engaging with potential vendors to acquire collateral for review and evaluation and ensuring that all of our requirements are met.

Key Responsibilities

IT Analysis and Support:

  • Collect, organize, and analyze data related to IT systems, security protocols, and technical assessments.

  • Collaborate with IT teams to identify requirements, vulnerabilities, and alignment with IT standards.

  • Coordinate logistics for security and technical assessments, including scheduling and documentation.

  • Document findings, track action items, and monitor resolution progress.

  • Manage the intake and review of vendor security assessments, ensuring proper documentation is collected and analyzed.

  • Facilitate effective communication between internal teams and external vendors.

  • Work with the service managers and owners to ensure project deliverables and documents are uploaded and archived and the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) and Knowledge Base is updated.

Project Management:

  • Manage multiple IT projects simultaneously, ensuring timely delivery within budget, scope and standards.

  • Develop detailed project plans, timelines, and resource allocations using tools like Asana, Microsoft Project, or Jira.

  • Track project progress, identify risks, and propose mitigation strategies to ensure project success.

  • Provide regular status updates to stakeholders through clear and concise reporting.

  • Facilitate stakeholder meetings to gather requirements, share progress, and resolve issues.

  • Oversee the transition of completed projects into operations, coordinating with ITS Help Desk, service owners, and any Third Party Support.

  • Perform additional duties as assigned to meet departmental and university objectives.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in business management, information systems, project management, or related field (or equivalent experience).

  • Three or more years of progressive experience in information technology, preferably in a higher education setting.

  • Proven ability to lead multiple projects to successful, on-time, and on-budget completion meeting quality standards.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for technical and non-technical audiences.

  • Collaborative team player with the ability to work independently.

  • Adaptable and resilient, capable of managing shifting priorities and tight deadlines.

  • Technically proficient in tools such as Microsoft Office Suite, Google Suite, Jira, ServiceNow.

  • Skilled in researching project-related issues and evaluating IT solutions.

  • Ability to learn and apply new technologies effectively.

  • PMI's Certified Associate in Project Management (CAPM) or equivalent certification is preferred.

Full-Time/Part-Time:

Full time

Pay Rate:

Salary

Salary Range :

$75,000-$100,000 annualized; commensurate with experience

title: Senior Project Manager
description:
SpecPro Sustainment and Environmental (SSE) is seeking Senior Project Managers to provide project management and general engineering support to the U.S. Army Garrison Hawaii (USAG Hawaii) Hawaii Infrastructure Task Force (HITF) on Oahu, Hawaii.
The Senior Project Manager will support the planning, design, and construction of potable water infrastructure repair, replacement, modernization, and capital improvement projects from initiation through commissioning. Each Project Manager will oversee a portfolio of projects and coordinate with HITF leadership, the Directorate of Public Works, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and other project stakeholders.
What You’ll Do:

Support infrastructure projects through planning, design, construction, and commissioning.
Manage a portfolio of potable water utility repair, replacement, modernization, and capital improvement projects across multiple sites on Oahu.
Develop programming documentation, including DD Form 1391 and DA Form 4283 (Facilities Engineering Work Request), as required.
Organize and participate in project planning and design charrettes.
Conduct technical reviews of concept, mid-design, and final design packages for compliance with applicable Unified Facilities Criteria (UFC), USAG Hawaii requirements, Army standards, and applicable codes.
Participate in project synchronization meetings with the Directorate of Public Works (DPW), U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), and other stakeholders.
Support cost, schedule, finance, and administrative analysis associated with assigned projects.
Provide ancillary real estate support, as required, including research and assessment of easements, leases, licenses, and other project-related real estate instruments.
Maintain required project records and contribute to recurring project and status reporting.

What You Bring:
Required:

Senior-level project management capability supporting infrastructure, engineering, design, construction, or facilities projects.
Ability to manage multiple projects and coordinate project requirements, schedules, technical reviews, and stakeholder activities.
Ability to review engineering and design documentation for compliance with applicable project criteria, standards, and codes.
Strong written, verbal, organizational, and stakeholder-coordination skills.
Must reside on Oahu or be willing to relocate to Oahu to support frequent on-site project visits, in-person meetings, and planning/design charrettes.
Must be able to satisfy applicable installation access, background screening, identity verification, and Common Access Card (CAC) requirements, as required for assigned duties.

Preferred:

Prior experience supporting military infrastructure and facilities repair projects and/or Military Construction (MILCON) projects.

This position is located on Oahu, Hawaii, and operates in a hybrid work environment. Personnel may perform certain duties remotely; however, this position requires residence on Oahu and frequent in-person availability at designated project sites, synchronization meetings, and planning/design charrettes.
Normal hours of operation are Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding recognized federal holidays and Government-directed facility closures.
All offers are contingent upon a thorough background check conducted on all final candidates, as deemed necessary and per State and Federal laws.
What We Offer:
SSE offers a competitive benefits package to include: paid holidays, paid time off including sick and vacation leave, medical, dental and vision insurance, flexible spending accounts, short and long term disability, company paid life insurance, 401(k) with a company match and discretionary profit sharing and tuition reimbursement.
SpecPro Sustainment and Environmental, LLC is an environmental and facility services firm headquartered in San Antonio, TX. We are a subsidiary of Bristol Bay Native Corporation (BBNC). If you are interested in joining our team, please submit your resume, qualifications, and salary requirements.
SSE is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to any protected category. Hiring preference will be given to BBNC shareholders, their spouses and descendants and Alaska Natives in accordance with Public Law 93-638.

title: Research Associate 1/Research Associate 2
description:
POSITION DURATION:

This is a six-month contract role located in San Carlos with the potential to extend or convert to full-time based on performance and business needs.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Research Associate 1/2 performs laboratory procedures of varying complexity contributing to cross functional activities as part of the RUO Oncology Team, a multidisciplinary team within the research and development department.

PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Normalize plasma samples.
  • Extract nucleic acids from whole blood, plasma, tissue blocks using automated and manual extraction methods
  • Perform library preparation for nextgen sequencing using automated and manual methods
  • Determine quantity and/or quality of nucleic acids using Quant-IT, Qubit, Nanodrop, BioAnalyzer, and qPCR
  • Load libraries onto next generation sequencing platforms ( NovaSeq, iSeq,, Miseq, etc)
  • Interpret data and determine appropriate next steps per outlined requirements
  • Perform routine laboratory equipment maintenance as defined in standard operating procedures
  • Recognize equipment and instrument malfunctions and escalate to R&D equipment support team and relevant team members
  • Track sample inventory and status using Laboratory Information Management Software or Google Sheets
  • Maintain accurate records of lab work using a variety of softwares including Google Sheets, Microsoft Excel, and internal databases
  • Periodically review standard operating procedures (SOP) and other work instructions
  • Suggest process improvements to subject matter experts as needed
  • Ensure accurate, ethical, and appropriate management of samples in compliance with all applicable federal regulation
  • Perform other tasks as specified by the manager/director
  • This role occasionally works with PHI both in paper and electronic form and has access to various technologies to access PHI (paper and electronic) in order to perform the job
  • Employees must complete training relating to HIPAA/PHI privacy, General Policies and Procedure Compliance training and security training as soon as possible but not later than the first 30 days of hire
  • Must maintain a current status on Natera training requirements
  • Employee must pass post offer criminal background check
  • Additional requirement: This role requires onsite work in San Carlos and flexibility to work shifted schedules (e.g., 7am - 4pm, 11am - 8pm, 7pm - 3am)

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS/BA in a biological science or equivalent required
  • 1-3 years of related laboratory experience

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES:

  • Extremely familiar with good pipetting practices (single and multi-channel micropipettes, serological pipettes)
  • Hands-on experience with library preparation and next generation sequencing platforms highly preferred (NovaSeq, MiSeq, iSeq etc.)
  • Hands-on experience with nucleic acid techniques (purification, quantification, amplification, etc)
  • Able to operate independently in lab under general supervision with minimal human error
  • Knowledge of LIMS/database softwares
  • Experience with laboratory automation is a plus
  • Excellent with Microsoft Office programs
  • Excellent with Google Drive including Docs, Sheets, Slides, and Forms
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills
  • Ability to think creatively and analytically with strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills
  • Team player with demonstrated strong interpersonal skills with an ability to build effective working relationships within functional area
  • Ability to thrive in a fast paced, evolving environment, and manage competing priorities efficiently

PHYSICAL DEMANDS AND WORK ENVIRONMENT:

  • Duties are typically performed in an office and laboratory setting daily
  • This position requires the ability to perform repetitive motions during pipetting and sample processing
  • This position requires the ability to use a computer keyboard, communicate over the telephone and read printed material
  • May require lifting or moving items weighing up to 25lbs.
