title: Nuclear Medicine Technologist II
description:
Better at Work. Better at Life.

When you work at St. Jude, you’ll join a highly collaborative work culture that inspires you every day to be your best. With opportunities for learning and growth, you can shape a career path that is right for you while also enjoying all the benefits and stability of working for a world-class institution. This includes work-life balance with generous paid time-off and on-campus conveniences that make life a little easier. Join us and you’ll quickly see why St. Jude is consistently ranked by our employees on Glassdoor as a “Best Place to Work.”

The Nuclear Medicine Technologist II performs a variety of advanced diagnostic and therapeutic nuclear medicine procedures utilizing radiopharmaceuticals and specialized imaging equipment. This position is responsible for producing high-quality diagnostic images, ensuring patient safety and comfort, adhering to radiation safety practices, and collaborating with physicians and multidisciplinary healthcare teams to support quality patient care.

Job Responsibilities:

  • Perform routine procedures within area (nuclear medicine procedures).
  • Operate equipment and execute processes as per protocol to ensure optimal diagnostic quality of patient care.
  • Communicate with patient and family around procedures; monitor and address/escalate any distress reported by patient.
  • Conduct documentation tasks within relevant information systems as per defined guidelines (e.g., storage, retrieval, tracking, disposal of paper, electronic and film imaging records, process logs, files, billing reports).
  • Produce and evaluate data, information, and images as required.
  • Perform quality control activities, document results and escalate issues as required.
  • Assist in set-up, calibration, preventive maintenance, and troubleshooting activities for equipment within area.
  • Support inventory management including monitoring, receipt, and appropriate storage of supplies; report inventory replenishment requirements to relevant teams.
  • Perform other duties as assigned to meet the goals and objectives of the department and institution.
  • Maintain regular and predictable attendance.

Minimum Education and/or Training:

  • Graduate of an accredited nuclear medicine technology program required.
  • Bachelor’s Degree preferred.

Minimum Experience:

  • 3+ years in performing nuclear medicine exams/procedures required.
  • Experience Exception: Bachelor's degree within relevant area (e.g., radiologic technology, nuclear medicine technology, ultrasound technology) with 1+ years of relevant experience.
  • Experience with documentation of diagnostic procedures and working with MS Office/ other relevant electronic systems preferred.
  • Experience with medical terminology related to area of Diagnostics/Imaging.
  • Proven performance in earlier role/ comparable role.

Licensure, Registration and/or Certification Required by Law:

  • Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification by either the American Registry of Radiologic Technologists (ARRT) or the Nuclear Medicine Technology Certification Board (NMTCB) required.

Licensure, Registration and/or Certification Required by SJCRH Only:

  • Certification in MR or CT preferred.

Special Skills, Knowledge and Abilities:

  • Ability to understand and adapt to changing priorities. Skills in structured problem-solving and openness to learning new approaches to execution.
  • Is able to apply knowledge/skills within own area to deliver tasks with limited guidance
  • Addresses problems in a structured, logical approach. Asks for guidance and tries out new ideas when changes in approach are required. Adapts quickly and positively; learns from mistakes.
  • Skills in clear and effective communication (written and verbal) and timely exchange of information with relevant stakeholders for work outcomes.
  • Questions, clarifies, and provides explanations as needed. Checks documents and reports for clarity and accuracy. Seeks and provides information within and outside team in a timely manner.
  • Skills in planning, prioritizing, and organizing work well. Ability to deliver under tight timelines with focus on quality and efficiency.
  • Plans around multiple tasks and priorities well within own work. Is able to cope with unexpected changes in routine and delivers planned outcomes on time. Escalates issues/problems and seeks support in a timely manner.
  • Skills in engaging with patients and prioritizing and addressing needs with a focus on efficient, responsive, high-quality delivery.
  • Promptly and effectively responds to patient queries and requests. Explores optimal solutions for patient needs with a focus on seamless hand-offs with other patient care teams. Escalates/ redirects effectively for quicker patient support with a focus on overall patient priorities.
  • Skills in imaging techniques, medication administration, and equipment operation to provide deliver safe and compliant diagnostic and imaging services within area.
  • Demonstrates strong knowledge/skills within area on a consistent basis to solve complex problems independently
  • Can conduct complex testing/ treatment procedures and analysis on general patient population autonomously in line with safety standards. Proactively communicates with patients and teams within area around education and support; understands, prioritizes and addresses/ escalates concerns in a timely manner. Analyzes and applies emerging research guidance within area of diagnostics/ imaging/ advanced imaging.

Compensation

In recognition of certain U.S. state and municipal pay transparency laws, St. Jude is including a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. This is an estimate offered in good faith and a specific salary offer takes into account factors that are considered in making compensation decisions including but not limited to skill sets, experience and training, licensure and certifications, and other business and organizational needs. It is not typical for an individual to be hired at or near the top of the salary range and compensation decisions are dependent on the facts and circumstances of each case. A reasonable estimate of the current salary range is $31.50 - $55.00 per hour for the role of Nuclear Medicine Technologist II.

About Advocate Health

Advocate Health is the third-largest nonprofit, integrated health system in the United States, created from the combination of Advocate Aurora Health and Atrium Health. Providing care under the names Advocate Health Care in Illinois; Atrium Health in the Carolinas, Georgia and Alabama; and Aurora Health Care in Wisconsin, Advocate Health is a national leader in clinical innovation, health outcomes, consumer experience and value-based care. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina, Advocate Health services nearly 6 million patients and is engaged in hundreds of clinical trials and research studies, with Wake Forest University School of Medicine serving as the academic core of the enterprise. title: Senior Ecological Management Specialist
description:
The Opportunity:

The Lands Branch of the Ministry of Environment is seeking a highly motivated, independent individual to work within the Land Management & Permitting Unit for a two year term. The successful candidate will be part of a provincial team that is responsible for leading the ministry’s response to the complex and growing demands associated with multiple industries such as mineral exploration, oil and gas, irrigation or linear disturbances.

The position requires an energetic and knowledgeable individual with the demonstrated ability to establish successful working relationships with various internal and external stakeholders and bring demonstrated working knowledge and experience within these industries to the role. The successful candidate must thrive in a high workload volume atmosphere.

  • Lead priority files involving emerging industries and resource development.
  • Review and support Crown land and environmental regulatory decisions.
  • Provide technical expertise on industry, policy and program issues.
  • Work with ministries, agencies, Indigenous communities, industry and stakeholders.
  • Assess competing environmental, regulatory, economic and policy interests.
  • Conduct fieldwork, inspections and information gathering across Saskatchewan.
  • Communicate technical and regulatory information clearly to diverse audiences.
  • Mentor staff and provide guidance on emerging trends, policies and procedures.

Job Capabilities:

As a public servant, we are seeking someone who:

  • Is accountable, takes ownership of their work by contributing to organizational outcomes and demonstrates the corporate values in our Commitment to Excellence.
  • Is innovative and seeks out ways for improvement by thinking creatively, identifying new ideas and taking responsible risks.
  • Works collaboratively with others to understand, engage and have meaningful dialogue to achieve work outcomes.
  • Is inclusive, identifies and is aware of personal bias, and readily seeks out and appreciates diverse perspectives.
  • Is adaptable, continuously learns from experience and applies those learnings to new situations.
  • Focuses on achieving public service excellence.


Technical Knowledge and Skills:

You will have demonstrated a thorough knowledge of:

  • Principles of integrated resource management and ecological protection;
  • Industry/scientific terminologies and principles and applied methodologies related to relevant petroleum, natural gas or mineral exploration, and linear developments;
  • General agricultural practices;
  • Crown land management issues;
  • Processes for reviewing, approving and monitoring the petroleum industry, the mineral exploration industry;
  • Applicable acts, regulations and legislation; and
  • First Nations and Métis constitutional rights, treaties and the relationship to the Duty to Consult and implementation of The First Nation and Métis Consultation Policy Framework, 2023

Typically, knowledge for this position is gained through a degree in natural sciences or integrated resource management, or other related degrees, supplemented by a minimum of ten years of related experience in environmental/ecological program delivery associated crown land management and recent experience regulating ecological/environmental impacts associated with oil and gas exploration, mineral exploration or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • Influence (Level C)

title: Senior Cybersecurity Business Analyst – Encryption & Post-Quantum Cryptography 3672717 (New York City, NY)
description:
Be Part Of A High-Performing Team

Join the enterprise information protection organization of a major global financial institution known for combining deep financial-services expertise with a strong emphasis on integrity, collaboration, innovation, and disciplined risk management. The cybersecurity organization works across engineering, architecture, infrastructure, application development, and risk teams to protect highly regulated enterprise environments. This position will support strategic cryptography modernization efforts, including enterprise encryption discovery, crypto-agility, and preparation for the transition to post-quantum cryptography.

What's In Store For You

  • Engagement: W2 only (no C2C/1099)
  • Hybrid opportunity based in New York City.
  • Work on a highly visible cybersecurity initiative addressing enterprise encryption modernization and emerging post-quantum cryptography requirements.
  • Partner with cybersecurity, infrastructure, application, architecture, and risk professionals across a large financial-services environment.
  • Gain exposure to enterprise-scale cryptographic discovery, PQC readiness, crypto-agility, and security-control modernization.

How You Will Make An Impact

  • Lead business and technical analysis activities supporting enterprise encryption and post-quantum cryptography initiatives.
  • Gather, analyze, and document requirements across cybersecurity, infrastructure, application development, architecture, and risk stakeholders.
  • Drive cryptographic inventory and discovery efforts spanning applications, databases, cloud platforms, middleware, certificates, file systems, and key-management environments.
  • Analyze dependencies involving PKI, TLS/SSL certificates, HSMs, key-management systems, database encryption, tokenization, data masking, and related cryptographic controls.
  • Document current-state and future-state processes, data flows, control requirements, dependencies, and crypto-agility requirements.
  • Support identification of legacy algorithms, protocols, and certificate dependencies that may require modernization as part of PQC transition planning.
  • Maintain requirements traceability, RAID logs, remediation milestones, project documentation, executive reporting, and readiness dashboards.
  • Facilitate workshops and working sessions between security engineering, security architecture, technology, application, and risk stakeholders.
  • Support vendor assessments, proofs of concept, cryptographic discovery tooling, and technology evaluations.
  • Help establish roadmaps for encryption modernization and adoption of emerging NIST post-quantum cryptography standards.

Do You Bring Proven Success in Cybersecurity Business Analysis and Cryptography?

  • 7+ years of Business Analyst experience supporting complex enterprise technology or cybersecurity initiatives; senior-level experience is strongly preferred.
  • Strong requirements elicitation, analysis, process documentation, stakeholder management, workshop facilitation, and executive reporting capabilities.
  • Financial-services experience within a large, regulated enterprise environment.
  • Demonstrated exposure to cybersecurity, data protection, encryption, PKI, certificate management, key management, or related cryptographic technologies.
  • Working understanding of enterprise cryptographic controls and dependencies across applications and infrastructure.
  • Familiarity with encryption technologies and protocols such as AES-256, RSA, ECC, TLS, SSH, PGP, and KMIP.
  • Exposure to PKI platforms, certificate authorities, HSMs, KMS platforms, and secrets-management technologies.
  • Knowledge of encryption approaches for data at rest, data in transit, databases, files, disks, cloud environments, and application platforms.
  • Familiarity with AWS, Azure, or GCP encryption and key-management capabilities.
  • Knowledge of crypto-agility and Post-Quantum Cryptography concepts, including emerging NIST standards and algorithms such as ML-KEM and ML-DSA.
  • Exposure to cybersecurity frameworks or regulatory standards such as NIST, CRI, NYDFS, FFIEC, PCI-DSS, or comparable banking-security requirements.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to translate complex security and cryptographic concepts between highly technical teams and business stakeholders.

title: Tournament Logistics Operator (m/f/x)
description:
• Do you enjoy keeping complex event logistics organized, on track and running smoothly?

If the answers to the above questions are yes, then this role could be ideal for you!

GRID is looking for a Tournament Logistics Operator to join our Tournament Services team and take ownership of the operational logistics that support our tournaments.

You will be a key point of contact for participating teams throughout the tournament lifecycle, coordinating Team Participation Agreements, prize money processes, travel arrangements and other team logistics. Working closely with Tournament Services, Finance and Legal, as well as esports teams, travel providers and other tournament stakeholders, you will ensure that every requirement is understood, delivered accurately and completed on time.

This role combines team relationship management, financial and legal coordination, travel logistics and operational execution. You will manage multiple deadlines and stakeholders simultaneously, identify potential issues before they become blockers, communicate clearly and provide teams with timely, professional support throughout their engagement with GRID.

From preparing teams ahead of an event to supporting them during the tournament and ensuring all outstanding requirements are closed afterward, you will play an important role in making sure the team experience is smooth, efficient, and well-organized.

What you will do

  • Before the tournament

    • Coordinate the operational logistics required for participating teams, including Team Participation Agreements, prize money and travel.

    • Manage team travel arrangements, including flights, accommodation, visas and other event-related logistics where required.

    • Identify logistical risks and coordinate their resolution.

  • During the tournament

    • Act as the primary point of contact for participating teams regarding tournament logistics and provide timely operational support.

    • Maintain clear communication between teams and relevant GRID stakeholders to ensure logistical issues do not impact tournament delivery.

  • After the tournament

    • Coordinate outstanding prize money, TPA, and travel-related requirements through to completion.

    • Maintain accurate logistics records and provide visibility of outstanding actions and key operational information.

    • Support post-event reviews and identify opportunities to improve team logistics and the overall team experience.

What Success Looks Like

  • Prize money payment cycles and Team Participation Agreements are completed accurately and within agreed timelines.

  • Participating teams receive timely, professional and consistent support throughout their engagement with GRID.

  • Tournament travel is delivered efficiently and with minimal disruption to tournament delivery.

  • Finance, Legal and Tournament Services have the information required to complete their responsibilities on time.

  • Team logistics requirements, risks and outstanding actions are identified and managed proactively.

  • Teams have clear visibility of relevant requirements, timelines and changes throughout the tournament lifecycle.

  • Logistical issues are resolved quickly or escalated appropriately when required.

Nice to have

  • Previous experience working directly with esports teams, players or tournament participants.

  • Experience in esports tournament logistics, team services, event operations or travel coordination.

  • Experience coordinating participation agreements, contracts, invoices, prize money or other event-related financial processes.

  • Experience coordinating prize money, invoices, payments or other event-related financial processes.

  • Experience managing international team travel, including flights, accommodation, visas, ground transportation or hospitality.

  • Experience managing travel budgets, event expenditure or supplier costs.

  • Additional language skills relevant to GRID's tournament regions.

title: Senior Digital Design Verification Engineer
description:
Renesas is seeking a Senior Digital Design Verification Engineer to join our team developing complex power management SoCs. These products integrate digital control, telemetry, fault management, communication interfaces, configurable peripherals, and advanced power-control functions for AI, datacenter, enterprise computing, networking, and high-performance power delivery applications.

You will independently own verification of significant blocks and features from planning through closure. The role combines hands-on UVM development, coverage-driven verification, complex debug, and close collaboration with architecture, RTL design, firmware, analog, validation, and systems teams.

Responsibilities

  • Own verification of complex digital blocks or major SoC features from requirements analysis through coverage closure.

  • Develop feature-based verification plans from product, architecture, and microarchitecture specifications; identify gaps, ambiguities, corner cases, and risks.

  • Build and extend reusable SystemVerilog/UVM environments, including sequences, monitors, scoreboards, checkers, assertions, and coverage models.

  • Develop constrained random and targeted tests for normal operation, error handling, recovery, and system-level interactions.

  • Drive functional, code, toggle, FSM, and assertion coverage closure using regression and coverage data.

  • Debug RTL, testbench, assertion, integration, and regression failures; collaborate with design and firmware teams to isolate issues and verify fixes.

  • Automate regression, triage, reporting, and analysis workflows using scripting and modern engineering tools.

  • Communicate status, risks, dependencies, and closure evidence clearly; provide technical guidance to less-experienced engineers.

  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field.

  • 4 or more years of relevant digital design verification experience, or equivalent directly applicable experience.

  • Demonstrated ownership of a complex block, subsystem, or major feature from verification planning through closure.

  • Strong proficiency in SystemVerilog, UVM, constrained random verification, functional coverage, and SystemVerilog Assertions.

  • Experience translating specifications into test plans, test scenarios, checkers, scoreboards, assertions, coverage models, and closure criteria.

  • Hands-on experience developing and debugging reusable UVM environments and analyzing complex regression failures.

  • Strong RTL and testbench debug skills, with the ability to distinguish design, environment, test, firmware, and specification issues.

  • Working knowledge of digital design fundamentals, including state machines, clocks and resets, interrupts, register interfaces, memories, and clock-domain crossings.

  • Proficiency in Linux and at least one scripting language such as Python, Bash, Perl, or Tcl.

  • Ability to work independently and collaborate effectively across architecture, design, firmware, analog, validation, and systems teams.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience verifying complex SoCs, power management ICs, voltage regulators, digital controllers, or mixed-signal products.

  • Experience verifying RTL interfaces to embedded processors, memory-mapped peripherals, and firmware-controlled hardware features.

  • Familiarity with PMBus, AVSBus, SVID or SVI3, I2C, SPI, or similar control and communication protocols.

  • Understanding of telemetry, fault and alert handling, power sequencing, multiphase regulation, or digital control loops.

  • Experience with Cadence Xcelium, SimVision, vManager, JasperGold, Synopsys VCS, Verdi, or comparable tools.

  • Experience with formal verification, gate-level simulation, silicon bring-up, or pre-silicon-to-silicon correlation.

  • Experience improving regression infrastructure, coverage analytics, failure triage, or verification automation.

What You Bring

  • Strong technical ownership and a disciplined approach to verification completeness.

  • Ability to reason beyond directed requirements and identify meaningful corner cases and feature interactions.

  • Clear communication of technical risk, progress, and signoff evidence.

  • A collaborative mindset and interest in improving verification methodology and productivity.

Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier. With a global team of over 21,000 engineers and problem solvers in more than 30 countries, we offer the opportunity to work on world‑leading technology for Automotive, Industrial, Infrastructure, and IoT, shaping a safer, healthier, greener, and smarter future.

At Renesas, TAGIE is our culture, grounded in being Transparent, Agile, Global, Innovative, and Entrepreneurial. It shapes how we work, grow and deliver on our purpose together. This collaborative spirit and mindset drive our semiconductor technology to transform industries and impact millions of lives.

title: Director of Operations
description:
Director of Operations

Community Management Services

Company: Inframark — Community Management Services
Reports to: VP, Operations
Industry Context: Community Management Services industry

About the Role

Inframark Community Management Services provides management services to clients in Florida, Texas and Arizona. Our clients in Florida include homeowner associations, Community Development Districts under Chapter 190 — special districts governed by elected Boards of Supervisors that finance, construct, operate, and maintain community-wide infrastructure such as roads, stormwater systems, and amenities. The Director of Operations will have P&L and operational leadership of multiple departments within the business to ensure consistent, compliant, high-quality service delivery across the business portfolio. This is a hands-on operating leadership role: building cross-functional alignment among department heads, owning portfolio-wide performance, and serving as the VP's operating partner on growth and service quality.

Key Responsibilities

Lead and align multiple department leaders into a single, coordinated operating team
Own end-to-end service delivery across the CDD portfolio: district governance support, field/maintenance execution, amenity operations, and administrative/records compliance
Ensure compliance with Florida Chapter 190 governance requirements across all managed districts (Board meetings, records custodianship, public records requests, election cycles)
Partner with Business Development and Department Leaders on new client wins, RFP responses, and onboarding of newly formed or newly awarded districts
Set portfolio-wide performance standards and KPIs for management, maintenance, field services, and amenity operations; hold department heads accountable to them
Own budget and fiscal performance across the various departments in partnership with all Department leaders
Resolve cross-departmental bottlenecks
Serve as an escalation and resolution point for client concerns
Report KPI performance, compliance risk, staffing needs, and growth pipeline to the VP

Preferred Qualifications

Open to candidates from outside the CDD/community management industry — strong operations leadership in another multi-site, multi-department, or regulated-services environment is valued as much as sector-specific tenure
8+ years in operations leadership overseeing multiple departments, functions, or business units — property/facilities management, hospitality, healthcare operations, municipal services, utilities, or similar multi-site industries all translate well
3–5+ years leading multiple functional leaders or department heads (not just individual managers or single-site supervisors) in a multi-disciplinary operations structure
Experience owning P&L or budget performance across a multi-department or multi-site organization
Demonstrated ability to manage through department heads rather than direct field execution — a true second-layer operating leader
Comfortable serving as a senior escalation point in front of executive leadership, governing boards, or key clients/stakeholders
Comfort operating in a regulated, public-facing, or governance-driven environment; specific experience with Florida Chapter 190 CDD governance (Board of Supervisors relations, public meetings, records/compliance administration) is a strong plus but not required — this can be developed on the job

Preferred / Differentiators

Prior experience specifically managing a CDD services organization with separated functional departments (vs. a generalist property/community manager background)
Experience supporting or partnering with Business Development on new client capture and onboarding process
Experience integrating acquired or newly awarded clients into standardized operating processes
Track record building shared standards/KPIs across previously siloed departments

title: Payload Operations Engineer III (TS/SCI Required)
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

The role is part of the In-Space Systems business unit, which is focused on addressing two of the most compelling challenges in spaceflight today: space infrastructure and increasing mobility on-orbit.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

This role is part of the Blue National Security (BNS) Business Unit, which is focused on delivering resilient, mission-critical space capabilities, including Blue Ring, to support national defense and objectives. With Blue Ring, our customers are empowered to achieve operational advantage across cislunar and Earth orbit domains, redefine mission flexibility, and pursue bold new concepts that were once beyond reach.

As a Payload Operations Engineer supporting Blue Ring, you will ensure mission readiness by contributing to the development of hosted and separable payload-specific operational concepts, preparing essential operations products, and serving as a key member of the on-console team during mission execution. You will collaborate extensively with engineers from across the space and ground segments to ensure payload operations and the associated mission planning are successfully performed on orbit. The ideal candidate is a systems-thinker with a strong focus on customer experience, possessing the persistence and passion to build and execute space operations from the ground up.

Join us in enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth — passion for our mission is required!

Special Mentions

  • This role requires occasional periods of shift work and on-call availability during mission-critical phases, anomaly resolution, and key customer milestones.

Responsibilities Include But Are Not Limited To:

  • Contribute to the development of hosted and separable payload mission plans, operations concepts, tools, and processes that enable highly effective real-time operations.
  • Develop and implement detailed spacecraft payload operations procedures, executables, telemetry displays, and other technical documentation.
  • Conduct testing and validation of payload operations products using a variety of hardware and software simulation environments.
  • Support mission planning efforts with geographically separated payload teams to ensure operational objectives are met during on-orbit operations.
  • Support the development of the overall spacecraft concept of operations, ensuring payload operability and efficiency.
  • Create detailed test procedures alongside of systems engineering teams to validate end-to-end ground to payload system capabilities.
  • Support mission readiness activities including mission rehearsals, timeline development, and post-launch test planning.
  • Monitor payload state-of-health, perform trending and analysis on performance data, and track system configurations throughout on-orbit execution.
  • Serve as liaison between payload customers and Blue Ring operations team during pre-launch coordination as well as during long-term operations.
  • Support development of payload operations sequencing and incorporation into the mission planning system.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • B.S. in Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 5+ years of proven experience in spacecraft operations development or execution.
  • Must have an active Top Secret / Sensitive Compartmented Information (TS/SCI) U.S. Government security clearance.
  • Experience developing spacecraft or hosted payload operations products, such as procedures, telemetry displays, or technical documents.
  • Experience with supporting external customers or government teams.
  • Ability to support on-console activities, including shift work, in a dynamic, real-time environment.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • M.S. in Space Systems, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or Aerospace Engineering.
  • Direct support for a commercial or government spacecraft operations organization.
  • Proficiency with command-and-control scripting languages, such as Python, SPELL, STOL, or JAS.
  • Experience working with virtualized Ground Software (e.g., Command & Control, Mission Planning, Flight Dynamics, Electronic Procedures).
  • Experience with mission planning and contact planning tools.
  • Experience with satellite fault management and/or onboard autonomy.
  • Familiarity with designing and evaluating operational readiness tests integrated with hardware-in-the-loop and software-in-the-loop simulators.

title: Group Lead Intellectual Property Counsel
description:

This role will partner closely with cross‑functional leaders to design, direct, and execute robust IP strategies that protect and advance Dr. Reddy’s mission of providing affordable and innovative healthcare solutions.

The Group Lead will play a pivotal role in guiding patent litigation strategy across North America (small and large molecules), overseeing the full IP life cycle from project identification to commercial launch. This position requires strong collaboration with Portfolio, R&D, Regulatory Affairs, Business Development, and external legal partners, and demands strong leadership capabilities, technical insight, and strategic foresight.

  • Guide the development and implementation of legal claims, defenses, and litigation strategies, including management of external counsel
  • Ensure freedom‑to‑operate (FTO) for Dr. Reddy’s products across APIs, synthetic routes, formulations, and polymorphs
  • Supervise and guide drafting, prosecution, and maintenance of patent applications in coordination with R&D and global teams
  • Lead IP due diligence for in‑licensing, partnerships, and other strategic collaborations
  • Provide senior‑level IP input to commercial teams to support portfolio shaping, launch planning, and deal evaluations
  • Act as a key partner to R&D, Regulatory Affairs, Portfolio, and Business Development teams to ensure alignment of IP strategy with scientific and business priorities
  • Counsel internal partners on regulatory and patent law matters, exclusive frameworks, litigation risks, and launch pathway scenarios

Educational qualification:

  • Juris Doctor (JD) from an accredited law school
  • Licensed to practice in New Jersey or at least one U.S. state with eligibility for the New Jersey in‑house counsel license
  • Registration to practice before the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) strongly preferred
  • Bachelor’s or higher degree in Science or Engineering required; Chemistry, Biochemistry, or related disciplines preferred
  • Advanced scientific degree (MS or PhD) highly desirable

Minimum work experience:

  • 12+ years of progressive experience in pharmaceutical patent law, including extensive Hatch‑Waxman and BPCIA litigation experience
  • Prior experience leading teams or managing complex, multi‑stakeholder IP programs strongly preferred
  • Demonstrated track record in developing and executing successful IP strategies in the generic, branded, or biosimilar pharmaceutical space
  • Experience in IPR proceedings preferred

Skills & attributes:

  • Deep expertise in patent litigation, prosecution, regulatory exclusivities, and pharmaceutical law
  • Strong leadership presence with the ability to inspire teams and influence at senior level
  • Highly strategic mindset with the ability to balance legal risk with business objectives
  • Strong analytical, problem‑solving, and decision‑making skills
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder‑management abilities
  • High degree of independence, ownership, and professional judgment

Incumbent must be a U.S. citizen or lawful permanent resident of U.S. or otherwise authorized to work in the U.S. without requiring visa transfer or sponsorship, now or in the future.

Incumbent should be willing to work in person from our Princeton, NJ office

Boardwalk is a limited partnership operating in the midstream portion of the natural gas and natural gas liquids industry, providing transportation and storage services for our customers. Our 14,000 miles of pipeline and storage assets provide diverse market connectivity to producers and end-users who need reliable sources of natural gas for power generation, home heating or petrochemical feedstocks. We have the experience, knowledge, and flexibility to design service offerings and create system enhancements tailored to our customers’ needs throughout the 13 states in which we operate. As an organization focused on sustainability, we are committed to protecting the environment while delivering this energy source. This commitment is made to our customers, employees, and the communities in which we operate. We incorporate environmental stewardship, safety, and compliance into our day-to-day operations and seek to strengthen and support the communities we serve. Additional information about the company can be found online at www.bwpipelines.com.

We are currently looking for a Mechanical Specialist/Sr Mechanical Specialist for our Dillsboro, IN location.

POSITION DESCRIPTION:

This position is responsible for regulatory compliance and the operation, maintenance, and repair of station equipment, including reciprocating and centrifugal natural gas compressors, air compressors, natural gas-fired engines, turbines, fluid separation equipment, valves, and related appurtenances. This includes following DOT regulations, industry standards, manufacturer recommendations, and BWP guidelines. This position must follow all BWP safety rules, environmental and OSHA regulations, document maintenance and operational activities, respond to emergencies, and may occasionally assist at other compressor stations.

Key responsibilities include operating equipment and leading repairs and maintenance of reciprocating natural gas-fired engines, turbines, and associated compressors, including overhauls and mechanical repairs. The role involves completing OMS database compliance, performing routine maintenance such as filter changes, cleaning and inspecting coolers, and periodic checks of components throughout the facility and engines/compressors (e.g., valves, shutdown devices, rod/bearing clearances, packing, piston clearances, lube oil samples, web deflections, cooling fans, emergency shutdown systems, fire/gas detection). The position also requires monitoring flows and operating conditions for assigned area.

This position will be located at our Dillsboro, IN Compressor Station and will operate in a scheduled rotation. Normal work hours for this position are 7:00 a.m. – 3:30 p.m. weekdays but are subject to change; however, this position is subject to occasional call-out and schedule adjustments, as necessary.

This position's primary area of responsibility will be at our Dillsboro, IN Compressor Station, and successful candidate will be required to reside within 30 miles of this facility.

REQUIRED SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE

Progressive, hands-on mechanical experience with natural gas engines and compressor equipment, including installation, operation, maintenance, troubleshooting, repair, and/or overhaul of reciprocating and/or centrifugal compressors. Candidates must demonstrate substantial, continuous experience specializing in natural gas compression equipment.
Mechanical knowledge of 2- and 4-stroke, slow and high-speed engines and compressors
Mechanical knowledge of gas turbines
Excellent communication skills and the ability to interact with all levels of personnel, as well as strong critical thinking and problem solving skills and a strong ability for prioritizing and scheduling multiple projects.
Experience with Microsoft programs, including Word, Excel and familiarity with CMMS system for maintenance documentation.
Valid Driver’s license is required and the ability to operate an all-terrain vehicle.
Must have a strong commitment to personal and team safety.
Ability to work independently without direct supervision.
Ability to read and comprehend
manufacturer’s equipment manuals
Good troubleshooting skills
Physical requirements of the role include the ability to lift and carry 50 lbs. for a minimum of 50 feet in order to transfer tools and equipment, the ability to operate valve control wheels with a minimum of 50 turns, and the ability to work alone as required in extreme weather conditions including hot, cold, muddy, and wet environments.

description:
Autonomy Strategist
2.5-year Full Time term
Regina Campus

The First Nations University of Canada (FNUniv) provides students of all nations to learn in an environment of First Nations cultures, values and traditions. The University continues to uphold its mission of enhancing the quality of life and preserving, protecting, and interpreting First Nations people's history, language, culture, and artistic heritage. FNUniv is a unique learning place specializing in Indigenous knowledge and providing post-secondary education for Indigenous and non-Indigenous students within a culturally supportive environment.

The First Nations University of Canada is a federated college of the University of Regina, and its academic programs are accredited through that institution.

Under the direction of the Director of Autonomy, the Autonomy Strategist will engage with Indigenous Knowledge Keepers, other Elders, FNUniv leaders and communities to assist in developing a holistic multi-generational vision and strategic guiding document; one that embodies traditional Indigenous ways of knowing, being, and doing to support academic independence, realizing full university autonomy. This position will collaborate internally with various units to manage project plans and develop a comprehensive organizational framework and roadmap for autonomous academic systems.

Duties:

Participate in the research, planning, development, writing and implementation of a multi-generational (seven generations) vision document containing the creation story of FNUniv and a vision for an autonomous future.

Develop an institution-wide strategic plan with goals and objectives to achieve autonomy.
Plan and organize gatherings to seek input, report and communicate progress including public speaking and presentations with FNUniv Elders, faculty, staff, students, alumni and other stakeholders, as needed.
Collaborate with various units such as University Relations, Finance, Administration, Academic, Graduate Studies and Research, Library Services to develop an operational framework and roadmap including academic standards, accreditation and systems.

Contribute to developing options papers for those areas that have various alternatives with the pros and cons, rationale, analysis and background information that can assist executive decision-making.
Engage, share information and work with partners such as Elders, Knowledge Keepers, leaders, educational institutions, quality assurance boards, provincial, federal, and First Nations governments in the development and implementation of partnerships and agreements to advance autonomy.
Participate in relevant internal and external committees and working groups.

Qualifications:
Applicants must have an undergraduate degree. Preference given to applicants with a Master’s degree with a minimum of five (5) years’ related experience, preferably in a post-secondary environment. Familiarity and knowledge of First Nations cultural protocols and traditions is essential. Experience working with diverse groups of organizations and peoples, particularly Elders, Knowledge keepers, students, faculty, staff, alumni and First Nations communities and organizations. Proven understanding of university administrative structures, Indigenous governance systems and provincial and federal governments and corresponding jurisdictional issues. Comprehension of decolonizing education and Indigenous self-determination. An equivalent combination of education, training and experience may be considered.

title: M02 - Platform Operations Engineer
description:
About the Role

We are looking for an experienced Platform Operations Engineer / Operations Support Engineer to provide Day-2 operational, maintenance, and patching support for enterprise Oracle platforms.

The role will support Production (PROD), User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and Development (DEV) environments and will be responsible for maintaining platform stability, security, availability, and compliance.

The successful candidate should have strong hands-on experience across Oracle Fusion Middleware, WebLogic, Oracle Database, Data Guard, and Oracle Enterprise Manager, particularly within mission-critical production environments.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide Day-2 operational and patching support across Oracle platforms.
  • Monitor and assess quarterly Oracle Critical Patch Updates (CPU) and monthly Critical Security Patch Updates (CSPU).
  • Conduct pre-patch assessments covering compatibility, dependencies, conflicts, vulnerabilities, and potential impact.
  • Plan and schedule patching activities across DEV, UAT, and PROD environments.
  • Stage patch binaries and prepare environments for implementation.
  • Perform Oracle Home backups and ensure rollback and recovery readiness before patching.
  • Execute patch deployment while minimising service disruption, particularly within production environments.
  • Provide operational and patching support for Oracle HTTP Server (OHS).
  • Support Oracle WebLogic Server and Oracle Application Development Framework (ADF).
  • Support Oracle Forms and Reports and Oracle Fusion Middleware 14c environments.
  • Support Oracle Database Enterprise Server 19c and Oracle Data Guard environments.
  • Perform database patching within active/passive Data Guard architectures.
  • Manage database switchover activities and validate database health, connectivity, listeners, redo transport, and synchronization.
  • Support and patch Oracle Enterprise Manager (OEM) 13c, including Management Servers, repository databases, and monitoring agents.
  • Support patching and validation activities for Pro*C environments.
  • Review vulnerability assessment findings, security reviews, and audit findings.
  • Determine the applicability of identified vulnerabilities and recommend appropriate remediation actions.
  • Implement approved patching, configuration hardening, and remediation activities.
  • Conduct post-remediation validation and support vulnerability re-scanning activities.
  • Raise and manage Oracle Service Requests (SRs) for patch-related technical issues.
  • Coordinate with Oracle Support engineers to troubleshoot and resolve technical issues.
  • Perform post-patch validation, service health checks, and stabilization support.
  • Troubleshoot middleware, database, application connectivity, and patch-related issues.
  • Prepare patch documentation including CPU Assessment Risk Matrix, Method of Procedure (MOP), implementation schedules, rollback plans, validation records, and completion reports.
  • Ensure all activities comply with operational, security, change management, and governance requirements.
  • Support knowledge transfer and technical handover activities when required.

Requirements

  • Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience administering Oracle Fusion Middleware environments, preferably 14c or above.
  • Hands-on experience supporting Oracle Database 19c and Oracle Data Guard environments.
  • Strong experience with Oracle HTTP Server (OHS).
  • Strong experience with Oracle WebLogic Server.
  • Experience with Oracle Application Development Framework (ADF).
  • Experience supporting Oracle Forms and Reports.
  • Experience with Oracle Database administration and patching.
  • Experience supporting Oracle Enterprise Manager (OEM).
  • Experience working with Pro*C environments.
  • Proven experience performing Oracle CPU patching.
  • Experience supporting mission-critical production systems with minimal or no downtime.
  • Strong knowledge of Oracle backup, rollback, recovery, and restoration procedures.
  • Hands-on knowledge of Data Guard switchover and synchronization procedures.
  • Strong troubleshooting skills across Oracle middleware, databases, connectivity, and patch-related issues.
  • Experience working within enterprise-scale or regulated environments with formal change, release, and configuration management processes.
  • Strong documentation, stakeholder coordination, and incident-management skills.
  • Able to support scheduled production maintenance activities after office hours, on weekends, and on public holidays when required.

title: Principal Architect, Autonomous Systems (Ground and Space)
description:
Application close date:

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!

The role is part of the In-Space Systems business unit, which is focused on addressing two of the most compelling challenges in spaceflight today: space infrastructure and increasing mobility on-orbit.

Role Summary

You are the technical owner of Blue National Security's autonomy product architecture, spanning both ground and space. You will define how autonomous capability is decomposed across the ground segment and the vehicle, drive that architecture through implementation across every contributing discipline, and carry it to operational deployment.

Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end autonomy product architecture across ground and space. Define the system decomposition, interfaces, and functional allocation between ground based and onboard autonomy, and own the technical roadmap that takes it to flight.
  • Make and defend the hard allocation decisions. Determine what reasoning executes on orbit versus on the ground, and architect for degraded, latent, and communications denied operations.
  • Drive architectural coherence across disciplines. Coordinate across ground systems, perception, flight software, electrical hardware, GN&C, simulation, and navigation and trajectory functions, translating operational requirements into a single, consistent, buildable architecture.
  • Own the embedded AI/ML realization. Guide model architecture, training and data pipelines, compression and quantization, and hardware aware optimization, so that models meet real time and deterministic behavior requirements within actual SWaP-C constraints.
  • Build the assurance case for the full autonomy loop. Establish V&V practices for ML in high consequence systems, including uncertainty quantification, fault detection and isolation, runtime assurance, robustness testing, and simulation to hardware validation.
  • Set the technical direction and raise the team with you. You own the autonomy architecture baseline and technical roadmap. You will mentor and unblock engineers across the AI, FSW and Autonomy team, and represent Blue National Security's autonomy and AI/ML capability to government customers and partners.

Minimum Qualifications

  • B.S. in Computer Science, Electrical or Computer Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field, or equivalent hands on experience.
  • 10+ years developing software or systems for mission or safety critical applications, including architectural ownership of a distributed or multi segment system.
  • 3+ years developing and deploying ML systems into production, with demonstrated deployment on resource constrained or embedded targets such as edge GPUs, FPGAs, DSPs, or radiation tolerant processors.
  • Proficiency in Python and C/C++, and working expertise with modern ML frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, or ONNX Runtime) and edge optimization toolchains (quantization, pruning, TensorRT, TFLite, or equivalent).
  • Demonstrated experience leading architecture across multiple engineering disciplines, including flight software, hardware, and vehicle dynamics or controls.
  • Demonstrated ability to build technical consensus across disciplines, earning influence through depth and credibility, and to brief executives, government customers, and engineering peers with equal clarity.
  • Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Advanced degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or Aerospace Engineering.
  • GN&C, navigation, trajectory, or estimation background for flight vehicles, including experience bringing learning-based methods into classical control and estimation architectures.
  • Autonomous spacecraft operations experience: on orbit fault detection and isolation, autonomous mission sequencing, RPO, closed loop vehicle control, or autonomous operations in communications denied environments.
  • Ground segment or mission operations experience, including tasking, ground autonomy, or ground to space autonomy handoff.
  • Space grade or radiation tolerant compute (NVIDIA Orin, Xilinx Versal, rad hard SoCs); real time and safety critical environments (RTOS, bare metal); hardware in the loop and simulation to hardware workflows; or formal V&V methods for ML.
  • DoD, USSF, NRO, or IC program experience, and an active U.S. Secret or TS/SCI clearance.


Base Pay Range for:

CO applicants is $218,520.00 - $305,926.95

Other site ranges may differ


Culture Statement

Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.


Export Control Regulations

Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


Background Check

What you’ll be part of:

Circle is committed to visibility and stability in everything we do. As we grow as an organization, we're expanding into some of the world's strongest jurisdictions. Speed and efficiency are motivators for our success and our employees live by our company values: High Integrity, Future Forward, Multistakeholder, Mindful, and Driven by Excellence. What you’ll be responsible for

Circle is looking for a Lead Product Designer to shape high-quality customer experiences across our currency, treasury, and payments products. You will own end-to-end design for complex product areas, partnering closely with Product Management, Engineering, Research, and other cross-functional teams to identify customer needs, define opportunities, and deliver thoughtful, scalable solutions. You will apply strong product judgment and systems thinking to balance customer, business, and technical considerations, while influencing product direction, raising the quality of design execution, and contributing to a cohesive experience across Circle’s platform.

What you’ll work on

  • Own end-to-end product design for complex customer journeys, from problem definition and exploration through launch and iteration.

  • Develop a deep understanding of customer needs, behaviors, and workflows across payments, treasury, digital assets, and blockchain-enabled products.

  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Research, and other stakeholders to define, scope, and prioritize high-impact customer and business problems.

  • Use qualitative research, quantitative data, and product insights to shape design direction and influence cross-functional decisions.

  • Lead alignment on complex design problems, clearly communicating rationale, trade-offs, and recommendations to stakeholders.

  • Identify patterns and opportunities across product areas to create cohesive, scalable experiences and strengthen Circle’s design system.

  • Elevate design quality by contributing to team practices, providing thoughtful critique, and coaching other designers through complex work.

About Sanctions Screening Center of Excellence: The Center of Excellence for economic sanctions monitoring is part of Global Payment Operations (GPO). title: Data Scientist (Conversational AI)
location: Ho Chi Minh City, Ho Chi Minh, Vietnam
description:
Location: Ho Chi Minh City,Ho Chi Minh,Vietnam

Trusting Social is an AI Fintech company building credit profiles for underserved consumers across Vietnam, Indonesia, India, and the Philippines, combining alternative data with advanced AI to expand access to credit. Having profiled over 1 billion consumers, the company is now pushing toward 100 million credit lines delivered — grounded throughout in strict data privacy and consumer data rights.

How You’ll Make an Impact

We build the AI that talks to our customers, at the scale of a national consumer portfolio: real conversations, in production, every day. As a Data Scientist on the Data Science team you own the harder half of that. You decide what the agents should be optimized for, you design the experiment that grades a change, and you are the person who can say with evidence whether we got better.

The scope is deliberately broad: modeling, experimentation, unit economics, and the conversation with the business, in one seat. Decisions you make land on live traffic within the week, and you see the result in the numbers rather than in a slide. It suits someone strong technically who is not content to stop at the model, and who wants the judgment side of data science, not just the tooling.

What You’ll Do

Objective and Agent Logic

  • Own the objective the conversational stack is optimized against, and keep it tied to a business number rather than a proxy.
  • Own the dialogue and decisioning logic behind what the agent says and does, and be able to tell which layer a behavior came from.

Quality, Cost and Speed

  • Hold quality, cost per conversation and speed together, set the thresholds the team works to, and defend the trade-off to the business.
  • Own how agent quality is measured, and the monitoring that catches a regression before a customer does.

Evidence and Judgment

  • Design and read the experiments behind every change: size them before they run, separate the agent effect from mix and seasonality, and say plainly when a movement is not attributable.
  • Benchmark new AI models and methods on our own traffic before adopting them, and be willing to say a shiny thing is not worth the migration.
  • Turn results into decisions with senior management, and mentor junior members on method and rigor.

What We’re Looking For

Experience & Background

  • Postgraduate degree (Masters or PhD) in a quantitative field such as Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Economics, or equivalent experience preferred.
  • 4 to 6 years of professional experience applying statistical and machine learning solutions to business problems.
  • Strong hands-on experience in machine learning, statistics, and experimentation, including experiment design and causal measurement on observational data.
  • Strong Python and SQL, and comfort working directly on large datasets without waiting for a curated table.
  • Hands-on experience with LLM-based systems, prompt iteration, and the evaluation of generated output is strongly preferred.
  • Familiarity with bank-related products such as unsecured personal loans and credit cards is preferred.
  • Experience with big data processing is a plus.
  • Startup or tech background is a strong plus.

How You Work

  • You use AI tools as part of your method — precise prompts, critical reading of what comes back, and the instinct to check an output against evidence before you act on it.
  • You don't wait for a spec to test an idea. You form the hypothesis, run it, and bring the result to the table.
  • You move between modeling, product, and the business conversation without needing a handoff, and you can hold a room of non-technical stakeholders.
  • You treat a failed experiment as information and keep raising your own bar on method, without being told to

Skills & Competencies

  • Domain Expert — Teaches method and rigor to others; edge cases are covered and documented rather than carried in one person's head.
  • Product Architect — Prototypes working agentic systems, reads the metrics they produce, and iterates before anyone has to ask.
  • AI Engineer/Architect — Ships end-to-end ML and agent systems, owning the path from data pipeline to production behavior.
  • AI Operator — Keeps agents performing above quality threshold at target cost, catching drift before it reaches customers.
  • Strong English communication skills (spoken and written — professional fluency required).
  • High adaptability and comfort operating in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.

What We Offer

Join our vibrant team and enjoy:

  • Opportunity to work and learn from one of the best and brightest technology teams in Vietnam
  • Be part of a winning team with exponential growth regionally, experience recruiting world-class talents
  • Competitive compensation package, including 13th-month salary and performance bonuses
  • Comprehensive health care coverage for you and your dependents
  • Generous leave policies, including annual leave, sick leave, and flexible work hours
  • Convenient central district 1 office location, next to a future metro station
  • Onsite lunch with multiple options, including vegetarian
  • Grab for work allowance and fully equipped workstations
  • Fun and engaging team building activities, sponsored sports clubs, and happy hour every Thursday
  • Unlimited free coffee, tea, snacks, and fruit to keep you energized
  • An opportunity to make a social impact by helping to democratize credit access in emerging markets

At Trusting Social, we live by ownership, integrity, and agility in execution. We believe in doing what’s right, what’s best, and what’s innovative. If you’re smart, driven, and want to make a difference in the world with the most advanced and fascinating technology, come join our team. We offer the runway to truly make an impact.

description:
Lightmatter is leading the revolution in AI data center infrastructure, enabling the next giant leaps in human progress. The company invented the world’s first 3D-stacked photonics engine, Passage™, capable of connecting thousands to millions of processors at the speed of light in extreme-scale data centers for the most advanced AI and HPC workloads.

Lightmatter raised $400 million in its Series D round, reaching a valuation of $4.4 billion. We will continue to accelerate the development of data center photonics and grow every department at Lightmatter!

If you're passionate about tackling complex challenges, making an impact, and being an expert in your craft, join our team of brilliant scientists, engineers, and accomplished industry leaders.

Lightmatter is (re)inventing the future of computing with light!

We are hiring a Sr Technical Program Manager (TPM) to drive program execution across Lightmatter's Hardware Systems team. You will drive schedules, resource planning, priorities, and cross-functional alignment for all projects and activities within the team - spanning electrical, mechanical, and system engineering.. You will work closely with internal teams such as SI, PI, SW, supply chain, and with external partners, including contract manufacturers, PCB and sheet metal fabricators, assembly houses, and other suppliers, to keep programs on track from early design through production.

In this role, you will manage dependencies and trade-offs across concurrent workstreams, facilitate alignment across internal and external stakeholders, and maintain program visibility for engineering leadership. Your scope covers the full hardware development lifecycle, from design through production, including the engineering support programs, test infrastructure, and tooling that keep the broader team moving. You will also serve as the team's primary program interface to broader organizational programs, ensuring that schedule changes, material commitments, and engineering status are communicated accurately and on time to cross-functional program stakeholders.

This is a hands-on role that combines strong program management fundamentals with a working knowledge of hardware engineering. You will be equally at home in a design review, a supplier call, a resource planning discussion, and an executive status update. You will also need to thrive in a fast-moving environment where requirements evolve, priorities shift, and not every process is fully established, and bring the clarity and structure that turns that ambiguity into forward progress.

Responsibilities

  • Own program coordination across all HW Systems activities: maintain an integrated schedule across all concurrent projects and workstreams, surface priority conflicts, and drive resolution of resource contention with engineering leads.
  • Drive cross-functional alignment between HW Systems and other teams: setting agendas, facilitating meetings, capturing decisions, communicating delays and risks, and relentlessly following up on action items
  • Manage team-wide resource loading and capacity visibility, partnering with engineering leads to flag overallocation risks and drive trade-offs discussions across concurrent programs
  • Build and maintain integrated program schedules that reflect hardware development realities - bring-up milestones, NPI phases, EVT/DVT/PVT gates, and cross-team dependencies
  • Own program scope that lives outside formal project charters: tester boards, demos, lab fixtures, calibration equipment, and internal engineering tools that teams depend on but that would otherwise lack dedicated ownership
  • Coordinate material flow within the HW Systems team: track component orders, PCB fab runs, PCBA and mechanical assemblies, and engineering samples; partner with supply chain to ensure critical materials land on schedule
  • Track and coordinate cross-functional teams' HW deliverable dependencies including quantities and timelines, and ensure downstream teams are unblocked with accurate, up-to-date visibility into HW schedule and status
  • Serve as the primary hardware program interface with external contract manufacturers, PCB and sheet metal fabricators, and assembly houses: managing schedules, tracking deliverables, facilitating technical alignment, and driving closure on open issues in partnership with Supply chain.
  • Represent the HW Systems team in company-wide program reviews and cross-functional planning cadences; own the team's program interface to broader organizational stakeholders, communicating schedule changes, material needs, and engineering commitments proactively and clearly
  • Track HW Systems budgets for engineering activities, prototype builds, and tooling; coordinate with finance and operations to ensure spend is planned, visible, and aligned with program milestones
  • Adapt quickly to change: replan and realign when scope shifts, schedules move, or engineering realities force a pivot; maintain momentum and clarity even when the path forward is not fully defined
  • Establish and maintain lightweight program management processes: status reporting cadences, risk registers, dependency tracking, and decision logs

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related technical field.
  • 5+ years of program management experience in hardware engineering, with direct exposure to electrical and mechanical development cycles.
  • Proven track record managing concurrent engineering programs with shared resources and overlapping timelines.
  • Deep familiarity with hardware development processes and terminology across the full lifecycle—including PCBA and mechanical enclosures, PCB fabrication, system integration, bring-up, EVT/DVT/PVT, and production—enabling clear communication with engineers and vendors.
  • Proven experience coordinating with contract manufacturers (CMs) and ODMs to manage schedules, track deliverables, and resolve open issues.
  • Hands-on experience with material flow, component tracking, and BOM management.
  • Skilled facilitator who drives productive meetings, captures critical context, and ensures action items are owned and closed.
  • Strong written and verbal communicator, comfortable presenting program status and risk assessments to engineering leads and executives.
  • Expert in project management tools such as Microsoft Project, Jira, Smartsheet, or equivalent platforms.
  • Strong bias for action—consistently closes loops, follows up independently, and identifies potential slips before they impact project timelines.
  • Thrives in fast-paced, ambiguous environments; proactively creates structure and drives clarity without waiting for complete information.

Job Description:

GDIT has an immediate opening for an early-career Systems Engineer supporting the CITS contract for USCENTCOM. This position is based on-site in Tampa, Florida, with direct focus on enterprise lab infrastructure, integration, patching, and testing.

Position Overview

The Systems Engineer serves as a core technical contributor responsible for executing software and hardware testing, baseline integration, systematic vulnerability patching, and functional validation within the USCENTCOM enterprise laboratory. Working under the guidance of senior engineering staff, this role provides technical support across physical and virtual environments to ensure lab systems remain secure, properly baselined, and fully validated prior to operational or exercise deployment. The engineer will assemble hardware, deploy operating systems, execute structured test plans, apply security baselines, and assist in maintaining laboratory readiness in a fast-paced defense environment.

HOW A Junior Systems Engineer WILL MAKE AN IMPACT

Duties and Responsibilities

  • Perform physical installation, racking, stacking, cabling, and baseline configuration of servers, workstations, storage devices, and lab network appliances.

  • Execute standardized software and hardware test plans, procedures, and validation scripts to verify system functionality and interoperability.

  • Identify, document, and track hardware defects, software bugs, and performance bottlenecks, reporting findings to senior engineering leads.

  • Apply scheduled security patches, operating system updates, application hotfixes, and hardware firmware upgrades across Windows and Linux environments.

  • Validate post-patching system stability, performance, and application dependencies to ensure zero degradation of lab baselines.

  • Support virtualization environments, including creating, configuring, and maintaining virtual machines in VMware vSphere/ESXi and Hyper-V.

  • Assist in the implementation of DISA Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs) and support vulnerability remediation efforts.

  • Maintain laboratory configuration documentation, hardware/software asset inventories, test execution records, and Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs).

  • Provide Tier I/II troubleshooting support for hardware faults, operating system anomalies, and network connectivity issues within the test environment.

WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO SUCCEED:

Education, Clearance & Certifications

Security Clearance: Active SECRET clearance required with the ability to upgrade to TS/SCI.

Certifications: Current DoD 8140 / DoD 8570 IAT Level II baseline certification (e.g., CompTIA Security+ CE, CCNA-Security, CySA+, or equivalent).

Required qualifications: Foundational technical knowledge of Windows Server (2019/2022), Windows 10/11, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and virtualization environments using VMware ESXi or vCenter.

Education: Bachelor of Science or Bachelor of Arts in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent operational experience/military training).

Experience: 3+ years of related experience in systems engineering, hardware staging, systems administration, or laboratory test environments.

Required and Desired Qualifications

Required qualifications include foundational technical knowledge of Windows Server (2019/2022), Windows 10/11, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and virtualization environments using VMware ESXi or vCenter. Candidates must have practical experience with physical server racking, stacking, cabling, and hardware component replacement, alongside a clear understanding of patch management lifecycles and basic networking concepts including TCP/IP, VLANs, and routing.

Desired qualifications include hands-on exposure to vulnerability scanning tools such as ACAS (Tenable Nessus) and automated configuration management frameworks. Experience with basic automation and scripting using PowerShell or Bash, along with prior experience operating within DoD test labs, military command environments, or USCENTCOM networks, is highly advantageous.

Travel and Shift Requirements

Position may require up to 10% travel in support of USCENTCOM mission requirements. Work hours and shift schedules are determined by lab operational requirements and support needs.
